Thus the glorious surah begins, making clear that God's decree and judgment regarding the victory of the Messenger and the believers is beyond doubt and inevitable, and that the defeat of the people of disbelief is coming, with no escape from it if they persist in disbelief. The Messenger (ﷺ) had already warned them with what was revealed to him of the verses of the Book: in the previous surah he warned them of some worldly punishment, such as the victory of faith over disbelief, and earlier still he warned them of some punishment in the Hereafter, as the Truthful One, glorified be He, said: ﴿So whether We show you part of what We promise them, or We take you (in death), to Us they will return﴾ (Surah Ghafir, 77).

And likewise His saying, the Truth:

﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs﴾ (Surah al-Qamar, 45).

Thus God, glorified be He, promised His Messenger (ﷺ) that He would defeat the camp of disbelief and grant victory to the camp of faith; whether he would see that with his own eyes, or if the Truth took his life, he would see it in the Hereafter. Concerning the state of the Messenger (ﷺ), He, glorified be He, said: ﴿We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 95).

And the Truth, glorified be He, warned the people of polytheism that they would be in Hell on the Last Day. Here He, glorified be He, says:

﴿The command of God has come⁠—﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 1). This is a clarification at one stage of the stages of the information about what they are being warned of, as He said once: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been split﴾ (Surah al-Qamar, 1), meaning: the Hour of Resurrection has drawn near, after which will come the reckoning of the Hereafter and punishment for whoever disbelieved, and Paradise for whoever believed and did righteous deeds. The approach of the Hour is not frightening in itself, but frightening because of the reckoning and retribution it contains. It was said: when the people of disbelief heard the words of the Truth, glorified be He, ﴿The Hour has drawn near⁠—﴾ (Surah al-Qamar, 1), they said: "Let us wait a little; perhaps what Muhammad conveys is true." After they had waited some time, and the Hour did not come as the noble Messenger (ﷺ) had announced, they said: "We waited and the Hour did not come." Then the word of the Truth, glorified be He, was revealed:

﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near for them⁠—﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 1).

This speaks of the matter that will occur immediately upon the establishment of the Hour. So they made a truce and waited a little, then said: "Where, then, is the reckoning?" So the words of the Exalted were revealed: ﴿The command of God has come⁠—﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 1).

When everyone heard that, they were alarmed, including the Muslims; and the reassurance came in His saying afterward:

﴿So do not seek to hasten it⁠—﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 1). That is: the matter that Muhammad (ﷺ) announces, its appointed time is known only to God, glorified be He; and the Muslims were reassured. Every event, as we know, requires two frames: a frame of time and a frame of place. Verbs that indicate these frames are either a past verb, whose frame was before we speak, or a present verb, meaning it has occurred, unless it is preceded by "sa-" or "sawfa." That is: the verb will occur in the near future if it is preceded by "sa-," or in the undetermined and distant future if it is preceded by "sawfa." Thus verbs are past, present, and future.

The word "atā" (has come) indicates that the One who informs you, namely God, glorified be He, is informing you of something that happened before the speech, while He tells of it. Humans may speak of things that have occurred and inform one another of them. But the speaker here is the Truth, glorified be He; and when He speaks through the Qur'an, His knowledge is never diminished. His knowledge is eternal, and He is able to bring the future in accordance with what He said. He had determined the timing and place of everything before He created it; He is Creator before He created anything, for creation is an essential attribute of His. He is transcendent in all things. Therefore He said: ﴿The command of God has come, so do not seek to hasten it—glorified be He⁠…﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 1). That is: He is the All-Knowing of the time of the occurrence of every event. His glorification was established in His essence before creation existed, for He is the One who said:

﴿They glorify Him night and day without respite﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 20). Then He created the heavens, the earth, and other things. That is: He was glorified before the creation of the heavens and the earth, and He is the One who said, glorified be He:

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God⁠…﴾ (Surah al-Hashr, 1).

But has glorification ended? No; glorification is continuous forever. He is the One who said: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God⁠…﴾ (Surah al-Jumu'ah, 1).

So: His "subhaniyyah" (being glorified) was established in His essence; then He found the angels glorifying Him night and day without respite; then He created the heavens and the earth, and whatever is in them and between them glorified Him. His creatures also glorify Him, so O you who have believed in God as God, glorify Him as the whole universe glorifies Him. Someone may ask: what is the connection between "glorified be He, exalted above what they associate" and the verse? We know that they associated with God gods who do not impose on them any devotional obligation and did not send down a method; rather, they make lawful for them everything forbidden, and forbid them some of what is lawful, thereby abandoning the following of what the Messengers brought, conveying from God an obligation that carries the burden of faith. These are the ones who will meet God, and the angels will ask them: "Where are the partners you worshipped besides God?" And no one will repel from them the terror of the torment they face.

Thus we have come to know that the glorification of God, glorified and exalted be He, in His essence, attributes, and acts, is a matter established for Him before anything existed, a matter established for Him after the angels, and established for Him after the existence of the heavens and the earth. It is a matter God requested of the servant who has choice to do; the servants divided into two groups: a group that believed and glorified Him, and a group that did not glorify Him, so the Truth, glorified be He, exalted above them because they are polytheists.

And when we recite His words "yunzilu" (He sends down), the word suggests that there is a height from which something can be sent down to a lower place. The example I would like to give here to clarify this matter is the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you...﴾ (Surat al-An'am). That is: come and listen from me to the commandment that has been sent down to you from One who is higher than you. Do not remain in the lowland of the earth and its legislations, but rise up and take the matter from One who has no desire in your affairs, the Supreme Truth. As for those who are sent down, they are the angels. We know that the angels are an unseen creation in which we believe, because Allah, glorified is He, has informed us of their existence. Everything that is absent from the mind, whose proof is hearing, must be received from one whose truthfulness you trust. The Prophet (ﷺ) conveyed to us what the Qur'an came with, and informed us of the existence of the angels and that the Truth, glorified is He, created them. Although we do not see them, we affirm what came in the message from the Truth, from the truthful and veracious one, Muhammad (ﷺ). When the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants...﴾ (Surat al-Nahl). We know that nothing can descend from the high to the low except through intermediaries that are close to Him. The Truth, glorified is He, has chosen one of the angels to convey revelation from Allah to His messengers. And the angels, as the Truth, glorified is He, has informed us: ﴿Honored servants. They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command﴾ (Surat al-Anbiya').

He says in another verse: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ (Surat al-Tahrim).

They are made of light, no misfortunes touch them, and they have no desire, so they do not marry or beget offspring. They are closer to purity, and they are the ones who are able to receive from the Highest and convey to the lowest. Therefore, we find the Truth, glorified is He, saying about the Qur'an: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ (Surat al-Shu'ara').

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿He sends down the angels...﴾ (Surat al-Nahl). The comprehensive verse that explains this is the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾ (Surat al-Hajj). That is: He, glorified is He, chooses angels capable of receiving from Him, to give to those chosen from among mankind, so that these chosen ones convey from Allah to the rest of mankind. This is because the lofty heights do not allow the lower being the capacity to bear what the high matters are sent down with directly from the Truth, glorified is He. I have previously compared this to the transformer that we use in electricity, which transmits the high energy to the lower one for the lamps. We all know what happened to the Messenger (ﷺ) when he received revelation through Gabriel, peace be upon him: "He pressed me until I reached the limit of my exertion," and his pure forehead sweated, and he returned to his house saying, "Wrap me up, wrap me up" and "Cover me, cover me."

This is because a high energy descended upon a human energy, even though the energy of the Messenger of Allah is a chosen energy. Then the Messenger grew accustomed to revelation, and such burdens became lighter for him, and there was sent down to him the saying of the Truth:

﴿Did We not expand for you your breast? And We relieved you of your burden, which had weighed down your back, and We raised high your mention. So indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease.﴾ (Surat al-Sharh).

Then revelation paused for a period of time, to the extent that the Prophet (ﷺ) longed for it. Why did he long for revelation when he is the one who said, "Cover me, cover me"? The pause of revelation was because Muhammad (ﷺ) was becoming accustomed to the hardships of the descent of the angel, so the hardships of the encounter would depart and the sweetness of what he was conveyed would remain. Some of the foolish said: "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him." Then the Almighty sent down His saying: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you. And the Hereafter is better for you than the first. And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ (Surat al-Duha).

The word "al-Ruh" (the Spirit) occurs in the Qur'an with several meanings. Sometimes it is the spirit by which there is life in matter, so that feeling and movement occur through it: ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My Spirit, fall down to him in prostration﴾ (Surat al-Hijr).

This breathing into matter happens to both the believer and the disbeliever. There is another spirit that gives a higher life than temporal life: ﴿And indeed, the Home of the Hereafter — that is the [true] life, if they only knew﴾ (Surat al-'Ankabut).

Therefore: the angels descend with the message from Allah, which contains a life more elevated than the life in which we live and move upon the earth. Thus there are two spirits, not one spirit: a spirit for feeling and movement, and a spirit that gives the values that lead us to another life more elevated than the life we live, a life without end. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, calls the Qur'an a spirit, saying: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you an inspiration of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor [what] faith [was]...﴾ (Surat al-Shura).

The Truth, glorified is He, also calls the angel who descends with the Qur'an a spirit, saying: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, upon your heart, that you may be of the warners﴾ (Surat al-Shu'ara').

The Truth, glorified is He, explains that the Qur'an is a spirit that gives us a higher life, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when He calls you to that which gives you life...﴾ (Surat al-Anfal). That is: He brings you into the eternal life in which there is no death and no fear of losing the blessing or of the blessing departing from you. Here He informs us that the Qur'an descends with the angels: ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command...﴾ (Surat al-Nahl). That is: a descent issued by His command, glorified is He. The Truth, glorified is He, says in another place: ﴿For him are successive [angels] before and behind him, who protect him by the command of Allah...﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd). The superficial ones do not pay attention that the meaning of "by the command of Allah" (min amri Allah) here means that they protect him by a command from Allah. The "command" in the verse we are reflecting upon is what came in its first verse: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it...﴾ (Surat al-Nahl). This command is the result of what Allah wills of life for people upon the earth. We know that the Truth, glorified is He, has multiple commands, which are gathered in bringing what does not exist into existence. He, glorified is He, is the One who says:

﴿Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is﴾ (Surat al-Nahl).

If He wills a particular matter, He says to it: "Be," and it is. If He wills a method, He sends it down. If He wills a reckoning, a punishment, and an Hour, He is the One who says: "The command of Allah has come." Thus we understand that the meaning of "the command of Allah" is "Be, and it is," that is, bringing the nonexistent into the realm of existence, whether it is a particular nonexistent, or a total nonexistent, or an eternally nonexistent. All of that is called a command, and at the moment Allah commands, we are sure that what is commanded by Allah emerges. Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿When the sky has split open, and has responded to its Lord and was obligated﴾ (Surat al-Inshiqaq). That is: it did not merely hear the command; it executed it immediately upon its issuance, without the slightest particle of delay. The command of Allah is executed immediately upon its issuance from the Truth, glorified is He. As for the command of human beings, it is liable to be obeyed and liable to be disobeyed. He, glorified is He, sends down the angels with the Spirit upon whom He wills, so that they may warn; and the Truth, glorified is He, did not bring good tidings here, because the address is directed to the disbelievers in His saying: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it...﴾ (Surat al-Nahl).

And He declared His essence free of imperfection, saying: ﴿Exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾ (Surat al-Nahl).

Or: the Truth warns His Messenger: if you enter upon them, explain to them what is ambiguous to them, which they do not know. They do not know how selection occurs, and He is the Truth who knows best whom He chooses. His will of selection, choosing, and electing is accomplished only according to the attributes of the Truth, glorified is He. He says: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ (Surat al-An'am).

And know that the disbelievers said: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from one of the two cities?﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf). And the Truth, glorified is He, responded to them, saying: ﴿Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf).

If the Truth, glorified is He, has apportioned among creation their provisions in their material livelihood, and if He has raised some of them above others in ranks, and He is the One who makes the raised lowered and the lowered raised, then how do these people come to interfere in the matters of value related to the spirit and the method, attempting to make alterations upon Allah, saying, "We want so-and-so and we do not want so-and-so"? Or: the Truth clarifies to His Messenger: after you have explained to these people the matter of revelation, you must convey to them the word of Allah: ﴿There is no deity except Me, so fear Me﴾ (Surat al-Nahl).

Since there is no other deity, the Messenger must give them counsel, by sparing themselves the bewilderment of searching for a god, and he clarifies to them that there is no deity except Him, and that they must fear Him. In this there is tenderness from the Truth toward creation, the Truth who prevented the creatures that were astonished and rejected some people's disbelief in Allah, and sought to take revenge upon man, and He said to them: "If you had created them, you would have shown them mercy. Leave Me and My creation; if they repent to Me, then I am their beloved; and if they do not repent, then I am their physician." And the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿That warn that there is no deity except Me, so fear Me﴾ (Surat al-Nahl) is the summary of the creeds of heaven for the earth, and the summary of the acts of worship that Allah asked of His creation to organize for them the movement of life in harmony, not in conflict. So it is as if: ﴿That warn that there is no deity except Me, so fear Me﴾ is an explanation of what Allah sent down to the angels of the Spirit, which we said before is the second spirit that revelation brings, carrying the method of Allah to guarantee for the adherent a life whose bliss does not cease and whose enjoyer does not perish; and it is other than the first spirit which, when the Truth breathes it into man, life stirs in him in movement and feeling, but toward annihilation. It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, in His mercy toward His creation, sent down for them the method that guides them to the enduring life instead of remaining captives of the transient life alone. And from His mercy also is that He warned them of the evil destiny awaiting whoever disbelieves in Him; and such a warning comes only from one who loves; so He, glorified is He, loves His creation, loves that they be sincere and believing toward Him, and loves for them to enjoy in a Hereafter with no causes in it, because they will live in it by the word "Be" from the Causer.

So when He says to them: "Indeed, there is no deity except Me..." (al-Nahl 2), He clarifies that there is no god other than Him, so do not associate anything with Me, do not deny the messengers, and you must apply My method that organizes your lives, for which I will reward you in the Hereafter. Beware of being deceived by the fact that I created causes subjected to serve you; for I am able to seize these causes. I wanted life to be a trial and a test, and in the Hereafter there is no authority for causes at all: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer﴾ (Surat Ghafir).

The apparent matter is that dominion belongs to Allah in the Hereafter, and the reality is that dominion belongs to Allah always, in this world and in the Hereafter; but He willed to make the created causes, by His will, respond to the human being. So beware of thinking that you have become capable; for in this life you possess things, and a king or a ruler like you possesses you. The sunnah of the universe is that there exists a system that governs everyone. But in the Hereafter the matter is different; there is no kingship for anyone except Allah. Indeed, even the limbs themselves do not move by the will of their owners, but by the will of the Truth; those limbs that used to submit to your will in this world, you will have no authority over them in the Hereafter; rather, they will be witnesses against you.

If Allah has given you the ability to move your limbs in this world, then if you direct them toward what Allah commands, you are one of His servants; and if you do not direct them toward what Allah requires, you are one of His slaves. Then He, glorified is He, presents to you the rationale that reinforces His command to worship Him alone, and that there is no god other than Him; for He did not ask us to worship Him except after He had created for us the heavens and the earth, and the whole universe prepared to receive the human being with truth, that is, with what is established, and with the law that is not in the choice of anyone other than Him, glorified is He.

Meaning: He, glory be to Him, is exalted above what they associate with Him of deities. None assisted Him in creating the universe and arranging it; so how do you make other gods along with Him? Glory be to Him, who is exalted above having any other deity with Him. He created for us before He created us: He created the heavens and the earth and decreed the sustenance. If you look at your own creation, you would find that the great world has been folded up within you; and He is the One who said: ﴿And in yourselves. Will you not then see?﴾ (Surah adh-Dhariyat, 51:21). And from what were you created?

The najs (nutfah) from which he was created, which is the sperm cell that unites with the ovum found in the woman's womb, producing the clot ('alaqah). And He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Does man think he will be left neglected? Was he not a drop of semen emitted? Then he became a clinging clot, and He created [him] and proportioned [him]. And He made of him two mates, the male and the female.﴾ (Surah al-Qiyamah)

Indeed, a single emission from a man may contain offspring sufficient to create millions; and the naked eye cannot see a single sperm cell because of its extreme minuteness. This extreme minuteness can only be seen through magnifying microscopes, and hidden within this sperm cell are all the characteristics that combine with the characteristics hidden in the woman's ovum to form a human being. May God have mercy on al-'Aqqad, who spoke truly when he said: "If half of a sewing thimble were filled with sperm cells, there would be produced from it offspring equal in number to all of mankind."

God, glorified is He, willed that only the strong sperm cell should penetrate the ovum, to confirm for us that there is no survival except for the most fit. If the sperm cell carries the hereditary traits for the birth of a female, a female is born; and if it carries the hereditary traits for the birth of a male, a male is born. You see the like of this in plants: the first grain of wheat was like Adam as the first human, in the manner we know; and in that first grain God brought into existence the essence of all wheat grains thereafter, until the Hour arises. Such is the greatness of God, glorified is He, in creation. God, glorified is He, has explained to us in more than one place in the noble Qur'an the stages of human creation; He says:

﴿from a despised fluid﴾ (Surah al-Sajdah)

He is from a drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, formed and unformed. The sperm cell called "nutfah" is what carries the characteristics of femaleness or maleness, as modern science has established, and the woman has no role in this determination. It seems that this is an indication of the woman's task as a dwelling, because the ovum receives the sperm cell and embraces it, so that development is completed until it becomes a human being:

﴿So blessed is God, the best of creators﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun)

And He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Does man think he will be left neglected? Was he not a drop of semen emitted? Then he became a clot...﴾ (Surah al-Qiyamah)

The clot ('alaqah) took its name from its function, since it clings to the wall of the womb, as contemporary science has established. He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Then We made the clot into a lump of flesh...﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun)

The mudghah (lump) is the thing that is chewed; then He, glorified is He, describes the lump as:

﴿formed and unformed...﴾ (Surah al-Hajj)

One may ask: we understand that in the formed lump there is that which can become an eye or an arm; but what about the unformed? We say: it is a reserve stock for the maintenance of the body. For when you, O created being, build a house, you buy some extra items, such as sanitary fittings for example, in anticipation of events that may occur in which you need spare parts; so what of the Truth who created man? God has made that unformed lump a reserve for maintenance, or renewal for whatever circumstances may befall a person; it remains as a surplus in the body, as if it were a storehouse of spare parts.

An example is the wounds that afflict a person, which he then leaves for the body itself to treat; we find them healing without leaving a scar or mark, because they have been treated by the internal pharmacy that God, glorified is He, placed within the body itself. The surprise is that this human, created by God:

﴿then he is an open adversary﴾ (Surah al-Nahl)

rebels against his Creator, and some of the creation even deny that there is a god, forgetting that by the power of God within them they dispute. The adversary (khasim) is one who argues and denies realities; when something unseen is mentioned, he tries to refute its reasonableness. He, glorified is He, says in Surah Ya-Sin:

﴿Does man not see that We created him from a drop, and then he is an open adversary?﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin)

It may be acceptable for you to be an adversary to your peers; but it is not acceptable for you to be an adversary to the One who created you, formed you, and proportioned you, and in whatever form He willed, assembled you.

The warmth (al-difʾ) is heat for the one who feels cold, just as we give the one overheated coolness, and this is what air-conditioning does in modern homes. Here we find that the Exalted One has spoken of warmth and not spoken of cold, because the counterpart is known. In another verse He says: ﴿And He made for you garments that protect you from the heat...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl 16:81).

This is what happens when we walk in the hot sun: we place an umbrella over our heads to shield us from the heat of the blazing, intense sun. And in winter we wear a qalansuwa (a close-fitting cap), that is, we wrap something around our heads. Thus we know that clothing does the thing and its opposite, on condition that a person chooses the clothing suited to the climate. In the livestock (al-anʿam) there are many benefits: we drink their milk, and we make cheese and clarified butter from it; we card the wool to spin and weave woolen garments from it, they carry loads, we benefit from their offspring, and likewise we eat their meat. We know that the livestock has been detailed in another place, when the Exalted One said: ﴿Eight pairs...﴾ (Surah al-Anʿam 6:143).

These are the sheep, the goats, the camels and the cattle. We know that warmth comes from wool, fleece (al-wabar) and hair, and whoever observes goat hair finds each hair on its own; but the fleece (wabar) that we card from the camel is matted (mulabbad), and this is evidence of the precision of its twisting. As for wool, each strand of it is a cylindrical tube whose core is hollow.

Here, we find that the Almighty has given us luxury alongside necessities. Warmth, benefits and food are necessities of life, whereas beauty is among the luxuries of life. Beauty is what the eye sees, so joy is realized within the soul. Warmth, benefits and food are matters specific to the one who owns the livestock; beauty, however, is a common good shared by people. When you see a beautiful horse, or a cow radiant with health, you see the blessing of God, which He created to delight the one who looks upon it. We notice this beauty in the moments when livestock go out to pasture and in the moments when they return.

In the countryside we say "sarahat al-bahaim" (the beasts went out to graze), meaning they came out of the pens to graze and eat. We notice that the Almighty mentioned the return (ruwah), that is, their coming back to the pens, before the going out (sarah); because when the beasts return to their pens after grazing, their bellies are full and their udders are swollen and brimming with milk, so whoever sees them is delighted even before he drinks of their milk. Whoever goes out with his beasts in the morning from his house, and leads them from their enclosures to the field, finds beauty together with dignity and strength, with sounds that give the owner a sense of prestige; and one who does not own them can still behold the beauty of those livestock.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 7:

We know that a person in his life is between two states: either he is ẓāʿin (i.e., travelling, on the move), or he is muqīm (resident, settled). In the case of the resident, livestock (al-anʿām) provides him with warmth, food and clothing. The person of average means usually suffices with settling in his place of residence, and so does the poor man. As for the wealthy and capable person, you find him one day in Cairo, another day in Alexandria or Tanta, and he may travel abroad, and all of that is easy in the time of modern transport. In former times, means of transport were arduous, and no one could travel except him who had sound camels or strong horses; as for him who owned only a lean donkey, he would think only of short distances. For this reason, when the Qur'an speaks of the people of Sheba, it says:

﴿So they said, "Our Lord, make the distances between our journeys farther," and they wronged themselves...﴾ (Surah Saba', 19).

They said this out of pride in what they possessed of horses and means of travel, of sound and strong mounts, which made for comfortable travel, a travel that reveals honour, strength and wealth. And His saying, the Truth (al-Ḥaqq):

﴿And it carries your loads...﴾ (Surah al-Naḥl, 7)

means: placing what is heavy upon what is heavy. Therefore we do not find a person carrying his mount; rather we find one who carries his loads on the animal, to lighten for himself the burden of weights he cannot bear. We know that weight follows density, just as volume follows area. When you look at a kilogram of cotton, you find the volume of a kilogram of cotton greater than the volume of iron, because the density of iron is compressed within it, whereas the fluffy fibres of cotton are what make it require a larger space. The Truth, glory be to Him, continues His saying in the noble verse:

﴿And it carries your loads to a land you could not have reached except with great hardship...﴾ (Surah al-Naḥl, 7).

Whoever probes the styles of the Qur'an among the orientalists may say: "The end of the verse does not agree with its beginning." We say to the likes of this speaker: you have not perceived the favour with which God bestows upon His creatures. They could not have reached this land with their burdens except with hardship; so how much more the weight of hardship when they have with them loads of goods and belongings? It is a great blessing that they find what they can load their burdens and themselves upon, to reach where they wish to go. The word (bishaqq) in al-Naḥl derives from shaqq, which is the cleft between two things, meaning the separation of two connected things; and He, glory be to Him, is the One who says:

﴿So proclaim what you are commanded...﴾ (Surah al-Ḥijr, 94).

There is also shaqq, meaning exertion, and shuqqah (distance). And a person, as we know, is in three states: either he is asleep, so he does not need a great deal of energy to sustain his life; and also when he is awake, his bodily systems do not need great energy, but only moderate energy to function; but if he is carrying heavy things, a person needs greater energy for his systems to function. Likewise, the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Had it been a near gain and a moderate journey, they would have followed you; but the distance seemed long to them...﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah, 42).

The meaning here of shuqqah is the distance which is difficult to traverse. The Truth, glory be to Him, concludes the noble verse by saying:

﴿Indeed your Lord is Most Kind, Most Merciful.﴾ (Surah al-Naḥl, 7).

The two attributes here are ra'fah (tender compassion) and raḥmah (mercy), and each of them is suitable to what came in the verse. The Lord (al-Rabb) is the One who undertakes nurture and provision. Every journey has an aim: a journey is either for investment (istithmār), or for reflection (i'tibār), or for both together. If it is a journey of investment, your mount must be strong to bear what you carry of loads, and to carry upon it what you will return with of goods. If the journey is for reflection, you, by this travel, remove the pain of not knowing and the longing to reach the place you intended.

Thus you find ra'fah suitable for fulfilling benefit, achieving need and removing pain. And the word raḥīm is suitable for preventing pain by achieving arrival at the goal. Some scholars paused at the aim of the journey, such as that you are travelling for trade, or that you are travelling for reflection. But this is travel by choice; there is also compulsory travel, such as the necessary journey to Hajj once, or to ʿUmrah. The Truth, glory be to Him, removes the pain of the heavy load, and thereby His ra'fah is realised; and He is Raḥīm because He has fulfilled for you the wish of travel.

Having mentioned the livestock from which we take food, the Almighty now mentions in this verse the animals we use for transport or for adornment, and which we do not eat the flesh of: horses, mules and donkeys. He reminds us that they are for riding, for benefit, and for adornment, because people adorn themselves with what they ride, just as the people of our age take pride in adorning themselves with luxurious cars. The structure of the verse indicates the differences in rank among people: every rank of people has what suits it to ride. Horses are for the lords, the knights and the wealthy; those of lesser means ride mules; and whoever does not have enough to buy a horse or a mule may buy himself a donkey.

One person may own three mounts, another may own two, a third may own only one mount, and there are those who do not have enough money to rent even a mount of any kind. The Almighty willed to distribute the provision of each of His servants among people, few or abundant. Otherwise, if people were equal in provision, who would perform the tasks that we, mistakenly, call menial tasks: who would sweep the streets, who would carry bricks for construction, and who would stand in grease amid car repair workshops?

As we see, all those tasks are necessary. Were it not for people's desire for provision, such tasks would not have been undertaken or found pleasing in the eyes of those who perform them, for they protect them from the evil of asking. Were it not that whoever works in those tasks has a stomach that wants to be filled with food, and children who want to eat, he would not have undertaken the hardships of those tasks. If you look at the poorest person in the world, you will find in his life a period in which he achieved some of his dreams. We may find a person who toils for ten years and then rests the rest of his life; and we find one who toils for twenty years and thus relieves himself and his children after him; and there is one who toils for thirty years and so relieves his children and grandchildren after him. What matters is the value of what he masters, and that he be content with the decree of God concerning him, for God gives to whoever has accepted His decree concerning him.

If you look at those whom God has blessed with wealth and affluence, you will find that at the beginning of their lives they toiled, exerted themselves, and were content with the decree of God concerning them, and did not harbor resentment toward anyone; you will find that He guides them to tranquility and peace of mind. The Almighty willed to diversify the levels of human life so that no one would disdain to serve another as long as he needs his services. The expressive text in the verse we are contemplating is: horses, mules and donkeys; and the Almighty has placed the mules in the middle, because they are not a single species but come from two different species. At the end of the verse, the Almighty alerts us that this is not the final destination; rather there is more, so He said:

﴿And He creates what you do not know.﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 16:8)

The Almighty made the Buraq a servant of our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and made the flying carpet a servant of Prophet Sulayman (peace be upon him). If such miracles occurred for prophets, He has guided mankind to invent, from means of transportation, many carriages drawn by steeds, and then automobiles, trains and airplanes. Science continues to develop those means, and nevertheless there are those who keep horses, raise them, train them, and race them for the beauty of their appearance. If those means of transport carried our burdens, and those inventions are what God has guided us to, then what of transport in the Hereafter? There must be means suited, in their luxury, to the enjoyments of the Hereafter that do not exist in this world.

The way (al-sabil) is the road, and the aim (al-qasd) is the goal. It is a verbal noun, and from it they say "a direct road" (tariq qasid), meaning a road with no winding or detours. The Almighty wants us to reach the goal with the least effort.

In our colloquial language we ask the traffic policeman, "Is this road moving (masha)?" Although the road does not move, it is you who travel along it, but you mean that the road should lead to the goal. When the means fail you, you say "leave it to God" (khalliha 'ala Allah), meaning that you refer what your means cannot achieve to the Highest Cause. In this way the believer wants to reach his intended aim, which is the worship of God, in order to reach the ultimate goal, which is Paradise, as a reward for faith and good deeds in this world.

When you examine the course of the Nile, you find in it turns and meanders, because the water itself carved its path. But when you look at the al-Tawfiqi winds, for example, you find them straight, because humans are the ones who dug (or directed) them toward a specific destination. When the aim of the way is God, then God has no desire, no partner, no offspring, and He favours no one, and all creation is equal in relation to Him. Therefore, when He lays down a path, He lays it straight, with no crookedness in it. He, the Almighty, says: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ (Surah al-Fatihah, 6), meaning the path that has no twisting for any purpose, but whose purpose is the goal by the easiest way.

The word of the Almighty here: ﴿And upon God is the direction of the way﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 9) brings us back in memory to what Satan said in his dialogue with God, when he said: ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them﴾ (Surah Sad, 82–83).

He, the Almighty, also said: ﴿Then this is a straight path upon Me﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 41).

And the Almighty also says: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance﴾ (Surah al-Layl, 12), meaning that when He created man, He clarified for him the path of guidance. Likewise He says: ﴿And We have shown him the two ways﴾ (Surah al-Balad, 10), meaning that the Almighty made clear to man the paths of truth from falsehood. Thus His word here: ﴿And upon God is the direction of the way﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 9) indicates that the path laid out has its goal determined by God, and the road to that goal is balanced by the Truth, which has no desire, and all creatures are equal before Him. So, the thinkers should not exhaust themselves trying to set up a legislation of their own for the movement of life, because the One who originated life has already set down its law for preserving it. Nothing shows the inability of thinkers to establish laws regulating human life more clearly than that they change their laws every period, whereas the law of God is eternal and everlasting, and there is no correction to it. Therefore it is more comfortable for humans to follow the methodology of God, which the Almighty has stated as a judgment that they must apply, while what He has left for us to exert effort in, we do exert effort in.

His word, the Truth: ﴿And upon God is the direction of the way﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 9) means that He is the One who made the way of faith direct toward the goal He set, since among the ways there is that which is deviating. Therefore He said: ﴿and among them is the deviating﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 9). To prevent deviation, He made the way of faith direct. He says: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun, 71). Whereas the just, straight way is the one that God has taken upon Himself, and it is the way of faith. Among ways there is that which is deviating, meaning that it lengthens the distance for you, or exposes you to dangers, or contains curves that mislead a person so that he does not proceed on the straight road. We know that a way connects two points ("from" and "to"), and every point you reach also has ("from" and "to"). God willed not to compel man to a single way, but wanted him to choose. This is because subjugation was willed by God for other than man, for the service of man. As for man, the capacity of choice was created for him, so that He might know who comes to Him obediently and who disobeys His commands. All humans will be gathered for reckoning, and whoever chooses the path of obedience comes to God as a lover, and establishes for Him the state of being beloved, which is the purpose of the Truth in creating choice. But if He had willed to establish for Himself the absolute power of compulsion, He would have created humans compelled to obedience, as He subjected the other creatures. The Almighty desires hearts, not mere moulds. Therefore He says at the end of the verse: ﴿And if He willed, He would have guided you all﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 9). All kinds of existence, as we know, prostrate to God: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it exalts [God] with His praise, but you do not understand their exaltation﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 44). In another verse He says: ﴿Have you not seen that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight? Each has known its prayer and its exaltation﴾ (Surah al-Nur, 41).

So, if the Almighty had willed, He would have guided the two weighty ones, that is, mankind and the jinn, just as He guided all the other creatures. But He desires hearts, not mere moulds.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 10:

The words of His, ﴿He it is who sends down water from the sky...﴾ (Surah an-Nahl) appear to be a simple statement; but if we consider the factories that distil water and purify it of impurities, we will know the amount of effort expended for clear water to descend from the rain. The sky, as we know, is everything that is above us, and we see the clouds that come about as a result of the sun evaporating water from the oceans and seas, so that vapour rises, then condenses to become rain thereafter; and the rain descends upon the earth.

We know that the globe of the earth is composed of oceans and seas covering three-quarters of its surface, while the land area amounts to a quarter of the globe. It is as though He made three-quarters of the surface of the globe to serve one-quarter of the globe. And it is remarkable that rain falls in places from which it may not benefit, such as the highlands of Abyssinia (al-Habasha), upon which the rains fall and carry from those highlands the sediment of silt, so that it forms the Nile River for us to benefit from it. And we find the Truth, glorified is He, saying:

﴿Do you not see that Allah drives the clouds, then joins them together, then makes them into a heap, so that you see the rain coming out from their midst; and He sends down from the sky mountains [of clouds] wherein is hail, and He strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills...﴾ (Surah an-Nur, 43)

And here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿It is He who sent down water from the sky; from it you have drink, and from it [grows] vegetation in which you pasture [your livestock]﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 10). Had it not been for the process of evaporation and the re-condensation of vapour after it becomes cloud, man would not have been able to drink the salt water found in the seas. And it is among the wisdom of the Truth, glorified is He, that He made the waters of the seas and oceans salty; for salt preserves water from corruption. After the sun evaporates the water to become cloud, and the rain falls, man drinks this water, which feeds the rivers and wells, and likewise the water makes the crops grow, from which we eat.

The word (shajar) denotes vegetation that intertwines with itself, and from it comes the word "mushajarah" (dispute/entanglement), which means the interlocking of those who quarrel with one another. And shajar is of kinds: there is that which is planted and owned, belonging to whoever plants it and supervises its growth; and there is that which comes forth from the earth without anyone sowing it, and this is common property, and usually we leave animals to graze upon it, so they eat from it without anyone turning them away. And here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿in which you pasture [your livestock]﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 10), from sāma (to pasture) the animal that grazes on public land. When an animal grazes on public land, it leaves its traces in paths and marks. And they call a land in which there is vegetation and no animal approaches it a "rawdat anf" (a meadow of disdain), meaning that no one has come to it or approached it; as though it disdained that anything be plucked from it.

Thus Allah teaches us that vegetation does not grow by itself, but needs someone to make it grow. Here the Truth, glorified is He, singles out kinds of cultivation that have a life-giving effect on it, and mentions the olive, the date palm, the grapes, and other fruits of every kind. The olive, as we know, contains fatty substances; the grape contains sugary substances; likewise the date palm, which yields dates, contains sugary substances. The nourishment of man comes from starches and proteins. What the Truth, glorified is He, mentioned first about the cattle, and what He mentioned about plants, makes clear that He has given man the components of food. He is the One who said: ﴿By the fig and the olive, and Mount Sinai, and this secure city. We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾ (Surat al-Tin). That is, He has provided for man's sustenance proteins, fats, starches and vitamins that preserve his life. When doctors wish to feed a person during illness, they dissolve the nutrients he needs in liquids which they drip into his veins by injection, but they fear prolonged feeding in this manner, because the intestines may shrink. Those who feed livestock know that feeding consists of two kinds: a food that fills the belly, and a food that supplies the necessary elements. Straw, for example, fills the belly and supplies it with fibres that help the movement of the intestines, but oilcake nourishes and ensures fatness and abundance of flesh. When the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, the olives, the date palms, the grapes, and of all the fruits...﴾ (Surat al-Nahl), you should receive this statement in the light of the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Is it you who cultivate it, or are We the Cultivators?﴾ (Surat al-Waqi'ah). That is because you only plough the earth; as for the One who makes it grow, it is the Truth, glorified is He. You plough with the iron which Allah placed in the earth and which you extracted yourself, and with the wood which Allah caused to grow; you made from them the plough with which you till the earth that belongs to Allah, and the strength with which you ploughed is granted to you by Allah. Then Allah reminds you that all fruits are of His bounty, so He joins the general to the particular, and says:

﴿...and of all the fruits...﴾ (Surat al-Nahl, 11). That is, what you take is a part of all the fruits, for fruits are many and more than can be counted. The Truth, glorified is He, concludes the noble verse by saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought﴾ (Surat al-Nahl, 11). That is, man must employ his thought upon the gifts of the universe, then examine his position with regard to those gifts, and define his state, so that he finds himself not an agent, while he is capable of acting. The Truth, glorified is He, willed to remind us that reflection is not the task of one person but the task of everyone, as if the Truth, glorified is He, wants our thoughts to support one another; so whoever has an intellectual insight that leads to Allah must speak it to others. In the Qur'an there are verses that end with remembrance (tadhakkur), reflection (tafakkur), contemplation (tadabbur) and understanding (tafaqquh), and each of them leads to certain knowledge. When He says "they remember" (yatadhakkarun), the meaning is that a recollection of it had already occurred, but forgetfulness erased it; so it is as if your task is to remember. As for the word "they reflect" (yatafakkarun), it is the mother of all those meanings, because when you engage your thought you need two things: to look at the data of their outward aspects and the data of their inward aspects. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ (Surat al-Nisa', 82).

This means that you should not take only the façade; rather you must look at the underlying data in order to understand, and when you understand you have come to know. So the task is composed of four stages: you think (tafakkur), then you contemplate (tadabbur), then you comprehend (tafaqquh); then comes knowledge and science ('ilm).

We know that the night and the day are two clear signs; the moon befits the night and the sun befits the day, and they are all bound to one act and form one order. Subjugation (taskhir) means one creature being compelled to serve another, so that each performs its task. The subjugation of the night, the day, the sun and the moon: each has its task, and the task of the night is rest. The Truth, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ (Surah al-Qasas, 28:73)

As for the day, its task is that you toil on the earth to seek sustenance and bounty from God. The sun He made a source of energy and warmth, and it gives you without your asking, and it too cannot refrain from giving by the power of God. It belongs to no one other than God; rather it is part of the order of the cosmos, over which God, glory be to Him, has given no one power, so that no one may dominate another. Likewise, the moon was given by the Truth another task. Beware lest you imagine that there is a task that contradicts another task; rather they are complementary tasks. The Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who said:

﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it appears, and by Him who created the male and the female, indeed your efforts are diverse.﴾ (Surah al-Layl, 92:1-4)

That is: although the night and the day are opposites, they are not in conflict; just as the male and the female are opposites, not so that the task of each contradicts the other, but so that they complete one another. The Truth, glory be to Him, gives the example to clarify this complementarity, saying:

﴿Say: "Have you considered, if God made the day perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than God could bring you a night in which you rest? Will you not then see?"﴾ (Surah al-Qasas, 28:72)

Any person who stays awake two consecutive days cannot resist sleep, and if he performs a task during those two days, he may need rest afterwards extending a week; for this reason God said:

﴿And We made the night as a garment, and We made the day for livelihood.﴾ (Surah al-Naba', 78:10-11)

When a person prays the night prayer (ʿishāʾ) and goes to his bed, he will surely awaken before dawn while at the height of activity, after having spent a restful night in deep sleep, with no anxiety in it. But the person in our countries has imported the dregs of civilization in the form of devices that make him spend the night awake, watching television, video films or satellite channels, so he rises in the morning exhausted, although the people of those lands that produced those inventions, when they use those inventions, place them in their proper position and at their proper time; therefore we find them sleeping early, so that they rise at dawn with determination and vigor. The Truth, glory be to Him, begins a new sentence saying:

﴿And the stars are subjected by His command...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:12)

We notice that He did not bring the stars in coordination with what precedes them, but singled them out with a new sentence, even though they are the least of the celestial bodies, and we may not discern them because of their multitude and the variety of their positions. Yet we find the Truth swearing by them; He said:

﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars, and indeed it is a great oath, if you only knew.﴾ (Surah al-Waqi'ah, 56:75-76)

Every one of those distant stars has a task. If you, in your daily life, when the light goes out, go to see what happened in the fuse box in your house, yet you do not know how electricity reaches your house, nor how science produced the electric lamp for you, nor how the state extended electricity from its generating stations to your home. If you are ignorant of what lies behind the single trace that reaches you in your house, then how about the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars.﴾ (Surah al-Waqi'ah, 56:75)

And He said: ﴿And by landmarks; and by the star they are guided.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:16)

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, has singled them out with a new, independent sentence in which He restated the report of subjugation, because each of them has stations, which are numerous beyond counting and enumeration, and some of them are so distant that their light reaches us only after millions of years. The Truth, glory be to Him, has singled them out with this report of subjugation so that we may perceive that God has a secret in everything He created between heaven and earth. He wants us to turn our attention to the fact that the compositions of things that benefit us face us, and behind them are other things that serve them. And we find the Truth, glory be to Him, concluding the noble verse by saying:

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:12)

We know that the signs are the wondrous matters that a person must not pass over heedlessly; rather he must contemplate them, for in this contemplation there is benefit for him, and he can derive from them the unknowns that bring blessings and happiness to mankind. The word (ya'qilūn, "they reason") means the exercise of the intellect ('aql). We know that the intellect has a special composition; it derives non-sensory matters from sensory ones, and thereby takes from the known a result that was unknown to it, so it is made happy by it and makes those around it happy; then it makes this unknown a premise by which it reaches a new result. Thus does a person derive from the secrets of the cosmos what God wills him to derive and discover of the secrets of the cosmos.

The word *dhara'a* (ذرأ) means that He created a creation which multiplies by its own nature, either through the female conceiving from the male, in humans, animals and plants, or through the hatching of eggs, as in birds. In this way we understand *dhara'a* to mean not absolute creation but creation that reproduces itself. Allah, glory be to Him, created Adam first, then brought forth his offspring from him, so that offspring multiply by their own nature when a pair comes together and produces a likeness of themselves. For this reason the Almighty said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun). Thus Allah, glory be to Him, willed to bestow upon His servants the attribute that they create, but they do not create as He creates. He created Adam and then brought the rest of mankind into being from his seed. Humans may fashion some of the equipment and tools of their lives, but they do not create as Allah creates. They do not create from nothing; they create from what already exists, whereas Allah, glory be to Him, creates from non-existence, from that which has no existence. In this sense He is the best of creators. The example I often give is the grain that grows into seven ears, each ear bearing a hundred grains. Allah, the Almighty, mentioned it to encourage man to spend in the way of Allah. This is tangible material creation: from one grain He causes all of that to grow. Here the Almighty says: ﴿And what He has created for you on the earth, of varying colours﴾ (Surah al-Nahl).

That is, what He has created for us of creation that multiplies by its own nature, varying in its colours. The variation and diversity of colours is evidence of the perfect power of Allah, in that creatures are not created in one pattern. The Almighty gives us the picture of this matter in His saying: ﴿Of varying colours, and some are deep black. And among men, beasts and cattle are [also] of varying colours. Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, Forgiving﴾ (Surah Fatir). And when the Almighty says: ﴿Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, Forgiving﴾ (Surah Fatir).

We should know that by "those who have knowledge" here is meant every scholar who comes to understand a cosmic matter embedded in the universe or sent down directly from the One who brought it into being. The Almighty did not intend by this statement only the scholars of religion. What is meant is every scholar who researches in order to derive knowledge from the unknown and to make clear the secrets of Allah in His creation. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to draw a clear distinction in this matter, so that the scholars of religion would not interfere in experimental scientific research which benefits people. He (ﷺ) found people pollinating date palms, meaning that they would bring the male pollen and fertilise the female palms. He said: "If you did not do it, it would bear fruit." When the palms did not bear fruit, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted the matter, ordered it to be corrected, and said the decisive word: "You are more knowledgeable about the affairs of your worldly life." That is, you are more knowledgeable about experimental and laboratory matters. We observe that what held back civilisation and development in Europe for many centuries was the attempt of the men of religion to restrict scientific research and to accuse every experimental scientist of disbelief. Islam is distinguished by being the religion that did not prevent the study of any sign of Allah in the universe. And from the mercy of Allah is that He makes clear to His creatures the importance of researching the secrets of the universe. He says: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾ (Surah Yusuf). That is, O believer, you must not turn away from any sign of Allah that is in the universe; rather, the believer must engage his mind and thought in contemplation so that he may benefit from it in his belief and his life. The Truth says: ﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ (Surah Fussilat).

As for matters on which the reckoning of the Hereafter depends, they fall within the specialisation of the scholars of jurisprudence (fuqaha). The Almighty concludes the verse about which we are reflecting with: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who remember﴾ (Surah al-Nahl).

Taskhir (subjugation, or making something serve a purpose), as we have already explained, is the bringing into existence of a being for a task from which it cannot deviate, and it has no choice in whether it performs that task or not. We know that the whole universe was subjugated for mankind before man himself was brought into existence; then God created man with choice. Some may think that subjugated beings have no choice, but this is an error, because those beings do have a choice, which they settled at the beginning of their existence. Let us recite His word, the Truth: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it...﴾ (Surah al-Ahzab, 33:72).

Thus we understand that the Truth, glorified be He, gave His creation the choice between subjugation and free choice. However, the beings other than man took their choice once and for all. Therefore it should not be said that the Truth, glorified be He, compelled them. Rather, they chose from the very beginning, because they assessed the time of performance, whereas they did not assess only the time of bearing, as man did. It is as if they said to themselves: "Let me leave by the gate of beauty before the gate of wronging oneself opens before me." We find the Truth, glorified be He, describing man: ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾ (Surah al-Ahzab, 33:72).

Man wronged himself when he chose to bear the Trust, because he assessed the time of bearing but did not assess the time of performance. He is ignorant because he did not know how to distinguish between performance and bearing, whereas the other beings prevented themselves from bearing the responsibility of the Trust, and so they did not wrong themselves by it. Thus we arrive at the affirmation and precise clarification of the meaning of taskhir: it is the bringing into existence of a being for a task that it cannot avoid. As for ikhtiyar (choice), it is the bringing into existence of a being for a task which it may perform or may fail to perform. We have clarified that the subjugated beings had the option to choose from the beginning, so they chose to be subjugated and not to bear the Trust, whereas man undertook a task, relied on his intellect and thought, and arranged the affairs of his life in light of that.

Nevertheless, God gave man some measure of taskhir, so that the whole universe would contain some taskhir and some ikhtiyar. For this reason we find that some events befall man without any choice on his part: he falls ill, or an accident happens to him, or he goes bankrupt. Therefore I say: the disbeliever is heedless of his own choice, because he denies the existence of God and rebels against faith, although he cannot ward off from himself illness or death. In the verse we are now concerned with, the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿And it is He who subjected the sea...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:14). This means that He is the One who created the sea, because He is the One who created the heavens and the earth, and He made the dry land a quarter of the earth's surface, while seas and oceans occupy three quarters of its surface. That is, He is speaking here of three quarters of the earth, and He brought into being the seas and oceans in a form from which we can take some of their food. So He says: ﴿that you may eat from it fresh tender meat and extract from it ornaments that you wear...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:14).

Among the bounties of the Truth, glorified be He, is that the tide sometimes comes in and then is followed by the ebb, so some fish remain on the shore, or a strong wave may carry some fish and cast them onto the shore. Thus provision comes without effort on the part of man. Indeed, the presence of some fish on the shore is what alerted man to the importance of devising ingenuity, making the fishhook, spinning the net, and then moving from these primitive means to modern techniques of fishing. However, the ornament extracted from the sea is pearl, and obtaining it requires that a person dive to the bottom to pick it up. The Truth, glorified be He, draws our attention to the secrets of His treasures, saying: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha, 20:6).

All the treasures of nations are found beneath the soil. If we divide the earthly globe as we divide a watermelon into slices, which we call "a slice of watermelon," we will find that the treasures of each slice are equal in utilitarian value to the treasures of another slice. But every provision found in a part of the earth has a birth time determined by the Truth, glorified be He. There is a place on earth where God has made provision in the form of agriculture, and there is another desert place that people imagine has no benefit at all, and then oil wells gush forth there, and so on. The Truth's subjugation of the sea is not only by its creation in the form it has; rather, you may find for it other things and functions, such as the splitting of the sea by the staff of Moses, peace be upon him, so that every part became like a great mountain. And before that, when the river carried Moses, peace be upon him, after his mother cast him into it by inspiration from God: ﴿Let the sea cast him onto the shore...﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha, 20:39).

Thus we find that a command from God was issued to the sea to carry Moses to the shore as soon as his mother cast him into it. In this way the meaning of the sea's subjugation for other tasks becomes clear to us, beyond the fact that fish are in it and we extract ornaments from it. We know that sea water is salty, unlike river water and rainwater. Water is thus divided into two kinds: sweet water and salt water. Concerning this, the Truth says: ﴿And not alike are the two bodies of water: this one is sweet, palatable, pleasant to drink, and this one is salty and bitter. And from each you eat fresh tender meat and extract ornaments that you wear...﴾ (Surah Fatir, 35:12). They are called "the two" by way of predominance in His word, the Truth: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 55:19). The intended meaning here is sweet water and salt water, and how they meet without mixing. But the sweet water seeps into the depths of the earth, and if you dug at the bottom of the sea you would find sweet water. The Truth, glorified be He, is the One who willed that, and He made it clear in His word: ﴿Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth...﴾ (Surah al-Zumar, 39:21).

Here He, glorified be He, says: ﴿And it is He who subjected the sea that you may eat from it fresh tender meat...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:14).

When the word "meat" is used without qualification, it means the meat of livestock. But when it is qualified as "fresh tender meat," the intended meaning is fish. This is one of the miraculous aspects of Qur'anic expression, because fish that is fit for eating is always fresh. We find someone buying fish and bending the fish, and if it is fresh, that is a sign that it is fit for eating; if it does not bend, that means it has spoiled. If you take a fish out of the sea, you will find its flesh fresh; if you throw it back into water, it returns to swimming and moving beneath the water. But if it is dead, it swells and floats. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade eating floating fish, because it is carrion. The qualification of "meat" here as "fresh" is so that it excludes ordinary meat, which is the meat of livestock. For this reason the scholars say: whoever swears not to eat meat and then eats fish does not break his oath, because custom has established that "meat" means the meat of livestock. In the same verse, the Truth says of the subjugation of the sea: ﴿and that you may extract from it ornaments that you wear...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:14). Thus we find that this matter requires effort, because it is a luxury, whereas about fish He said directly: ﴿that you may eat from it fresh tender meat...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:14). Eating is a necessity, so God guaranteed it and provided facilitations in hunting it, whereas for adornment you must exert yourself to extract it, for it is a luxury. The necessities of life are easy to obtain, but the luxuries of life require that you dive into the water and toil for them. This is an indication that whoever wants to advance in his livelihood should increase his income by exerting his own sweat, not make his living luxurious from the sweat of others. He says: ﴿and that you may extract from it ornaments that you wear...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:14).

The ornament (hilyah), as we know, is worn by women. The subtle point here is that a woman's adornment is for the sake of the man, as if it is the man who enjoys that adornment, and as if he is the one who adorns himself. Alternatively, these things extracted from the sea are not forbidden to men, like gold and silk; gold and silk are currency, whereas pearls are not currency. Wearing (al-libs) is the dominant and common use, but it may also be correct to make a staff or any other item you use from that ornament. He continues in the same verse: ﴿And you see the ships plowing through it...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:14). There were no large steamships like those of our time, only small boats. We know that Noah, peace be upon him, was the first to build a ship, and his people mocked him; had what he built been an ordinary matter, they would not have mocked him. Naturally there were no nails for it, so he tied its planks with ropes. Therefore the Truth, glorified be He, said of it: ﴿And We carried him on a vessel made of planks and nails...﴾ (Surah al-Qamar, 54:13).

The sailing of Noah's ark was by the will of God. The sciences had not yet advanced so that human beings could build the enormous ships that the Qur'an foretold in His word, the Truth: ﴿And His are the ships, raised high upon the sea like mountains﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 55:24).

When we read it now, we marvel at the Qur'an's ability to foretell what human beings would invent, for the Qur'an knows what they will find, not only by the compelling power of His omnipotence, but also by the choices of human beings. His word, the Truth: ﴿And you see the ships plowing through it...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:14). The one who "plows" (mākhir) is the one whose windpipe (ḥalzūm) cleaves the water, and the ḥalzūm is the chest. We find that those who build ships make the prow sharp so that it becomes the spearhead that cuts through the waters with a rushing sound. In this verse, the Truth, glorified be He, bestowed three favors upon His servants: catching fish, extracting ornaments, and the sailing of ships on the sea. Then He adds to them whatever may come about, saying: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:14).

It is as if the ships, as they cut through the water, while a person sees the soft water bearing the solid body of the ship, find in it a delight, besides the fact that these ships carry a person from one place to another. The Truth, glorified be He, concludes the verse by saying: ﴿so that you may be grateful﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:14).

This phrase is used only when enumerating a blessing whose effects are clear and evident, deserving of gratitude from ordinary reason and ordinary human nature. God willed to leave gratitude for those blessings to human beings, and He did not make them grateful by compulsion.

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, shows us that the earth was created in stages, and His saying, glory be to Him, explains this:

﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, alike for those who ask.﴾ (Surah Fussilat)

Thus we learn that the general mass of the earth was created first, and it was created in the state of motion. Because motion is what brings about swaying to the right and left and the body's failure to remain fixed in one position, Allah, glory be to Him, willed to create in the earth the firm mountains (rawasi), which make it appear stable and unagitated. The rasi (firm, anchoring thing) is that which makes something stable. Had the earth been created in the state of stillness, Allah would not have needed to create the mountains; but He created the earth in the state of motion, and He prevented it from swaying by creating the mountains, so that the mountains would be anchors for the earth. In another verse He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them solid, while they pass away as the clouds pass.﴾ (Surah An-Naml, 88)

The word (alqa) indicates that the mountains are a cohesive thing placed so that it would settle. Then He, glory be to Him, joins to the mountains:

﴿And rivers and roads...﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 15).

The Truth, glory be to Him, did not mention a verb suited to the rivers. It is remarkable that the expression gathers solidity in the mountains, fluidity in the rivers, and roads (subul), that is, paths. All of this is:

﴿So that you may be guided﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 15), meaning: the whole act of making is so that we may be guided. We know that the Arabs used to be guided by the mountains and made them into landmarks. An example is the mountain "Harsha," about which the poet says:

Take the belly of Harsha or its back, for on both sides of Harsha there are paths for them.

Likewise, the mountain of at-Tawbad was regarded as a landmark. Similarly, the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿And We called to him from the right side of the mount...﴾ (Surah Maryam, 52).

Thus we find that among the benefits of the mountains is that they are landmarks by which we are guided to routes and places, and that is among the secondary functions of the mountains. Or: "so that you may be guided" (Surah An-Nahl, 15) means by your reflecting on the created things made for you, so that you may be guided to the One who brought them into being for you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 16:

I mean: what has preceded of God's creation consists of signs that point to the necessity that you see the benefits which God has deposited in what He created for you, and that you be guided to belief in a God who originated these things for your benefit. What has been mentioned of the signs of the earth's stability, whether the mountains, the rivers, or the paths, is complemented here by a sign that exists in the sky, namely the stars. We know that everyone who travels on the sea is guided by the star. Almighty God speaks of it here as a specific subjugation; He did not include it among the multiple subjugations, because one star leads to another star, and there are stars whose light has not yet reached us, while we benefit from their effects through other things. We know that the Quraysh used to follow many routes, being guided by the stars along their way, and so they must have had knowledge of the positions of the stars. Almighty God says:

﴿And by the star they are guided﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16).

God has chosen this style from among three styles that could convey the meaning: "yahtadūna bil-najm" (they are guided by the star), "bil-najm yahtadūn" (by the star they are guided), and the third, which is the one God used when He said: ﴿And by the star they are guided﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16).

This is an affirmation of the Quraysh's knowledge of the positions of the stars, because they travelled two journeys every year, and there were no others who possessed that knowledge. The pronoun "hum" (they) comes to give two specificities: the first is that they are guided by the star and not by anything else; the second is that the Quraysh are guided by the star, while other tribes cannot be guided by it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 17:

We know that speech which a speaker addresses to a listener takes many forms. Sometimes it takes the form of a statement (khabar), as when one says: "He who does not create is not like one who creates." This is declarative speech: it is valid for you to affirm it, and valid for you not to affirm it. But if the speaker wants to bring you to affirm it and to make you utter it yourself, he brings it to you in the form of a question, to which you cannot do other than answer with certainty what the speaker desires. We know that the Quraysh worshipped idols and took them as gods, though they did not speak to them and did not send down any method, and they said what the Truth, glory be to Him, related of their speech:

﴿We do not worship them except that they may bring us near to Allah in position.﴾ (Surah al-Zumar, 39:3).

So why, then, do they not worship Allah directly without an intermediary? And why do they not relieve themselves of the hardship of worship and turn to Allah directly? Next, let us ask: what is worship ('ibadah)? We know that worship means obedience to "do" and "do not do" which proceed from the one worshipped. Naturally, there are no commands or obligations from the idols to those who worship them; they are objects of worship without a method, without reward for the one who disobeys, and without reward for the one who obeys. Consequently, those idols are not fit for worship. Let us discuss the matter from another angle. The Truth, glory be to Him, has made clear that He is the One who created the heavens and the earth, the night and the day, the sun and the moon, and subjected all beings to serve man, whom He entrusted with the task of vicegerency (khilafah) on earth. None of these matters is claimed by anyone other than Allah. Indeed, if you asked the disbelievers and polytheists who created them, they would surely say: "Allah." The Truth, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf, 43:87).

For the act of bringing into existence and creating is something no one would dare to claim unless he himself originated it, and when you ask them: "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would say: "It is Allah." Muhammad (ﷺ) had informed them that Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth, and that His method for managing the universe begins with worshipping Him, glory be to Him. Since the Truth, glory be to Him, has claimed this and no one has disputed Him, the claim stands in His favour until an opponent appears, and no such opponent has ever appeared. Here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, the Truth, glory be to Him, did not say: "Do you make the one who does not create like the one who creates?" Rather He said:

﴿Is then He who creates like one who does not create? Will you not then remember?﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:17).

Behind this lies a wisdom: those to whom this address was directed dealt with the idols as though they were God, and they imagined that God was created like those idols. Therefore the speech came in a form that suits this conception.
