The Truth, glory be to Him, wanted to nullify this conception from its foundation, so He made clear that those whom you worship are idols of stone, which are matter and have a form, and that you fashioned them according to your own imagination and capabilities. In this case the object of worship is lower in rank than the worshipper and beneath him, in addition to the fact that those idols possess neither harm nor benefit for those who worship them. Then: why do you call upon Allah when harm touches you? A person calls upon Allah in a situation of harm, because at that moment he does not dare to deceive himself; but the gods they fashioned and worshipped do not hear prayer:

﴿If you call upon them, they do not hear your call, and if they heard, they would not respond to you; and on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association. And none can inform you like the One who is All-Aware.﴾ (Surah Fatir, 35:14).

How, then, do you equate the one who does not create with the one who creates? You must remember, reflect, and employ your minds in what benefits you.

This verse was already mentioned in Surah Ibrahim, where the Truthful (al-Haqq) (subhanahu) said there:

﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him. And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is [often] a wrongdoer and ungrateful.﴾ (Surah Ibrahim, 14:34)

The discussion there concerned those who did not give due recognition to the Creating Divinity (al-uluhiyya al-khaliqa) and the Originating Lordship (al-rububiyya al-mujida) and the Sustaining Lordship (al-mumidda), who denied all of that. The same stance is addressed here, concerning the same people. Allah, glory be to Him, clarifies: if you were to review the favors of Allah, you would never be able to count them. This is because the countable is always made up of individual units that repeat, whereas a single favor in your view contains favors that cannot be counted or enumerated. So what about all the favors combined? Or: Allah, glory be to Him, does not bestow favor except in one respect, namely that He has brought you a blessing, and the individual instances of that blessing are very numerous.

The Truthful (subhanahu) concludes the verse with His saying:

﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 16:18)

That is: despite your disbelief, He will increase you in blessings and give you of the sources of mercy. From you comes wrongdoing, and from Allah comes forgiveness; from you comes disbelief, and from Allah comes mercy. The concluding phrase of the verse here is linked to the concluding phrase of the verse in Surah Ibrahim, where He said there:

﴿Indeed, mankind is [often] a wrongdoer and ungrateful.﴾ (Surah Ibrahim, 14:34)

So He, glory be to Him, is Forgiving of your denial and your ingratitude toward the goodness of Allah, and He is Merciful, so He continues His blessings upon you despite your being wrongdoers and disbelievers.

The secret, as we know, is what you hold within yourself, or what you confide to another while asking him not to make it known to anyone. And Allah, glory be to Him, knows the secret, and indeed He knows what is more hidden than it. He is the One who said: ﴿He knows the secret and what is yet more hidden﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha). That is: He knows what we conceal within ourselves, and He also knows what could become a secret before we conceal it within ourselves. And He, glory be to Him, does not know only the secret; rather, He also knows the open.

Namely, they are not able to create anything; rather, they are created. And the idols, as we have said, are inferior to those who make them. How, then, can it be equal that the object of worship should be inferior to the worshipper? This is a rebuke of their worship. For this reason, the Truth, glory be to Him, says on the tongue of our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him, at the moment he smashed the idols, when his people asked him: "Who has done this to our gods?" and he answered:

﴿He said: Rather, this was done by their biggest one, this.. " 63 "﴾ (Surat al-Anbiya').

They said to him: "The biggest one is merely an idol, and you know that it has no power over anything." And we find the Qur'an saying to the likes of these people:

﴿Do you worship what you carve? " 95 "﴾ (Surat al-Saffat).

So these gods do not create; rather, they are created. But Allah is the Creator of everything, and He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿O mankind, a parable has been set forth, so listen to it: Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it. And if the fly should steal from them a thing, they could not retrieve it from him. Weak are the seeker and the sought. " 73 "﴾ (Surat al-Hajj)

Al-Sha'rawi mentions, after this, the attributes of those idols.

They are indeed dead, for they have no perception and no movement. And His saying: ﴿They are dead, not alive﴾ (Surat an-Nahl 16:21).

It indicates that they never had life before, and life was never established for them in any period of the past, the present, or the future. Thus the attributes of those idols are completed: they create nothing, but rather they are themselves created by those who carved them. Those idols and images will never have life in the Hereafter; rather, they will be fuel for the Fire. The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their spouses, and what they used to worship﴾ (Surat as-Saffat 37:22).

Naturally, those stones will not feel the resurrection of those who worshipped them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 22:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, clarifies the matter of creed (al-mas'alah al-'aqdiyyah).

His saying, the Truth: ﴿Your God is One God. ... ﴾ [Surah An-Nahl: 22].

It prevents there being any other individual like Him. Some may imagine that it is equivalent to the word "ahad" (One). I say: the word "ahad" means the negation that He has parts; He is exalted above repetition or division. In this statement there is reassurance to the believers that they have reached the summit of understanding and belief that God is one. Or: it makes clear to the disbelievers that God is One in spite of your noses, and you will return to Him by force. And with this statement the Truth, glory be to Him, reveals the innate nature (al-fitrah) present in the human soul, which bore witness in the realm of the atoms (alam al-dharr) that God is One with no partner, and that the Resurrection and the Rising are true.

But those who do not believe in God and the Last Day are those who have concealed their innate nature from themselves. The word "kufr," as we have said before, is a covering that requires something covered, and disbelief covers the faith of the original nature. Those who deny the Hereafter only deprive themselves of conceiving what will certainly happen; namely, the reckoning by which reward and good deeds will be repaid for good actions. Perhaps their evil deeds are few, so the Truth, glory be to Him, compensates them for these and they attain Paradise. And those who are wasteful toward themselves hope that the matter of religion is a lie, because they want to distance themselves from the conception of reckoning, and they wish that there were no reckoning. The Truth, glory be to Him, describes them:

﴿Their hearts are deniers, and they are arrogant.﴾ [Surah An-Nahl: 22]. That is: they are not content merely with denying the Hereafter; rather they magnify themselves without any ground for greatness. "Istakbara" means he set himself up as great without possessing the components of greatness, for the "great" must rest upon the components of greatness and ensure for himself that those components remain intrinsic to him. But we humans are sons of accidents (aghyar); therefore it is not proper for us to be arrogant. One of us may fall ill, or the accidents of wealth or rank may leave him. The attributes and perfections of greatness are not intrinsic to any of us, and they may be stripped from one upon whom God has bestowed them. Therefore it becomes fitting for each of us to be humble, to remember his Lord, and to make himself small before his Creator. The Truth, glory be to Him, alone holds the right to pride; He is the One whose attributes and components reach the summit of perfection, and they never leave Him at all.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 23:

When we consider (la jaram), its meaning is that what comes after it is a fixed, established truth. Here "la" is a negation particle, and "jarm" is derived from "al-jarimah" (the crime, the transgression), which is the breaking of something that is believed in for the sake of the wholeness of the community. When we say "la jarm," it means: what follows it is an established truth. And what follows "la jarm" here is: that Allah knows what they conceal and what they disclose. Every verse of the Qur'an in which the words of the Truth "la jarm" occur conveys this same meaning, such as His saying, the Truth:

﴿Without doubt, for them is the Fire, and they will be neglected.﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 62)

And likewise His saying, the Truth:

﴿Without doubt, in the Hereafter they are the ones who will be the losers.﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 109).

Some scholars have said that His saying, the Truth, "la jarm" carries the meaning of "la budda" (there must necessarily be), and this means that His saying, the Truth:

﴿Without doubt, Allah knows what they conceal and what they disclose...﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 23).

Allah must necessarily know what they conceal and what they disclose, and there is no escape from the fact that those who disbelieve are the losers. The scholars have analysed the wording in order to reach its most precise secrets. Allah's knowledge does not apply only to what is open, but also to what is secret; for He will call them to account for all their deeds. Almighty Allah concludes the verse with His saying:

﴿Indeed, He does not love the arrogant.﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 23).

If we ask: what is the connection between Allah's knowledge and the punishment? We say: did they not say among themselves:

﴿Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?...﴾ (Surah Al-Mujadilah, 8).

When the word of Almighty Allah is revealed to inform them of what they said among themselves, this is evidence that the one who conveys to them is truthful in conveying from Allah. Despite that, they became arrogant; they persisted and were obstinate, and pride in sin seized them, and they wanted through arrogance to escape from adhering to the method that the Messenger ﷺ brought to them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 24:

And His saying, the Truth: ﴿What has your Lord sent down?﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 16:24).

It clarifies the evasion (istidrak) that God carried out on the tongue of the speaker, so that they would know that they have a Lord. Had they not been believers in a Lord, they would have declared that; but in their heedlessness they objected to the sending down, and did not object to there being a Lord for them. This is evidence of their belief in a Creator Lord; yet they object to Muhammad (ﷺ) and to what was sent down to him from God. And ﴿they said, "Tales of the ancients"﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 16:24). The asatir (tales) are falsehoods. Had they been sincere with themselves, they would not have acknowledged divinity while rejecting also the word sent down to them. Among them there were those who said:

﴿They said, "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, so they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾ (Surah al-Furqan, 25:5).

But there was another side whose stance was different, which will be explained later: the side opposed to these people. The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And it is said to those who were mindful of God, "What has your Lord sent down?" They say, "Good." For those who do good in this world there is good, and the abode of the Hereafter is better.…"﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 16:30).

Behind this there is a story that clarifies the points of disagreement between a believing group and an unbelieving group. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) called his people and his kin to belief in the One God, who had sent down to him a method in a miraculous Book, the news of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) began to spread among all the tribes of the Arabian Peninsula, and every tribe sent a delegation of its own to learn about and investigate the matter of this Messenger. But the unbelievers of Quraysh wanted to bar the way of God; so they divided themselves among the four entrances of Mecca, and whenever a questioner from the delegations of the tribes asked them, "What did your Lord, who sent you a Messenger, say?"

Here the group of unbelievers who met them would reply: "He is a lying Messenger, who distorts and blasphemes." The aim, of course, was that the unbelievers would turn away the delegations of the tribes. God, the Truth, informs His Messenger (ﷺ) of what happened. When those standing at the gates of Mecca were asked by the delegations that came to investigate the news of the Messenger, "What has your Lord sent down?", they would answer, "He repeats the tales of the ancients." This single answer from those standing at the four gates of Mecca indicates that it was an agreed-upon reply, prepared in advance. By this they intended to turn the delegations of the tribes away from listening to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). They likened the Reminder sent down from God to what, for example, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith used to recount to them of the old stories, which resemble the stories of ʿAntarah and Abu Zayd al-Hilali that are told among us. This was the first round of the exchange of claim and rebuttal.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 25:

Consider His saying, glorified is He:

﴿That they may bear their burdens in full﴾ (Surah An-Nahl 16:25).

Observe how the Truth, glorified is He, makes clear that the human soul has many conditions. If it overindulges itself in those domains, it may overindulge in the moral domain, the social domain, and others, and so it bears the burden of everything it does. Here the Truth, glorified is He, also makes clear that the soul which commits sins, when it misguides another soul, does not bear of the sins of the soul it misguided except what resulted from the misguidance. So He says:

﴿And of the burdens of those who mislead them without knowledge﴾ (Surah An-Nahl 16:25).

This is because the soul that has been misguided may commit sins in other fields that are not connected to the process of misguidance. The Truth, glorified is He, is too just to make the misleader bear burdens he was not the cause of. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, said here: ﴿And of the burdens of those who mislead them without knowledge﴾ (Surah An-Nahl 16:25), meaning: the misleader bears the burdens of his own soul, and likewise bears a portion of the burdens of those he misled, those burdens resulting from the misguidance. In this is the absolute justice of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. Those who were misguided commit two kinds of burdens and evil deeds: burdens and evil deeds resulting from the misguidance, which those who misled them carry with them; and the burdens and evil deeds they committed by themselves without being driven to them by those who misled them, for which they alone bear the consequences. Thus each person bears the loads of the sins he committed.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) settled this when he said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, none of you will take anything from it [unjustly] but he will come with it on the Day of Resurrection carrying it on his neck: a camel with a grunt, or a cow with a low, or a sheep bleating."

Apply the same to one who steals in bricks, cement and iron, and deceives people. And when the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Those who mislead them without knowledge﴾ (Surah An-Nahl 16:25),

this draws our attention to the necessity that worldly life not distract us from the most important matter occupying the mind of creation: the search for the Creator who honoured creation and prepared the universe for their reception. It was incumbent upon those who heard from the disbelievers of Quraysh to seek out the Messenger and to listen to him directly, for they were unlettered people to whom no messenger had previously come. Concerning them the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones who know not the Book except wishful thinking, and they are only assuming﴾ (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:78).

When the Messenger came to them, it was incumbent upon them to search and to listen to him directly, not merely by transmission from the disbelievers. Therefore Allah will punish them, because they neglected the matter of religion. But the severest punishment will be for those who had knowledge of the Book. The Truth, glorified is He, is the One who said: ﴿So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say, "This is from Allah," to exchange it for a small price﴾ (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:79).

The Truth, glorified is He, describes those who bear their own burdens and some of the burdens of those they misled: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they bear﴾ (Surah An-Nahl 16:25), meaning: evil is what they carry of sins. They were not content with their own burdens, but also barred from the way of Allah and prevented others from listening to the matter of faith. As a result of this, one who has not heard permits for himself some of what Allah has forbidden, and so bears the burden of the misguidance of the one who barred him from the way.

Therefore we find the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "The worst of you is one who sells his religion for his worldly life, and worse than him is one who sells his religion for the worldly life of another."

So one who sells religion to enjoy a little deserves punishment; but one who sells his religion so that another may enjoy will find the greater punishment from Allah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 26:

The Truthful, glorified is He, here brings the account of the earlier peoples and the patterns (sunan) which He established among them, in order to console His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and to clarify to him that what has happened to him is not unprecedented; rather, it has already happened to those messengers who came before him. And He informs him that no messenger was sent except after trials had become widespread and corruption had spread, and mankind had lost its immunity of faith, as a result of the absence of those who believe and do righteous deeds, and who enjoin one another to truth and to patience. The clear example of this is what happened to the Children of Israel, concerning whom the Truthful, glorified is He, said: ﴿They did not forbid one another from any wrongdoing they committed.﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah, 79], so the punishment of Allah descended upon them. This is the fate of every nation that does not forbid the evident wrong before it. And He, glorified is He, says here: ﴿Those before them had already plotted.﴾ [Surah al-Nahl, 26]. Makr (plotting) is a hidden scheming which the schemer plots in a way that conceals it from the one targeted by it. But when someone plots against the messengers, he is plotting against one whom Allah supports, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware. And when Allah informs His Messenger of the plot, He nullifies every effect of this scheming, for He has made known to him the One who is able to annul it. The Truthful, glorified is He, is the One who said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail."﴾ [Surah al-Mujadilah, 21].

And He is the One who said: {And již Our word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that they would surely be given victory} [Surah al-Saffat, 171–172].

The Truthful, glorified is He, applied this to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the disbelievers of Quraysh plotted against him and gathered young men from the tribes to kill him. So Allah covered them, and they did not see his departure for the Hijrah, and the camp of disbelief did not prevail over him by any means: neither by the assaults of the tongue nor by the assaults of the limbs. As for those who plot against the messengers, the Truthful, glorified is He, has not left them without punishment: ﴿So Allah came at their building from its foundations.﴾ [Surah al-Nahl, 26], meaning: if they make their plotting like a lofty building, then the Truthful, glorified is He, leaves them to the feeling of false security, and digs for them from beneath them, so the roof above them falls down upon them. Thus Allah strikes the abstract example with a perceptible matter. And His saying, the Truth:

﴿So the roof fell down upon them from above them.﴾ [Surah al-Nahl, 26]

clarifies that they are situated inside this building, and that the "above" here belongs to the roof, an "above" that Allah willed in order to come upon them:

﴿The punishment from where they did not perceive.﴾ [Surah al-Nahl, 26]. Thus the punishment of Allah comes suddenly, for they had plotted by night, and thought that this plotting was hidden from the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting.

Would that the matter were limited to this; but rather, Allah will also punish them in the Hereafter.

Thus is the punishment in this world and in the Hereafter, and they will suffer disgrace on the Day of Resurrection. Disgrace is humiliation and abasement, and it is stronger than beating and harm. No one can brace himself against it. Disgrace is a shivering that covers the body, and no one it reaches escapes it. Although a person may be able to conceal physical pain, disgrace is a psychological meaning, and psychological meanings seep through the skin. No one can conceal its effect, because it destroys the essence of arrogance by which the one who plotted and schemed lived. Allah, glory be to Him, clarifies this meaning in His words about the town whose provision came to it from Allah and which then disbelieved in Allah's blessings. He says: ﴿And Allah presents an example: a town that was secure and at peace, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place, but it denied the favours of Allah, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear, for what they used to do.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 112). That is, it is as if the whole body has become possessed of the sense of taste, and as if hunger has become a garment that its bearer suffers from. So he hungers in his nape, hungers in his face, hungers in his arm, skin and steps, and in everything he has.

When this disgrace occurs, all the cells of arrogance come to an end, especially before those whom a person claimed would confirm that his greatness, tyranny and pride would remain and that he had something to support him. He continues, glory be to Him, in challenge: ﴿Where are My partners about whom you used to dispute?..﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 27). That is, where are the partners you used to worship, so you made yourselves a faction and made the believers another faction. The word (tushaqqun) is derived from "al-shaqq," as one says "he split the wall" or "he split the wood." The intended meaning here is that you made the believers, and those who were with the Messenger, into a faction you opposed, and you took the side of falsehood and abandoned the side of truth. Here, those who were given knowledge by Allah say: ﴿Indeed, disgrace today and evil are upon the disbelievers.﴾ It is as though this matter will become a scene in the presence of the Truth, glory be to Him, among those who plotted against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and those whom Allah gave knowledge will attend it. Knowledge, as we know, comes directly from Allah, then is conveyed to the angels, then from the angels to the messengers, then from the messengers to the nations whom the Truth, glory be to Him, charged His messengers to convey His method to.

Just as the world witnessed the fall of the methods they followed out of their desires, and the fall of those they worshipped besides Allah, the Last Day will witness the disgrace and evil surrounding them. The disgrace may come from the terror of that great situation, and Allah protects those who believed in Him with tranquillity.

We know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Have I not conveyed? O Allah, bear witness."

Just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conveyed to his nation and they responded to him, he also asked them to be an extension of his message and to convey it to people. For the Truth, glory be to Him, has ended the messages after the message of Muhammad, peace be upon him. It has become the responsibility of the Muhammadan nation to convey the message of the Messenger (ﷺ) to everyone to whom it has not been conveyed.

The Messenger (ﷺ) also said: "May Allah make radiant the face of a man who heard my saying, memorised it, and conveyed it to one who did not hear it, for many a one who is conveyed to understands better than one who hears."

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and bring you as a witness against these? On that day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were levelled over them.﴾ (Surah al-Nisa, 41-42). That is, they will wish that they were turned into dust, as He, exalted is He, said in another place: ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, the Day when a man will look at what his hands have sent forward, and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾ (Surah al-Nahl).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 28:

He, exalted is He, says:

That is: they cause them to die while they are wronging themselves. In another verse, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, said: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 118).

It is well known that a person may wrong another for the sake of his own desire and benefit. So how does he wrong himself? This is what they call "foolish wrong," when you wrong your own self that lies between your two sides. But how is that?

We know that if the enemy comes from outside, it is easy to confront him, unlike when he comes from your own self that lies between your two sides. That is a dangerous enemy, hard to confront and to be rid of.

Here we pose a question: What is wrong (zulm)? Wrong is that you withhold from the rightful owner his right. So then: what right did your self have over you, such that it is said that you wronged it by withholding its right? We say: when you are hungry, do you not eat? When you are thirsty, do you not drink? When you are exhausted from work, do you not sleep?

So then: you give your self what it desires, which comforts it and which it hastens toward. Likewise, if you sleep and they try to wake you for work and you do not wake up, or they try to wake you for prayer and you are lazy, the outcome in the end is failure at work or loss in trade, and so on.

So then: this is a collective loss, and the loser is the self. Thus a person has wronged himself by what has escaped it of benefits in this world. Measure the matters of the Hereafter by this.

Look here at the particulars of this world: when they are complete for you, is that the end of everything, or with their end does something begin? With their end something begins. We ask: is the thing that is about to begin a repeated image of what ended in this world?

It is not so, because what ends in this world is cut off, and I took my share of it according to my capacities, and my capacities have limited possibilities. As for what will begin, that is, in the Hereafter, it does not end but is eternal, with no cessation, and the bounty in it comes according to the capacity of the Bestower, your Lord, glorified and exalted is He.

So then: when you give yourself pleasure in the transient, cut-off life of this world, you forfeit for it the lasting pleasure of the Hereafter. And this is the utmost wrong to the self. Now we return to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those whom the angels cause to die...﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 28).

This verse establishes the causing of death by the angels. Causing death in reality belongs to Allah, exalted is He, as came in His saying: ﴿Allah takes the souls at death...﴾ (Surah Az-Zumar, 42).

But since the angels are commanded, it is as if Allah is the one who causes the souls to die, although He, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah takes the souls...﴾ (Surah Az-Zumar, 42).

And He said: ﴿Say: The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will cause you to die, then to your Lord you will be returned﴾ (Surah As-Sajdah, 11).

And He said: ﴿Our messengers cause him to die﴾ (Surah Al-An'am, 61).

So then: the speech came from Allah once, from the chief of the angels, Azra'il, once, and from his assistants among the angels once more. So then: the matter is either direct performance, or through an intermediary, or from the original commander. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those whom they cause to die...﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 28).

The meaning of tawaffi (causing to die, taking in full) is from "waffahu haqqahu," that is: He paid him his full term, and diminished nothing of it, as you say to a man: "I have paid you your debt," that is: I have taken what is yours from me.

﴿Wrongers of themselves...﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 28).

We note that it came in the plural form, and "zalimi" means "zalimin" (wrongers), and "anfusahum" (their selves) is plural, and when a plural faces a plural, division requires singulars, that is, that each of them wrongs his own self. Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Then they will offer submission...﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 28), that is: they submitted and yielded, and their arrogance and haughtiness in the world no longer benefit them. All of that departed from them with the departure of the world that slipped out from between their hands. Since they now offer submission, then before that they were in war; they were at war with themselves, and they are the ones of discord in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who opposed...﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 27), that is: you make this on one side and that on another side. It is as if the verse says: they raised the white flag and said: we have no endurance for war. Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿We used to do no evil...﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 28).

This is like His saying in another verse: ﴿Then their temptation was only that they said: By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ (Surah Al-An'am, 23). The reality is that after they offered submission, raised the white flag and surrendered, the state of punishment seized them, so they said, trying to defend themselves: ﴿We used to do no evil﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 28).

And it is astonishing how these people lie to Allah in such a situation: "Upon whom are you lying now?!" So the Truth, glorified is He, answers them: ﴿Yes...﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 28).

It is a particle of negation for the negation preceding it, and it is well known that negating a negation is an affirmation, so "bala" negates: ﴿We used to do no evil﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 28).

So its meaning is: no, rather you did evil. Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed Allah is Knower of what you used to do﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 28).

And from the mercy of Allah, exalted is He, that He did not suffice with knowledge alone, but beyond that He recorded it against them in a book that will be presented to them on the Day of Resurrection, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We are sufficient as reckoners﴾ (Surah Al-Anbiya', 47).

And He said: ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird of omen to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find laid open. "Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this day as a reckoner"﴾ (Surah Al-Isra', 13-14).

Some like to deny the possibility of recording and writing deeds. We say to them: Come to what human reason has now reached in recording images, sounds, fingerprints and other things. All of this makes this matter easy for us when we raise the capacities of human reason to the divine capacities that have no limits.

So there is no basis, then, for denying the power of the angels, "watchful and ready" (Qaf, 18), in recording deeds in a book that preserves his actions and counts against him every major and minor thing.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 29:

We have already said, in explaining His saying, may He be exalted, describing Hell:

﴿It has seven gates; for each gate there is a portion assigned.﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 44).

That is: for each group of the people of disobedience there is a known gate. There is a gate for the people of usury, a gate for the people of bribery, a gate for the people of hypocrisy, and so on. You can imagine what befalls the one who combines these sins! He enters this gate, then comes out of it to enter another gate. Truly, how wretched are these people!

Here He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿So enter the gates of Hell﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 29).

Here the form is also plural, meaning: each one of you enters through the gate that has been assigned to him. Then He, glorified be He, says:

﴿So evil is the abode of the arrogant﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 29).

Al-mathwa (abode) is the place of residence. He, may He be exalted, says in another place:

﴿Without doubt, Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 23).

So takabbara (to be arrogant) and istakbara (to be arrogant, in the sense of seeking to be great) and everything that comes in the pattern (tafa''ala) indicate that this arrogance of theirs is not intrinsic. The one who is truly arrogant is arrogant by virtue of something intrinsic within him that no one can strip from him. But one who is arrogant by means of something he does not possess, his arrogance is not real, and it quickly passes away; these people will be made small by the very things they were proud of in this world. Thus no one has the right to be arrogant, because true greatness belongs to Allah, mighty and majestic.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 30:

We have already spoken about His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿And when it is said to them, "What has your Lord sent down?" they say, "Legends of the former peoples."﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

This is a scene and snapshots that show the situation which ended with their acknowledging against themselves that they had been disbelievers. These verses were revealed concerning a group who were entering Makkah, and at its gates through which the people of the desert came, the disbelievers had divided themselves among the entrances of Makkah in order to prevent those entering it from hearing the news of the people of faith in the new Prophet.

The believers among the Muslims would watch for the opportunity and go out to the outskirts of Makkah under the pretext of herding sheep, for example, in order to meet these questioners and inform them of the news of the Prophet ﷺ and of his call. This indicates that one who asks about something does not content himself with the first passerby he asks, but repeats the question in order to ascertain the contradictions. So when they asked the disbelievers, they said: ﴿Legends of the former peoples.﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

They were not satisfied with that, but asked the people of faith, and their answer was:

﴿They say, "Good."﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

This is so that we understand that when a person encounters something that has two opposing directions, he does not content himself with one direction, but must listen to the second, and then it is for the intellect to choose between the alternatives.

So then: when those entering Makkah asked the people of disbelief:

﴿"What has your Lord sent down?" They say, "Legends of the former peoples."﴾ (Surat an-Nahl)

And when they asked the people of faith and piety: ﴿"What has your Lord sent down?" They say, "Good."﴾ (Surat an-Nahl)

We note here, in His saying: ﴿And it is said to those who were mindful of God﴾ (Surat an-Nahl), that the Truth, glorified is He, did not make clear to us who they were, nor did He specify their identity, and this indicates to us that they were unable to confront and were concealing themselves, because they were still weak and could not confront. This situation of questioning was repeated until you reach the right direction, when the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, rebuked one of His prophets, our master David, peace be upon him, in His saying: ﴿Has the news of the litigants reached you, when they climbed over the walls of the prayer niche? When they entered upon David and he was startled by them, they said, "Do not fear. We are two litigants, one of whom has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth, and do not exceed the bounds, and guide us to the right path. Indeed, this is my brother; he has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe, and he said, 'Entrust it to me,' and he overcame me in speech."﴾ (Surat Sad). So what did David, peace be upon him, say?

﴿He said, "He has certainly wronged you by demanding your ewe in addition to his ewes..."﴾ (Surat Sad). It is evident in David's ruling, peace be upon him, that he was influenced by the words "he has ninety-nine," and let us suppose he had nothing: had he not wronged his brother by taking his ewe? So then: David was influenced by the claim of the litigant, and introduced another consideration into it, and this was a procedural error in presenting the case; for these "ninety-nine" have no bearing on the case. Rather, they were to sway the judge and to influence his feelings and his leanings, and to show that the litigant is rich and yet he is covetous and unjust.

David, peace be upon him, soon discovered his error in this judgment, and that it had been a trial and a test from God: ﴿And David thought that We had only tried him...﴾ (Surat Sad). That is, We tested him so that We might teach him the lesson in practice: would he judge with truth and observe all aspects of the case or not? Note here the prophetic acuteness: David quickly recognized what he had fallen into, acknowledged it, sought forgiveness from his Lord, and fell down bowing, turning in repentance. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and fell down bowing and turned in repentance.﴾ (Surat Sad).

So then: the evidence here is that it was incumbent upon David, peace be upon him, to hear the other side and the second party to the dispute before judging it. And His saying: ﴿And it is said to those who were mindful of God, "What has your Lord sent down?" They say, "Good..."﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

What is "the good"? The good is everything that the soul finds pleasant with all its faculties. But the pleasure may be limited to a time, and then it leaves regret and remorse. So then: this is not good; for there is no good after which comes the Fire, and likewise there is no evil after which comes Paradise.

So then: we must know that good remains good always, in this world and likewise in the Hereafter. If we take as an example the one who takes narcotics, we find him taking a momentary pleasure and a false euphoria that soon passes; then this "good" in his view soon turns into an immediate evil in this world and a deferred evil in the Hereafter.

So then: look at the lifespan of good in yourself, its manner and its outcome. This is the good in His saying: ﴿They say, "Good."﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

So then: it is good that the soul finds pleasant, and it remains good in this world, and there follows from it good in the Hereafter, or it is connected to the good of the Hereafter. Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, explained it in His saying, glorified is He:

﴿For those who do good in this world there is good, and the abode of the Hereafter is better...﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

From this verse we understand that the believer should not abandon the world and its means, for perhaps the disbeliever takes it from you and prevails over you by it, or tempts you in your religion through it. Whoever worships God is more entitled to His secrets in existence, and the secrets of God in existence belong to the believers, and they should not leave the taking of the means of this world to the disbelievers.

Strive, O believer, in the means of this world so that you may be safe from the temptation of the disbelievers in your worldly life. And what we are in now, of our need for others, is not hidden, for it has given them the opportunity to control our policies and our resources. Therefore He, glorified is He, says: ﴿For those who do good in this world, there is good...﴾ (Surat an-Nahl), that is: they take their good deeds, and they have the upper hand by what they strove for and what they did in their worldly life; and by this a person benefits himself and benefits others, and the more the circle of benefit from you to people widens, the higher your hand is, and your reward and your good are connected to the good of the Hereafter.

Therefore the Prophet ﷺ said: "No Muslim plants a plant or sows a seed, and a bird or a human or an animal eats from it, but it is for him a charity."

From this verse there also becomes clear to us another aspect, which is one of the fruits of good in this world, namely security. Whoever lives in this world upright, having committed nothing for which he would be punished, you find him secure and at peace; and if harm or adversity befalls him, you find him secure and unafraid, because he has committed nothing that calls for fear.

Take for example the thief: you always see him anxious and fearful, his eyes darting right and left; if he sees a policeman he panics and becomes watchful, saying to himself: "Perhaps he is after me." But the upright person is secure and at peace.

Among the fruits of this good and this uprightness in this world is that a person lives according to his capacity and does not burden himself with what he cannot bear. Long ago they said to one of them: "Meat has become expensive." He said: "Make it cheap." They said: "And how can we do that?" He said: "Abstain from it."

A poet versified this:

"When something becomes expensive for me, I leave it, and it becomes cheapest when it is most expensive."

Do not say: "The soul yearns for it, desiring it," for it is, as the poet said:

"The soul desires when you make it desire, and when you bring it back to little, it is content."

In our practical life, a person may return from his work and the food has not yet been cooked, and the table is not yet ready, and he is hungry, so he eats whatever is available and the problem ends; one thing takes the place of another, and the soul is content with what it has obtained. And so that a person may live according to his capacity, he must balance his income and his expenses; whoever has hardship in his income, or whose avenues of sustenance are constricted, must have hardship in his spending, and must restrict the soul's appetites; and thereby he lives concealed and at ease, content of soul, and calm of eye.

Some in such situations resort to borrowing to spend on the appetites of the soul, and may borrow for what he enjoys for a month and live in humiliation for a lifetime. Therefore it is wise, before you ask people for a loan, first to ask your own soul, and request of it that it be patient with you, and grant you respite until a time of ease, and not force you into the humiliation of asking. And before you blame the one who refused you, blame the soul that rebelled against you first.

How eloquent was our poet who formulated these values in his saying:

"If you wish to borrow money to spend, ask your soul to spend from the treasure of its patience. If it complies, you will be the rich one; and if it refuses, then the appetites of the soul in a time of hardship are upon you. And granting respite until a time of ease, every refuser thereafter has a broad excuse."

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And the abode of the Hereafter is better...﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

The good in the Hereafter is from God, and its bliss is according to the Benefactor, blessed and exalted is He, without toil, hardship, or work. And it is known that the phrase ﴿They say, "Good..."﴾ (Surat an-Nahl), which the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, explained by His saying: ﴿For those who do good in this world, there is good...﴾ (Surat an-Nahl), is contrasted with the word "evil." This evil is what was stated in the words of the disbelievers: ﴿"What has your Lord sent down?" They say, "Legends of the former peoples."﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

So those said "good," and those said "evil." But if it is said: "that is better than that," then good is present in both, except that one of them exceeds the other in goodness.

This is the meaning of the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "The strong believer is better and more beloved to God than the weak believer, and there is good in both."

Therefore, when He said: ﴿For those who do good in this world, there is good...﴾ (Surat an-Nahl), He said: ﴿And the abode of the Hereafter is better...﴾ (Surat an-Nahl), that is: better than the good of this world. So the good of this world is good, and the good of the Hereafter is better than it. The Truth, glorified is He, concludes the verse by saying:

﴿And how excellent is the abode of the righteous﴾ (Surat an-Nahl), that is: the abode of the Hereafter. Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, wished to give us a concise picture of the abode of the righteous, as though it were a telegram.

al-Sha'rawi's commentary, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66), on surah 16, verse 31:

"Al-jannat" means the gardens that contain trees, flowers, fruits and greenery, "such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." And this is not all. This is the general garden that everyone who enters it sees. Rather, each one has a private palace of his own, as proven by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And He will admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of Eden. That is the great achievement﴾ (Surat al-Saff, 61:12).

So here there is a common portion for all: ﴿Gardens of Eden which they will enter, beneath which rivers flow﴾ (Surat al-Nahl, 16:31).

The meaning of His saying ﴿gardens of Eden﴾ (16:31) is: gardens of permanent residence, because in them is everything a person needs, so he has no need for anything other than them. Suppose you entered the greatest gardens and parks of the world, Hyde Park for example. The most that can happen is that you stroll there for some time, then fatigue overcomes you, boredom and exhaustion strike you, and you seek rest from that outing. As for Paradise, it is the Garden of Eden, where you love to reside permanently.

The Truth, glory be to Him, describes these gardens, saying: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾ (16:31).

In another verse He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾ (Surat al-Tawba, 9:100).

The meaning of "flowing beneath them" is that they flow beneath them, though they may come from another place. Here someone might say: the flow of these rivers could be prevented from you. Therefore the verse came: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾ (16:31), meaning that their flowing is inherent in Paradise, and no obstacle prevents it from you. Then He, the Exalted, says:

﴿For them therein is whatever they wish﴾ (16:31). The "wish" here is not the wish of this world and its desires, but a wish according to the abundant disposition that suits the Hereafter and its bliss. For example: if you enter upon a person of modest condition, you have a wish in accordance with his state; if you enter upon one of the great or the wealthy, you have a higher wish, and so on.

So: psychological wishes differ according to the one from whom they are requested. If the one from whom it is requested is God, who is not incapable of anything, your wish is unrestricted. The "wish" in the verse is not like the wish of this world, because the wish of this world is limited by the environment of this world. As for the wish of the Hereafter, it is the wish that opens up, ascends and rises, just as wishes among human beings rise according to their ranks and positions.

It is related that when a daughter of one of the kings of Persia was taken captive by a man, they wished to buy her from him and offered him what he wanted. He said: "I want a thousand dinars for her." They gave him the thousand dinars and took her from him. One of them said to him: "She is the king's daughter; if you had asked him for such-and-such, he would not have withheld it from you." He said: "By God, if I had known that there was a number beyond a thousand, I would have asked for it." He had asked for the utmost that his knowledge reached.

Therefore, when the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to explain to us this Qur'anic text:

﴿For them therein is whatever they wish﴾ (16:31).

And likewise His saying: ﴿Therein is whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in, and you therein will abide forever﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf, 43:71).

He said: "Therein is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." So the frame of the verse is defined by the extent of what they have with their Lord.

﴿Thus God rewards the righteous﴾ (16:31): that is, this is the reward they deserve for what they sent forward in this world, and for what they denied themselves of forbidden pleasures. The time of reward has now come, and it is a reward that is longer-lasting and more enduring. Therefore the Blessed and Exalted Truth said in another verse:

﴿"Eat and drink with pleasure for what you sent forward in the days gone by"﴾ (Surat al-Haqqa, 69:24).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 16, verse 32:

Meaning: the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) are those whom the angels take in death (tatawaffahum al-mala'ikah) in a good state (tayyibin). As for the phrase:

﴿Those whom the angels take in death, while they are good.﴾ (Surah an-Nahl 16:32)

The meaning of "tatawaffahum" is: they come to seize their souls. Here the act of taking (tawaffi) is attributed to the angels collectively, as if they were the soldiers of the principal Angel of Death, 'Azra'il. We have already said that the Truth, blessed and exalted, sometimes attributes the taking to the angels, sometimes to the Angel of Death:

﴿Say: The Angel of Death who has been charged with you will take you.﴾ (Surah as-Sajdah 32:11)

and sometimes He attributes it to Himself, glorified be He:

﴿Allah takes the souls.﴾ (Surah az-Zumar 39:42)

This is because Allah, glorified be He, is the Supreme Commander, 'Azra'il is the principal Angel of Death, and the angels are his soldiers who carry out His orders. As for His words:

﴿good (tayyibin)﴾ (Surah an-Nahl 16:32)

it corresponds to the preceding verse:

﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves.﴾ (Surah an-Nahl 16:28)

The good (at-tayyib) is that thing in which there is a lasting good that does not cease, and whose good does not turn into evil; it is that thing in which the soul finds a rest that brings all its faculties into harmony, on condition that it continues toward something better than it. Nothing continues toward something better and finer than it except the good of values and the good of religion. As for anything else, it is a temporary good that soon is abandoned.

For this reason, when two people claim love for the sake of Allah, we say: this is a phrase that is said, and its proof is that the affection between you grows each day beyond the day before; for love for the world is tainted by greed and whims, so you see love decreasing day after day, according to what each of them takes from the other. As for those who love each other for the sake of Allah, they receive from a bounty that never runs out, which is the bounty of the Truth, blessed and exalted. So if you see two people whose affection increases, know that it is the affection of Allah and for Allah, unlike affection for worldly purposes, which soon ends.

Is there anything better than that they purified their souls from the defilement of shirk? Is there anything better than that they made their deeds sincerely for Allah? And is there anything better than that they did not commit excess against themselves in anything?

And enough of good for them is that, at the moment the Angel of Death comes to them, the reel of their deeds passes before them, and the summary of what they sent forward in the world; so they see good, and you see them joyful and rejoicing, and this appears on their faces at the hour of death. You see him white-faced, radiant, smiling, bearing the seal of good, goodness and happiness, because of what he witnesses of the goodness of his deed, and because of the reward he anticipates from Allah, blessed and exalted.

In complete contrast to this state, we see the people of wretchedness, and what they are in at the moment of the death-rattle: blackness of face and an evil end, we seek refuge in Allah.

﴿They will say: Peace be upon you.﴾ (Surah an-Nahl 16:32)

That is: when the angels take them in death, they say to them, "Peace," because you have departed the world in peace, and you will go forth to the Hereafter in peace. So the peace of the good is a peace connected from the world to the Hereafter, a peace resulting from the soundness of your religion in the world and the soundness of your turning toward Allah, without fear in the Hereafter.

Here there is another peace, which came in the words of the Truth, blessed and exalted:

﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, until, when they reach it and its gates are opened, its keepers will say: Peace be upon you; you have been good, so enter it, abiding eternally.﴾ (Surah az-Zumar 39:73)

Then comes the supreme peace upon them from Allah, blessed and exalted, for all these peace greetings to these good people are derived from the supreme Peace:

﴿Peace, a word from a Lord, Most Merciful.﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin 36:58)

And is there any better or finer than this peace that comes directly from the Truth, blessed and exalted? And here it is strange to consider the peace of the people of al-A'raf upon the good believers while they are in Paradise. We know that the people of al-A'raf are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, so they are held back at al-A'raf, a place between Paradise and Hellfire. The natural division requires that the scale have two pans, which the Truth, blessed and exalted, mentioned in His words:

﴿As for one whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasing life. And as for one whose scales are light, his refuge will be the Abyss.﴾ (Surah al-Qari'ah 101:6-9)

These are two states of the scale. Where then is the state of equality between the two pans? It came in His words, the Exalted:

﴿And upon al-A'raf are men who recognize each by his mark.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf 7:46)

That is, they recognize the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire.

﴿And they call out to the companions of Paradise, "Peace be upon you," not yet having entered it, though they hope.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf 7:46)

The wonder here is that the people of al-A'raf are in a predicament, hardship, and preoccupation with their own dire situation, yet we see them rejoicing for the good people of Paradise and hastening to greet them with peace.

So: the people of Paradise have peace from the angels at death, peace when they enter Paradise, supreme peace from Allah, blessed and exalted, and peace even from the people of al-A'raf, who are absorbed in their own condition.

﴿Enter Paradise by what you used to do.﴾ (Surah an-Nahl 16:32)

That is: because you paid the price; the price is your righteous deeds in the world and your following of the method of the Truth, blessed and exalted. Some see an apparent contradiction between this verse and the noble hadith:

"None of you will enter Paradise by his deed." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy."

In truth there is no contradiction between them. But how do we reconcile the verse and the hadith?

Allah, the Exalted, reveals to His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, the hadith just as He reveals the verse to him; both proceed from one niche and one source, in accordance with His saying:

﴿And they resent only that Allah and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty.﴾ (Surah at-Tawbah 9:74)

So the hadith here is one, and it is not that Allah enriched them with one thing suited to Him and the Messenger with another suited to him; rather it is one enrichment and one bounty. Likewise, there is no contradiction between the verse and the hadith. How? 

The Truth, blessed and exalted, imposed obligations on the human being after the age of maturity and reason, and He had been bestowing blessings upon him since his childhood; and when He imposed obligations, He imposed upon him something that returns to the benefit and good of the human being, and nothing of it returns to Allah. Then afterward He recompenses him for this obligation with Paradise.

So: the whole obligation is for the benefit of the servant in this world and the Hereafter. Therefore, the legislation of reward from Allah in the Hereafter is pure grace from Allah, and if the servant obeyed his Lord with the obedience required of him in voluntary, obligatory actions, he would still not fulfill the blessings of Allah upon him; and thus the reward in Paradise is a grace and favor from Allah. Or: when they said:

﴿by what you used to do﴾ (Surah an-Nahl 16:32)

they mean that their deeds were an ordinary cause for entering Paradise, and then they attain it by the grace of Allah. Thus the verse combines deeds and grace together; therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted, reinforces this with His saying:

﴿Say: By the bounty of Allah and His mercy, so in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate.﴾ (Surah Yunus 10:58)

They do not rejoice in deeds, because deeds do not match the blessing they are in; rather true joy is in the bounty of Allah and His mercy. And in the supplication: "O Allah, deal with us by bounty, not by strict justice."

Finally: did they used to act this way on their own? No, but by a method set for them by their Lord, blessed and exalted. So it is by grace, not merely by deeds. An example of this: a father says to his son, "If you work hard this year and excel, I will give you such-and-such." When the son excels, everything is in his favor: the success and the gift.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 33:

After the verses presented the reward of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) who said "good" (khayr), the discourse returns to those who said "the fables of the ancients" (asatir al-awwalin), who oppose the call to God (al-da'wa ila Allah), and who take toward it a stance of enmity, scheming, lying in wait, and harm. This is a rhetorical question (istifham) from the Truth, blessed and exalted, to them: what are you waiting for? After what you have done regarding the matter of the call, and after you have barred people from it, what are you waiting for? Do you expect to see with your own eyes? Before you there are only two matters, both of which will certainly befall you:

Either the angels will come to you and take your souls (tatawaffakum), or the command of your Lord will come, and that is the Day of Resurrection, and nothing will save you from it except that you believe. Or do you expect some good? Good will never come to you at all. As He, exalted is He, said in other verses:

﴿Has the command of Allah come? So do not seek to hasten it.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl).

And He said: ﴿The Hour has drawn near.﴾ (Surah al-Qamar).

And He said: ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near for them.﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya').

So, then: they are only waiting for events that come upon them with evil: the angels come to seize their souls while they are in a state in which they are wronging themselves, and then they offer peace (yulqun al-salam) against their will; or: the Great Calamity (al-tamma al-kubra) comes upon them, which is the Resurrection. Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Thus did those before them.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 33), meaning: among those who denied the messengers before them. That is, this is a matter well known about them from before: ﴿And Allah did not wrong them.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 33), meaning: Allah did not wrong them when He decreed to requite them with such and such; and the intended meaning here is not that He wronged them with punishment, because the punishment had not yet befallen them.

﴿But they were wronging themselves.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 33). This is what we call foolish wronging (al-zulm al-ahmaq), because wronging others may return to the wrongdoer with some kind of benefit, whereas wronging oneself returns nothing to him at all. That is because they transgressed against themselves in the world by what contradicts the method of Allah, and thereby they forfeited for themselves the bounty of this world and the bounty of the Hereafter. This is their wronging of themselves.

Meaning: when they wronged themselves, the requital of that came upon them, and what was done to them was called an evil deed (sayyi'ah), because the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, calls the requital of an evil deed an evil deed, in His words: ﴿Thus did those before them do﴾ [42:40].

He, exalted is He, also says: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾ [16:126]. This is called al-mushakalah (correspondence of like with like), meaning that this is of the same kind as that.

As for His words, ﴿what they did﴾ ('amal): 'amal is the exercise by any bodily member of a person of its function. Every limb has a function: the foot, the hand, the eye, the ear, and so on. The tongue's function is to speak, and the rest of the limbs' function is to act. Thus the tongue alone has taken half, and the remaining limbs have taken the other half, because the harvest of the tongues bears the principal share of the consequence.

The word of testimony, "There is no god but Allah," must be uttered so that one is known to be a believer, and then the role of action comes to support this utterance. For this reason He, exalted is He, says: ﴿O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Greatly hateful is it in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do﴾ [61:2-3].

Through speech, the methods reach the ears. So how can the limbs act without a method? For this reason the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, gave the ear a special status among the senses. It is the first limb of a person to perform its work, and it is the limb whose function never ceases. All the limbs, for example, do not work during sleep except the ear, and through it one is summoned and awakened from sleep.

If you survey the verses of the Noble Qur'an and consider the verses of creation, you will see the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, saying: ﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and He made for you hearing and sight and hearts that you may give thanks﴾ [16:78]. Then it is the instrument of testimony on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing and their sight and their skins will testify against them﴾ [41:20].

For this reason the Lord, glorified is He, says: ﴿So We struck upon their ears in the cave for a number of years﴾ [18:11].

The meaning of "We struck upon their ears" is that We disabled the ear, which is not disabled, so that their sleep would be undisturbed and they could settle in their cave. Had Allah not placed in their bodily constitution something specific, rest would not have been settled for them throughout 309 years.

The Truth, exalted is He, says: ﴿And there befell them what they used to mock﴾ [16:34].

What did the disbelievers mock? They mocked the resurrection, the reckoning, and the punishment that awaited them. They said, as the Qur'an relates: ﴿When we die and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected? Or our forefathers, the former ones?﴾ [37:16-17].

And they said: ﴿When we are lost in the earth, shall we indeed be in a new creation?﴾ [32:10].

Then their mockery reached the point that they hastened the punishment, saying: ﴿Bring us what you promise us, if you are of the truthful﴾ [7:70].

And they said: ﴿Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claim﴾ [17:92].

Would anyone ask his enemy to bring down punishment upon him unless he were mocking? So the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, said to them: You will not be able to withstand this punishment that you mock. So He said: ﴿And there befell them⁠…﴾ [16:34], meaning it encompassed them and descended upon them, so they cannot flee from it, nor find any escape from it, as in His words:

﴿And Allah encompasses them from behind⁠﴾ [85:20].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 35:

We observe that whenever the verb appears explicitly in its intended sense, its object (al-muta'allaq bihi) is not mentioned. Thus He did not say "they associated (others) with Allah," because that is known, and shirk means association with Allah. Therefore the Exalted says here:

﴿And those who associated [others with Allah] said...﴾ [16:35]

Then the Truth, glorified is He, relates their statement:

﴿Had Allah willed, we would not have worshipped besides Him anything, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything besides Him.﴾ [16:35]

Here they are defending themselves, and this is the kind of determinism on which the disbelievers hang their sins as a scarecrow (shammaah), saying: Allah has decreed upon us and ordained such-and-such. So the one who wrongs himself says: "My Lord is the One who willed this for me, He is the One who guides, He is the One who misguides, He is the One who made me commit sins," and so on through these statements empty of truth and of any real outcome. Then why does He punish me?

Let us discuss the one who makes these statements, for he has an intellectual contradiction, and the matter is not clear to him. To remove this ambiguity, we say to him: Why did you not say: "If Allah has willed obedience for me and decreed it upon me, then why does He reward me for it?" That is the counterpart. Why did you say the first and not the second? (Hmm!)

It is clear that the first drags evil and punishment upon you, so it stuck in your mind; but the second drags good upon you, so you overlooked mentioning it.

We say to him: When you do your deeds, are they all good? Or are they all evil? Or are some of them good and some of them evil?

The answer here is clear. Therefore: you are not always disposed toward good, nor are you always disposed toward evil, so you are capable of good just as you are capable of evil.

Therefore there is a difference between one who creates you capable of an act and its opposite, and one who creates you confined to an act and not its opposite. Since He created you capable of good and capable of evil, He clarified to you His method and explained the recompense to you. So He said: Do good, and its reward is such; do evil, and its reward is such. This is the method.

The one who wrongs himself likes to say: "Allah has decreed it upon me." This is strange, as though he had looked at the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) and examined it, and found that Allah had decreed for him to drink wine, for example, so he went and drank it because Allah had decreed it for him.

If the matter were so, you would be obedient in this drinking of yours. But the matter is contrary to what you imagine. You do not know that it was decreed for you until after you have acted, and the act on your part is preceded by the resolve to act. So have you looked at the Preserved Tablet, that you know what Allah has decreed for you?

Note here, and know that Allah, the Exalted, decreed from eternity, because He knew that you would act in time, and Allah's knowledge is absolute and has no limits. We strike an example, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude: a father observes his son in his studies, finds him negligent and not diligent, and so anticipates his failure in the examination. Did the father enter with his son and make him write wrongly? No. Rather he anticipated his failure because of his knowledge of his son's condition and his lack of merit for success.

Therefore: Allah decreed in advance and from eternity, because He knows what the servant does in the first place. The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, has given us another picture of this method when He directed the believers to the Ka'bah after their direction had been toward Bayt al-Maqdis. He, the Exalted, said:

﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah that pleases you. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it.﴾ [2:144]

Then He informed His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, with His words:

﴿The foolish among the people will say: "What has turned them from their qiblah which they were on?"﴾ [2:142]

The verb came thus in the future: "will say." They had not yet said this statement, and this is a Qur'an recited in the hearing of all, not hidden from any of these fools. Had these people had intellect, they would have kept silent and not hastened to this saying, and they would have forfeited the opportunity to undermine Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the truth of the Noble Qur'an.

They could have kept silent and charged the Qur'an with falsehood, but none of that happened. Thus the will and command of Allah were fulfilled, even against the disbelievers who seek a contradiction in the Noble Qur'an. And this verse:

﴿And those who associated [others with Allah] said...﴾ [16:35]

explains and clarifies the saying of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿Those who associated will say: "Had Allah willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything."﴾ [6:148]

Here "will say" (sayaqulu) and in the other verse "said" (qala), so that we know that no one can oppose the saying of Allah or change His judgment. Then He says:

﴿neither we nor our fathers﴾ [16:35]

Why did these people not speak only of themselves? What is the wisdom in their defending their fathers here? The wisdom is that they would need this matter later and would make it an argument when they say:

﴿Indeed we found our fathers upon a community, and indeed we are following in their footsteps.﴾ [43:22]

So there is no argument for those who hang their excess on the scarecrow of destiny, claiming that Allah decreed disobedience upon them. For we see even among Muslims those who speak this speech and incline to these falsehoods, and among them are those whose boldness toward Allah, Mighty and Majestic, carries them to liken this matter to the poet's saying: "He threw him into the sea bound, and said to him: Beware, beware lest you be wet with wealth." Only a wrongdoer does this!! Exalted is Allah and far above the statements of the ignorant and the disbelievers. And also there are those who say: man is the one who creates the act, and others oppose them, saying: No, rather our Lord is the One who creates the act.

We say to them all: Understand. In reality there is no disagreement. And we ask: What is the act? The act is the directing of a limb toward an event. When you direct a limb toward an event, what is it that you have done? Did you give the hand, for example, the power of movement by itself? Or was it your will that directed its movement?

The limb is created by Allah, the Exalted, and likewise the will that governed the limb is also created by Allah. Therefore: what you did is only that you directed what is created by Allah toward what Allah does not love in the case of disobedience, and toward what Allah loves in the case of obedience.

Likewise we must note that Allah, the Exalted, has cosmic wills (muradat kawniyyah) and legislative wills (muradat shar'iyyah). The cosmic will is what comes to be in fact; everything you see in the universe Allah willed to be. The legislative will is the requesting of a thing because it is beloved.

Let us take an example to clarify this: the disbelief of the disbeliever. Allah willed it cosmically to be, because He created him with choice and said:

﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve.﴾ [18:29]

And since Allah created you with choice, you are able to turn toward faith or turn toward disbelief, and then you disbelieved. So: did you disbelieve against His will, and contrary to His wish, exalted is He? Far be it from Allah. This means that the disbelief of the disbeliever is a cosmic will, and not a legislative will.

By the same measure, the faith of the believer is both a cosmic will and a legislative will. As for the disbelief of the believer: the believer in truth does not disbelieve. So it is a legislative will and likewise a cosmic will, and so on. Thus we must distinguish between what is willed cosmically and what is willed legislatively.

For this reason, when a commotion occurred in the Sacred Mosque in Mecca some years ago, in which gunfire was discharged and the safe were terrorized, some said: How can this happen when He, the Exalted, has said:

﴿And whoever enters it is safe.﴾ [3:97]

And here the situation is killing and disturbing the safe within it? In truth these people confused a cosmic will with a legislative will. The meaning of the verse is: "Whoever enters it, grant him safety," that is: make him safe. This is a demand from Allah, blessed and exalted, and it is a legislative will which may or may not come to pass. As for the cosmic will, it is what actually happens. Thus what happened in the Haram was a cosmic will, and not a legislative will.

Then He, the Exalted, says on their tongues:

﴿nor would we have prohibited anything besides Him.﴾ [16:35]

The explanation of this verse appears in His saying:

﴿Allah did not institute any bahirah, nor sa'ibah, nor wasilah, nor ham; but those who disbelieve invent falsehood against Allah, and most of them do not reason.﴾ [5:103]

Then He, the Exalted, says affirming:

﴿Thus did those before them.﴾ [16:35] That is: this is the custom of the earlier obstinate ones.

﴿So is there upon the messengers except clear notification?﴾ [16:35]

The notification (al-balagh) is what lies between the servants of Allah and Allah, and it is the notification of the messengers, and what is meant by it is the method: "do" or "do not do." Allah says this to you only while you are able to act and able to refrain.

Therefore we see the Truth, blessed and exalted, lifting obligation from the one under compulsion, so no ruling attaches to him, because in a state of coercion he may do what he does not will and does not love; and likewise the insane and the child who has not reached the age of reason. None of these is bound by a ruling. Why? Because Allah wants to guarantee soundness for the instrument of choice in decision, which is the intellect.

When a person is subject to obligation, he must make the decisive criterion in:

﴿So is there upon the messengers except clear notification?﴾ [16:35]

the notification of the method: do and do not do. For this reason the Noble Qur'an rebuked those who brought a saying from themselves without a basis from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. He, the Exalted, said regarding them:

﴿And they made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned. And they said: Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them.﴾ [43:19-20]

He, glorified is He, denounced them for that and asked them:

﴿Or have We given them a book before this, so they are holding fast to it?﴾ [43:21]

And He addressed them in another verse:

﴿Or do you have a book in which you study?﴾ [68:37]

And the phrase "the clear notification" means that the responsible person must be notified. If shortcoming occurs in that the responsible person is not notified, the shortcoming is attributed to the people of the true religion who are connected to it, and the charge upon them is to convey this method to whoever has not reached it. Many hadiths have been related urging the conveying of Allah's religion to those who have not received it.

As the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Convey from me, even if it is a single verse."

And his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "May Allah make radiant the face of a man who heard my saying, preserved it, and then conveyed it to one who did not hear it, for many a bearer of knowledge is more retentive than one who hears."

Thus the Almighty says here:

﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 36)

And in another verse He says:

﴿...from among every nation...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 84)

Each of these has its own meaning. As for His saying ﴿...from among every nation...﴾ (84), it means: from among themselves. He came forth from them and grew up and was raised among them, and they knew his qualities, his truthfulness, and his standing among his people. As for His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿...in every nation...﴾ (36), the word "in" here indicates containment: within the nation as a whole. This indicates penetration into the entire nation, so the message does not reach one group and bypass another, but must be delivered to the whole nation.

Similarly, He says once:

﴿We sent...﴾ (Surah al-Hadid, 26)

and once more:

﴿We raised up...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 36)

There is a difference between the two meanings. ("Arsalna," "We sent") indicates sending, which means that a sender reaches a recipient through an intermediary. ("Ba'athna," "We raised up") indicates that something previously existed and was obliterated, and that We wish to revive it anew.

To clarify this matter, we return to the story of Adam (peace be upon him), when God taught him all the names and then caused him to descend from the Garden to the earth. He said:

﴿Then when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 38)

And in another verse He said:

﴿Then when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will not go astray, nor will he be distressed.﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha, 123)

So this is a method from God for Adam (peace be upon him), and it was incumbent upon Adam to convey this method to his children, and upon his children to convey it to their children, and so on. However, heedlessness may overtake the one who conveys the method, or he may fail to safeguard it, and so the methods become obliterated. From here God revives them anew. The matter of messages does not come suddenly, as a sudden event for some group; rather, it has existed since the beginning of creation.

Messages, then, are a reviving of a divine method that was meant to remain in people's remembrance, passed down by fathers to sons. However, heedlessness may afflict the one who conveys, so that he does not convey, or it may afflict the one who conveys so that he does not adhere to what he conveys. Therefore God renews the messengers.

Many verses convey this meaning, such as His saying:
