It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted, wishes to draw His creatures' attention to a cosmic phenomenon in existence that is perceptible, which each of us perceives in himself and in what he sees of appearances; and among these appearances is the phenomenon of the shadow, whose motion man is unable to grasp.

In another verse the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿...and their shadows at morning and evening. (13:15)﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd). So Allah, glorified is He, wishes to generalize the idea of glorification (tasbih) throughout the whole cosmos, as He said:

﴿...And there is not a thing but exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their glorification... (17:44)﴾ (Surat al-Isra').

So everything that is called "thing" glorifies, however small it may be. And His saying:

﴿...whose shadows turn around from the right and the left... (16:48)﴾ (Surat al-Nahl).

Here we pause with the Qur'anic expression, where He used "al-yamin" (the right) in the singular, while He used "al-shama'il" (the lefts) in the plural. This is because when the Truth, blessed and exalted, said:

﴿Have they not looked at what Allah has created of a thing...? (16:48)﴾ (Surat al-Nahl),

He used the least of what can be conceived of His creatures, "shay'" (thing), which is singular; then He said, glorified is He:

﴿...shadows... (16:48)﴾ (Surat al-Nahl), in the plural form, meaning the aggregate of these things. A person does not cast the shadow of one thing only; rather, the shadows of many things. And "min" here indicates generality:

﴿...of a thing... (16:48)﴾ (Surat al-Nahl), i.e., every thing. Thus, to suit the singular, He used "al-yamin," and to suit the plural, He used "al-shama'il." Then He, exalted is He, says:

﴿prostrating to Allah, while they are humbled. (16:48)﴾ (Surat al-Nahl).

So what is the connection between the motion of the shadow and prostration? "Sujjadan" means humbling oneself before Allah. It is as if the motion of the shadow and its extension over the extent of time is evidence that it is connected to its highest Mover and the highest Speaker of "Be," and the shadow is one of His signs, subjected to Him, prostrating, humbled before His saying: "Be, and it is."

We have said that there is a difference between a thing you prepare with a cosmic preparation and a thing you prepare with a predestined preparation. The maker of a time bomb prepares it so that it explodes at the time he wishes; the matter is not so in the preparation of the cosmos.

Allah prepared the cosmos with a predestined preparation, resting on His saying "Be," and in continuous expectation of this divine command ("Be, and it is"). Thus, the matter is not mechanically fixed, no; rather, it is fixed by predestination.

Therefore some people like to say: the sun has so many years remaining, after which its light will end, and they build other judgments upon this. We say: No... the matter is not so. The sun is subject to predestined preparation, bound by it, and awaiting the "Be" to which the whole cosmos listens; therefore the Exalted says:

﴿Every day He is in a matter. (55:29)﴾ (Surat al-Rahman). Thus the noble verse has shown that everything called "thing" prostrates to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the word "thing" came in the singular indicating generality. We have known prostration in what Allah has obligated us of a pillar of prayer, and it is the utmost of humility, the humbling of the essence of the worshipper before the worshipped. So we humble ourselves standing, we humble ourselves bowing, we humble ourselves sitting, but the completion of humility is that we prostrate to Allah. And why was the completion of humility that we prostrate to Allah?

We say: Because man has a general essence, and within this essence is the chief of the essence, such that when it is mentioned, it refers to the essence, and what is meant by it is the face. Therefore, when the Truth, blessed and exalted, speaks of the annihilation of existence, He says:

﴿Everything is perishing except His Face. (28:88)﴾ (Surat al-Qasas).

And likewise in His saying:

﴿except seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High. (92:20) And he will surely be satisfied. (92:21)﴾ (Surat al-Layl).

So "the face" is used and what is meant is the essence. When the face prostrates to Allah, the Exalted, that indicates the humbling of the whole essence, because the most honored part of man is his face; so when he presses it to the ground, he has come with the utmost humility of his whole essence before the worshipped, the Mighty and Majestic.

The verse also shows that the shadow too prostrates to its Lord and Creator, glorified is He. Shadows may belong to inanimate things, such as a tree, a building, or a mountain; these fixed things have shadows that are also fixed and do not move. As for the shadow of a human or an animal, it is a moving shadow. The Truth, blessed and exalted, has given us an example of complete humility in shadows, because the shadow of every thing never leaves the earth at all, and this is an example of perfect submission.

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, elevates the matter of prostration from inanimate things to shadows in His saying:

﴿...and their shadows at morning and evening. (13:15)﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd), meaning the essences prostrate, and likewise the shadows prostrate; therefore some knowers marvel at the disbeliever, saying: O disbeliever, your shadow is prostrating while you are denying.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 49:

The kinds of existence (ajnas al-kawn) that man knows are four. Either it is inanimate matter (jamad); when the property of growth (numuw) is found in it, it becomes a plant (nabat); when the property of movement and sensation (harakah wa hiss) is found in it, it becomes an animal (hayawan); when the property of thought (fikr) is found in it, it becomes a human being (insan); and when the property of self-originated luminous knowledge ('ilm dhati nurani) is found in it, it becomes an angel (malak). These are the kinds that we know.

Here the Exalted Lord moves us from the prostrating shadows of the fixed inanimate objects to the thing that moves. Although it moves, its shadow is also upon the earth. So when the Ever-Glorified said:

﴿And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth…﴾ (Surah al-Nahl 16:49)

He explained this general statement with His words:

﴿…of creature (dabbah), and the angels…﴾ (Surah al-Nahl 16:49), meaning: from the least of moving things, which is the creature (dabbah), up to the highest things, which are the angels.

Someone may say: Does whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth prostrate to Allah?

We say to him: Yes. Because you define prostration in your own case as placing your forehead on the ground, which shows that the essence, in its height and its lowness, is prostrating to Allah, submitting in complete submission, since you have made the forehead together with the foot.

The Exalted Lord wants us to know that servitude (ubudiyyah) pervades all existence. For the disbeliever, although he is rebellious against Allah in what Allah has granted him choice (ikhtiyar) in—whether to believe or disbelieve, whether to obey or disobey—Allah has nonetheless given him that choice.

We say to him: You have become accustomed (ulif) to rebellion against Allah. He asked you to believe, but you disbelieved; He asked you, O believer, to obey, but you disobeyed. So you have a habit (ilf) of rebelling against the Truth. But do not think that you have left prostration and submission to Allah, because Allah makes things happen to you that you dislike, and they befall you despite your nose, while you are submissive. This is the meaning of His words in the previous verse:

﴿while they are humbled (dakhirun)﴾ (Surah al-Nahl 16:48), meaning: abased, subjugated, and compliant, even though they have become accustomed to rebellion against the Truth, glorified is He. Otherwise, could one who has become accustomed to leaving the wishes of Allah in what He has granted him choice in, be able to refuse Allah if He wills to make him ill, or impoverish him, or cause him to die?

No, he cannot. Rather, he is humbled and abased in everything that He brings upon him of decrees, even if he refuses them, and even if he has become accustomed to departing from the wishes of Allah.

Therefore: there is nothing in the creation of Allah that can depart from the wishes of Allah, because it departs from Allah's legislative wishes (al-muradat al-shar'iyyah) in obligation (al-taklif) only through the choice that Allah has given it. Otherwise, if He had not given it choice, it could not rebel, as is the case with the cosmic wishes (al-muradat al-kawniyyah) in which there is no choice.

So we say to the disbeliever who rebels against the Truth, glorified is He: Rebel if illness befalls you, and say: I will not fall ill; rebel against poverty and say: I will not become poor. And as long as you are not able, and you will submit unwillingly, then submit willingly, gain the matter, end the problem of your life, and face another life that is cleaner than this life.

As for His words:

﴿…creature (dabbah)…﴾ (Surah al-Nahl 16:49)

it is everything that crawls upon the earth, and crawling upon the earth means movement and walking. And His words:

﴿…and the angels…﴾ (Surah al-Nahl 16:49)

meaning: the angels are not called "creature" (dabbah), because Allah made their striving in affairs by wings. So the Exalted said:

﴿Possessors of wings, two, three, and four…﴾ (Surah Fatir 35:1)

And He said in another verse:

﴿There is no creature on the earth, nor a bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you…﴾ (Surah al-An'am 6:38)

So Allah created the bird that flies with its wings as the counterpart of the creature that crawls upon the earth, and thus it comprised both: the creature and the angels.

The particle (ma) in the verse is used for non-rational and non-discerning beings, because most things existing in the cosmos have no knowledge or understanding. Therefore the Exalted said in another verse:

﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it…﴾ (Surah al-Ahzab 33:72)

The Exalted Lord concludes the verse with His words:

﴿while they are not arrogant (yastakbirun)﴾ (Surah al-Nahl 16:49), meaning: the angels, who are the highest of Allah's creation, are not arrogant, because their loftiness in creation, of luminosity and so-and-so, does not give them presumption (idlal) against their Creator, glorified is He, since the One who gave them this honour is Allah, the Exalted and Glorified.

Since it is Allah who gave them this honour, it is not permissible to be presumptuous because of it, for the one who is presumptuous relies only on essential qualities that are not bestowed, whereas a thing bestowed by another may not be used to presume against the one who bestowed it on you. Therefore the Blessed and Exalted Lord says:

﴿The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels who are near [to Him]…﴾ (Surah al-Nisa' 4:172)

So they will not refrain from worshipping Allah and prostrating to Him, despite the fact that Allah has honoured and elevated them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 50:

What is fear? Fear (khawf) is dread and apprehension (fazaʿ wa-wajl). Fear, dread and apprehension arise only from anticipating something from above you, which you are not able to remove. Had you been able to remove it, there would be no reason to fear it. Therefore, matters that fall within your capacity you do not fear; you say: if such-and-such happens, I will do such-and-such, etc.

And since the noble angels ﴿do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ (Surat al-Tahrim: 6),

what then is the reason for fear? We say: fear may arise from a shortcoming that occurred on your part, whose consequence you dread; and fear may arise from awe (mahaba) of the one feared, and from reverence for him and magnifying him, without any sin and without any shortcoming. For this reason we find the Arab poet saying, justifying this fear:

I stand in awe of you out of reverence, though I have no power over you, nor could I ever fill the eye of one who loves her.

So: sometimes fear comes because of an anticipated harm resulting from a shortcoming on your part, and sometimes it comes merely from awe, reverence and magnification. As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿from above them...﴾ (Surat al-Nahl: 50).

What is meant here by "above"? We know that the directions are six: above, below, right, left, in front, and behind. The direction of "above" is the one that dominates; that is why, even in building fortresses, they erect them on high places, so that by their height they may control all directions in observation.

So: "above" is the place of elevation, and this elevation may be elevation of place (makan), or elevation of rank (makana).

The one who says it is elevation of place holds that God is in the heaven, on the evidence that the slave-girl who was asked, "Where is God?" pointed to the sky and said, "In the sky."

She pointed to the direction of elevation, because it is not correct to say that God is below. God, glory be to Him, is exalted above place. Whoever is exalted above place is exalted above time, for God, Mighty and Majestic, is exalted above being confined, neither by place nor by time, because place and time are created by Him... So who created time and place?

So: since they are created by Him, He, glory be to Him, is exalted above time and place.

They said that "above" here is literal elevation, elevation of place, meaning that He, exalted is He, is higher than us. We say to whoever holds this elevation: God is higher than us... from which side? From this one or from that one?

So: the elevation here is elevation of rank, on the evidence that we see the guards who guard palaces and fortresses, where the guard is higher than the one guarded, above him, so he is above him in place; but is he above him in rank? Certainly not. As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿and they do what they are commanded﴾ (Surat al-Nahl: 50).

This is obedience: that you do what you are commanded and avoid what you are forbidden. But the verse here mentioned only one side of obedience, namely:

﴿and they do what they are commanded﴾ (Surat al-Nahl: 50).

The verse did not say, for example, "and they avoid what they are forbidden." Why? We say: because the verse contains what they call logical implication (al-talazum al-mantiqi), and what is meant by logical implication is that every prohibition of something entails a command to its opposite, so every prohibition returns to a command to its contrary.

Thus His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿and they do what they are commanded﴾ (Surat al-Nahl: 50) logically implies "and they avoid what they are forbidden," as if the verse has combined both sides. God, Exalted is He, created the angels with no work except that they are absorbed in the Essence of God. Among them are angels appointed over creation, namely: ﴿and those who arrange affairs﴾ (Surat al-Nazi'at: 5).

He, Exalted, says: ﴿For him are successive angels before and behind him, who guard him by the command of God...﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd: 11).

And among them: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording﴾ (Surat al-Infitar: 10-11).

So: there are angels who have a relation to us, and they are those whom the Exalted commanded to prostrate to Adam when God created him, shaped him with His hand, and breathed into him of His spirit... as if God, glory be to Him, were saying to them: this is the human being whom you will serve. So prostration to him by God's command is a declaration that they guard him by the command of God, record for him such-and-such, act for him in such-and-such, and arrange his affairs, etc.

As for the angels who have no relation to the human being, who are unaware of him and know nothing of him, these are the ones meant in His saying, glory be to Him, to Iblis: "Did you become arrogant, or were you of the exalted category?" This category of angels has no relation to the human being; their whole task is glorification and remembrance, and they are the ones meant by His saying, Exalted:

﴿They glorify Him night and day, and they never tire﴾ (Surat al-Anbiya': 20).

Everything in existence, then, is subject to God's purposes for it, except what God has exempted, namely the human being in choice. God, glory be to Him, has not compelled anyone: neither the human being nor the cosmos in which he lives. God, glory be to Him, offered the trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, and they refused to bear it and feared it... as if they had said: we do not want to be choosers, but we want to be subjugated, and we have no part in the matter of trust and obligation!!

Why then do the heavens and earth with their sky refuse to bear this responsibility?

We say: because there is a difference between accepting a thing at the time of bearing it and having the ability to do it at the time of performing it. There is a difference: we have bearing, and we have performance. We have previously given an example of bearing a trust, and we said: suppose a person wished to deposit with you a sum of money, fearing its squandering, so that you might keep it for him until he needs it; and at this time you are able to bear it, you intend to return his trust when he asks for it, your obligation is sound, and your intention is sincere. This is the time of bearing the trust. But when the time of performance comes, circumstances may compel you to spend this money, or some obstacle may prevent you from returning it, or your obligation may change.

So: the time of performance is something else. Therefore, one who wants to clear his obligation does not guarantee the time of performance, and refrains from bearing the trust, saying to himself: No, if I can guarantee myself at the time of bearing, I cannot guarantee myself at the time of performance.

This is an example of what happened with the heavens, the earth and the mountains when they refused to bear the trust, because they assessed its responsibility and weight and their lack of assurance of fulfilling its right, so they refused to bear it from the outset. Likewise, the human being should be sensible when bearing trusts; therefore the Exalted says:

﴿But man bore it; indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾ (Surat al-Ahzab: 72).

What did the human being fail to know? He failed to assess his state at the time of performing the trust, so he wronged himself. Had he approached the matter from the door of beauty, as they say, he would have said: O Lord, make me like the heavens, the earth and the mountains, and do with me what You will, for I am obedient to Your command.

Therefore, among the servants of God are those who accepted choice and the bearing of obligation, but then went beyond their choice to the purpose of their Lord and Creator, and said: O Lord, You created in us choice, and we are able by it to act or not to act; but we have renounced our choice for Your choice, and our purpose for Your purpose, and we are obedient to Your command. These are the servants of God who deserve this attribution to Him, glory be to Him, and Exalted.

So: there is a difference between one who acts by choice while able not to act, and one who acts by compulsion and subjugation. The first, although able not to act, has let his Lord's purpose in obligation prevail over his own purpose in choice. Then the Blessed and Exalted moves on to the summit of doctrinal matters concerning the human being,

The verse's prohibition comes as a consequence of the human being's departure from the intent of his Lord, glorified is He. What is remarkable is that humankind and the jinn, that is, the two weighty ones (al-thaqalan), are the ones granted choice in the whole of creation: they have choice in some matters and are subjugated in others. Yet nothing else in God's creation has deviated from this arrangement.

The heavens, the earth and the mountains also had choice, and they chose subjection (al-taskhir, being made subservient). The matter was settled at the very beginning. Nevertheless, they are subjected and perform their task in the service of humankind. The sun has never objected or refused. It shines on the believer just as it shines on the disbeliever. The same is true of the air, the earth and the milch animal. Everything in God's universe is made subservient to all. So all these things have a function, and they perform it in the most perfect manner.

For this reason, the Exalted says concerning these things:

﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures, and many of mankind?﴾ (Surah al-Hajj, 18)

﴿And many of mankind...﴾ (Surah al-Hajj, 18). He did not say "and mankind" [in full]. Then He said: ﴿...and many have deserved the punishment﴾ (Surah al-Hajj, 18). This is the state of the honoured human being whom God chose and to whom He left choice. All other kinds fulfil their duties, because they took their share of the first choice: they chose to be subservient and to be subdued.

As for the human being: one says, "There is no god in existence; the world was created this way by its own nature." Another says, "Rather, there are many gods, because the world has many interests and things that one god cannot manage": that is, a god for the heaven, a god for the earth, a god for the sun, and so on.

So this is an opinion: in the world there are many things such that, in his view, one god cannot handle them. We say to him: you have taken God's power from your own individual power. No. Take it from the One of whom ﴿there is nothing like Him﴾ (Surah al-Shura, 11), because divine power does not deal with things as you do, requiring effort and work. Rather, with respect to Him, the Exalted, all of this is accomplished by the word "Be" (kun): He says "Be," and the matter is finished.

We marvel at the contradiction of these people. One says that the universe was created as it is, of itself, without a god. Another says that there are multiple gods. We say to them: you are contradicting yourselves. So come to the religion of God, and to the moderation (al-wasatiyya) that affirms one God, which neither denies divinity nor affirms plurality.

If you think that the wheel of the universe requires many machines to run it, know that God, the Exalted, does not directly undertake the management of the universe through treatment and effort, doing this and doing that as human beings carry out their works. Rather, He does it by "Be" (kun). For this reason, the Blessed and Exalted says in the hadith qudsi (a saying of the Prophet ﷺ in which God speaks in the first person, though not part of the Qur'an):

"O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the living of you and the dead of you, and your moist and your dry, were all gathered in one place, and every one of you asked, and I gave each asker what he asked, that would not diminish My dominion any more than if one of you passed by the sea and dipped a needle in it and then lifted it out. That is because I am Generous and Glorious. I do what I will; My giving is speech, and My punishment is speech. When I desire a thing, My command is only that I say to it, 'Be,' and it is."

So, O you who worry that the One God will grow weary of managing the universe in all its aspects: raise the concept of divinity above the likeness of human beings, because God, the Exalted, does not exercise His sovereignty through treatment in the universe, but exercises it through the word "Be." Therefore, one God is sufficient. Since we have accepted one God, beware of saying that the gods are many. If the Blessed and Exalted negated two gods, then negating more than that is more fitting, and two is the least form of plurality.

The meaning of (ilahayn) (إلهين), "two gods," is two worshipped beings, so each would have commands and prohibitions. Commands and prohibitions require obedience, and the universe requires management. Which of the two gods manages the affairs of the universe? Or does it need an assistant? If it needs an assistant, that is a deficiency in it, and it is not fit to be a god.

Likewise, if each of them specialized in a certain task, this one for such-and-such and that one for such-and-such, then one of them has become incapable of what the other does. Then which aspect of life would be the dominant one? It is well known that the aspects of life are shared and interwoven.

For this reason, the Blessed and Exalted says:

﴿Had there been with Him any other god, each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overpowered others.﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun, 91)

And He said: ﴿Had there been within them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined.﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 22)

What then of the situation if the first wants a thing and the other wants that thing not to be? If the thing comes to be, it is a weakness in the second; and if it does not come to be, it is a weakness in the first. So the strength of one of them is a weakness in the other.

In His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah has said, "Do not take two gods; He is but one God"﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 51), we notice an eloquent admonition. It is as though He, glorified is He, when He calls us to His tawhid (oneness), says to us: "Give yourselves rest through monotheism." The Exalted has clarified this rest in His saying:

﴿Allah presents an example: a man in whom are partners disputing with one another, and a man belonging entirely to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah! But most of them do not know.﴾ (Surah al-Zumar, 29)

That is: a man who belongs purely to one master, and a man whose masters are many, who are disagreeing partners. If one pleases this one, he angers that one; if one of them needs him, the other disputes him. He is always weary and burdened. As for the slave of one master, the ease in his condition is not hidden.

So in His command to worship Him alone there is rest for us. It is as though He, glorified is He, says: "You have one direction that suffices for all directions, and that guarantees you that approval is one and that displeasure is one." Therefore, His seeking of this rest for us, glorified is He, came before He asked it of us, for He testified to it for His own Essence, the Exalted, saying:

﴿Allah testifies that there is no deity except Him.﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 18)

If an objector says: "How can He testify for His own Essence?" We say: yes, He testifies for His Essence, glorified is He, because there is no one other than Him. No one is with Him. So the testimony of the Essence for the Essence here is something natural. It is as though He says: "There is no one but Me. And if there were another god besides Me, let him show himself and make his existence clear."

"I am God. I created the universe, I took it, and I did such-and-such. Either I am truthful in what I said, and the matter is ended, or I am not truthful, and there is another god who created it. Then where is he? Why does he not oppose me?" This has not happened: no one has disputed God in His creation. When a claim comes without any contender or opponent, it is accepted from its claimant.

If someone says: "Perhaps the other gods did not know that someone had taken divinity from them," then if that is the case, they are not fit for divinity, because they lack awareness. And if they knew and did not oppose, then they are cowards who do not deserve this station.

By His testimony for His own Essence that there is no god but Him, He proceeded to create creation, because since He knows that there is no god other than Him, when He says "Be," He is certain that it will be.

For this reason, at the moment God issues an unseen judgment, He says: "I have decreed this judgment, although you are free to do or not do. But I have decreed that you will not do it. And since I have decreed that you will not do it, though you have the ability to do it, yet you did not do it, this is proof that there is no god other than Me to help you to do it."

Then the angels bore witness by testimony of the Essence, and those of knowledge bore witness by inference, as the Exalted said:

﴿Allah testifies that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge.﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 18)

Here we pause at His saying: ﴿two gods﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 51). We have the number and we have the counted thing. If we say, for example, "I met three men," the word "three" indicates the number, and the word "men" indicates the kind of the counted thing. This is the case with all numbers except the singular and the dual. The word of each of these two indicates both the number and the counted thing together.

For example, if you say "ilah" (إله), "god," it indicates unity and it indicates the kind. Likewise "ilahayn" (إلهين), "two gods," indicates the dual and the kind of the counted thing.

For this reason, it would have sufficed in the noble verse for Him to say: "Do not take two gods," since it indicates the number and the counted thing together. But the Blessed and Exalted intended this as an emphasis of the doctrinal matter because of its importance.

One of the methods of the Arabs, when they wish to emphasize speech, is to bring after it the intended meaning. They say: "So-and-so is handsome, very handsome," "So-and-so is good, very good," "So-and-so is a devil, a devil indeed," intending to emphasize the attribute. Likewise, in His saying "ilahayn" (إلهين), divinity is established by the dual alone, and to emphasize this doctrinal question, because it is the most significant question for a human being, the question of the summit, He said: ﴿two gods, two﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 51).

Likewise in His saying: ﴿He is only one God﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 51), He brought the word "one" (wahid, واحد) to emphasize the oneness of God, the Exalted. In the verse there is another point to be considered: the speech here is in the third person (the absent form):

﴿He is only one God﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 51). The grammatical expectation here would have been to say: "So fear Him alone" (fa-iyyahu fa-arhabun, فإياه فارهبون). But behind the shift in the discourse from the third person to direct address by the speaker, He said:

﴿So fear Me alone﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 51). This has a wisdom and a rhetorical point. After He had affirmed divinity by His saying ﴿He is only one God﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 51), it was fitting that He confront them with His own Essence, because since the matter is one of awe, awe of the speaker is better than awe of the absent one. It is as though the context says: "Here He is, glorified is He, before you, and this is more conducive to awe."

Likewise in the Opening of the Book we read: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Sovereign of the Day of Recompense.﴾ (Surah al-Fatiha, 2–4). He did not say "Him we worship" in continuation of the third person, but shifted to the pronoun of address, saying: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.﴾ (Surah al-Fatiha, 5). That is because the servant, after calling to mind the attribute of majesty and greatness, becomes worthy of confrontation and of direct address with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

So His saying ﴿So fear Me alone﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 51) comes after the servant has called to mind the greatness of his Lord, acknowledged His oneness, and known that He is one God, not two gods. One says, "We will punish him," and the other says, "No."

The matter is not so. Rather, one God holds in His hand the power to punish and the power to pardon. So the context here fittingly confronts them, saying:

﴿So fear Me alone﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 51).

Here we have the particle al- (اللام), "to/for." It may be the lam of possession, as in the verse, and as in: "The wealth is for Zayd." It may also be the lam of specification when it is attached to what does not possess, as when we say: "The bridle is for the horse," and "The key is for the door." The horse does not own the bridle, and the door does not own the key. This is the lam of specification.

Al-Haqq (the Truth), glory be to Him, says here:

﴿And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ (Surat an-Nahl, 52)

Elsewhere He says:

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.﴾ (Surat Yunus, 68)

Likewise:

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him.﴾ (Surat al-Hashr, 24)

And once He says:

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah.﴾ (Surat al-Jumu'ah, 1)

When the lam (the lam of possession, al-lam lil-milkiyyah) indicates ownership, the owned thing may differ. In His saying:

﴿And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾

it means the common ground that exists in both, i.e., the things that exist in the heaven and in the earth. As for His saying:

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾

it means the things that exist in the heaven and not on the earth, and the things that exist on the earth and not in the heaven. That is, what is specific to the heaven and what is specific to the earth. This is what they call istiab al-milkiyyah (the comprehensiveness of ownership).

Since He, glory be to Him, owns whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, no one other than Him has independent ownership. And since no one other than Him has independent ownership, it follows that no one has an essential existence (dhatiyyat wujud), because his first existence is granted to him as a gift, and whatever sustains the subsistence of his existence is also granted to him. Therefore they say: whoever wishes to contend with Him in divinity (al-uluhiyyah) must have an essential existence, and this belongs to Allah alone, exalted is He.

Let us illustrate this with the example of a young child who defies his father while he is still dependent on him. The father says to him: "Wait until you grow up and become independent in your affairs." When the child matures, reaches adulthood, and begins to earn, he becomes able to rely on himself and to be free of his father.

So we say to whoever contends with Him in divinity: "You are not able, because your existence is a gift, and the subsistence of your existence is a gift. Everything can be taken from you." This is why the Almighty, glory be to Him, draws our attention to this matter in His saying:

﴿No! Indeed, mankind does transgress, when he sees himself self-sufficient.﴾ (Surat al-'Alaq, 6–7)

This one who sees himself as self-sufficient, free of others from his own point of view, has he truly become self-sufficient? No. He has not become self-sufficient, as is evident from the fact that he cannot even keep what he owns.

His saying, glory be to Him:

﴿And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ (Surat an-Nahl, 52)

— He to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and by whom their existence subsists through His self-subsistence (al-qayyumiyyah). He, glory be to Him, reassures you and says: "I am al-Qayyum," meaning: the one who stands over your affairs. He is not merely "qa'im" (standing) but "qayyum," with intensification in the act. Since He, glory be to Him, is the one who stands over your affairs, bringing you into existence from nothing and sustaining you from nothing, it follows that your obedience must be to Him, not to anyone else.

In proverbs they say: "Whoever eats my morsel listens to my word." So if you are dependent for your existence, your existence is from Allah, your sustenance is from Allah, and the preservation of the foundations of your life is from Allah. Therefore He, the Exalted, said:

﴿And His is the religion, constant.﴾ (Surat an-Nahl, 52)

That is, this is a consequence: since whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, His is the religion, constant, meaning His is obedience and submission, lasting and continuous. The dominion of Allah is enduring, and He does not hand over His dominion to anyone, and the hand of Allah is ever over His dominion. Since the matter is thus, the Almighty asks them:

﴿Then, other than Allah, would you fear?﴾ (Surat an-Nahl, 52)

The hamzah here is interrogative, for rebuke and denunciation. It is not permissible for you to fear other than Allah, because that is a folly unbecoming of you. You already know that to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Him belongs constant obedience and continuous submission, and by Him the heavens and the earth were established, and from Him comes bringing into existence from nothing and sustaining from nothing.

Therefore, it is folly to fear other than Him, when He is more deserving of being feared. If you fear other than Him, that is a foolish conduct that leads to ruin and destruction, if you are deceived into thinking that Allah has bestowed upon you blessings that cannot be counted or enumerated.

Among the favours of God is that He guarantees for His servants the soundness of their faculties and of what surrounds them. For if the intellect, for example, is sound, the matters connected to it are sound and correct: order is sound, conduct is sound, and the economy is sound. And this is a blessing.

Blessing is for the heart and blessing is for the body. For the body there is material enjoyment, and for the heart there is immaterial enjoyment. Among the most important immaterial enjoyments that give rest to the body is that a person has a religion that guides him, that he has a Lord who is able and whom nothing can overpower. If the world becomes narrow for him and the means become narrow for him, then he has a Lord to whom he turns, who relieves him and suffices him. This is true rest.

The Real, glorified and exalted is He, has guaranteed us the soundness of the body through what He has placed in the universe of the foundations of life, in His saying: ﴿And He determined in it its sustenance﴾ (Surat Fussilat). That is: be reassured about this matter. God, glorified is He, does not want from you anything except that you employ your intellects, which were created by God, to reflect on the matter created by God, and that you act upon it with the energy created by God in your limbs. You will find everything made easy for you. God, exalted is He, did not intend for you to create provision; rather, He intended that you employ the intellect and interact with the gifts of the universe.

But how does a person interact in life?

There are things in existence that God, glorified is He, created by His mercy and bounty, and they act for you even if you did not ask them to act. You do not ask the sun to rise upon you, nor the wind to blow upon you, and so on. And there are other things that act for you if you ask them and interact with them, like the earth: if you work it with your hand, plough it, plant it and irrigate it, it gives you what you want.

In this realm of interaction people differ in rank. They do not differ in what acts for them without any effort on their part. Rather, the elevation and differentiation of people occurs through the things that respond to them if they act. As for the others, they act for all people: the sun, the air and the water are for everyone, for the believer and the disbeliever, in any place.

So, man advances through the things that God created for him. If he engages with them, they engage with him; and if he is lazy and slack, they give him nothing and he benefits nothing from them. Therefore someone may say: the disbeliever has such-and-such and owns such-and-such, and yet he is a disbeliever. He marvels at the decree that gave this man and deprived the believing monotheist of it.

We say to him: Yes, he took what he took, because he shares with you in what acts for you even if you do not ask, and he additionally works, toils and engages with the universe and with what God has given him of foundations and energy, so the universe engages with him and gives to him, while you sit with no determination.

Likewise, the ascent of man may reach a higher level, so that he makes the thing that acts for him without his asking it, that is, the thing subjected to him, act for him, as we see in what science has reached, such as the use of solar energy to heat water. This energy is subjected to us without effort on our part, but the advancement and ambition of man brought him to this elevation. And all of these are blessings from God.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 54:

Among people there are those who, when Allah touches them with some harm, or when some calamity befalls them, humble themselves, cry out, turn to Allah and call upon Him. Sometimes their tears flow, and they begin to pray and say: "O so-and-so, pray to Allah for me, for such-and-such..." Then when Allah removes their harm from them, they revert to their old ways once more. For this reason, the Exalted says in another verse:

﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, whether lying on his side, sitting, or standing. But when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as if he had never called upon Us regarding the harm that touched him.﴾ (Surah Yunus, 12)

Among the subtleties of the Qur'anic expression here is that He says:

﴿Then when He relieves you of the harm, behold, a party of you associates others with their Lord.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 54) That is: a group of you, not all of you. As for the rest, they may remain steadfast upon the truth and take a lesson from what has befallen them, so they do not revert. So people differ in this matter: one humbles himself and turns to Allah because of a single harm that struck him, another turns to Allah because of two harms, and so on.

We have witnessed, in the events that have passed over our country, great events that turned the most prominent of people toward Allah. We saw those who did not know the way to the mosque praying, and those who had not considered performing the Hajj to the House of Allah hastening to it, circumambulating it, and weeping there at the Multazam. Nothing brought them to Allah and turned them toward Him, Glorified is He, except the events that passed over them. Are not these events, these crises and these calamities, good for them? Indeed, they are good.

Also, a person may be afflicted with an illness that strikes him, and it may persist for him. So he goes to the doctors, calls upon Allah, turns to Him, asks people to pray for his recovery, and does such-and-such. Then when Allah removes the illness from him and grants him recovery, he says: "I chose the skilled doctor, the beneficial doctor, and I did this and that..." Glory be to Allah!

Why do you not leave the matter to Allah, and spare yourself this procedure? In His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Then when He relieves the harm from you, behold, a party of you associates others with their Lord.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 54) there is a social safety valve in the universe. It says to people: Beware lest you hold back from others when you extend a kindness to them and they deny it. Beware lest you cease doing good to others, because this denial of kindness has been done by those above you; they have done it with Allah, Glorified is He. So let their denial of kindness not discourage you from doing it; rather, hold fast to it so that you may be among its people.

Blessed and Exalted is the Truth, who sets before us an example of denying kindness in the story of our master Musa, peace be upon him:

﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Musa, but Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of Allah.﴾ (Surah al-Ahzab, 69) His people accused him and sat saying false and slanderous things about him. Musa said: "O Lord, I ask You that it not be said of me what is not in me..." Allah, the Exalted, said to Musa: "I did not do that for Myself, so how would I do it for you?"

And why did the Truth, Glorified is He, not do it for Himself? He did not do it for Himself so that He might give us an example of bearing this denial. Allah created the creation, provided for them and encompassed them, yet they disbelieved in Him; and despite that, the Truth, Glorified is He, remains the Creator, the Provider, the All-Encompassing toward them.

Thus, in the verse there is regulation and security for society, so that the disease of abstaining from doing good does not spread within it. And the saying of the Truth, Glorified is He: ﴿behold, a party of you associates others with their Lord﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 54) includes those among the believers who deny kindness, and among the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 55:

Meaning: those who take pride (mustaʿzimīn), like Qarun, who said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I possess﴾ (Surah al-Qasas 28:78). He takes it as the result of his own effort and work. Similar to this is one who is told: "Praise be to God, who granted you success in the examination," and he replies: "I was diligent. I studied and stayed up late." Yes, you studied, but others also studied, strove and exerted themselves, yet one of them fell ill on the night of the examination and it laid him low, and perhaps you would have been like him. This is the tone of one who denies grace and is arrogant toward the One who bestowed the blessing, glory be to Him.

As for His saying: ﴿so that they may disbelieve﴾ (Surah al-Nahl 16:55): did they do that so that they would disbelieve, making the lam (ل) one of causation (taʿlil)? No. Rather, they said: the lam here is the lam of consequence (lam al-ʿāqibah, the lam indicating the outcome). Its meaning is that you may do something not for a reason, but the thing happens this way, and it was not in your mind at all; it simply came about in this manner. An example of this lam in His saying, in the story of Musa and Fir'awn: ﴿Then the family of Fir'awn picked him up, so that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ (Surah al-Qasas 28:8). When Fir'awn took Musa out of the river, adopted him and raised him, did he adopt him so that he would become his enemy? No. Rather, this was the outcome, so that God, glory be to Him, might demonstrate that they were heedless, and that God came between their hearts and what they wished. So the matter was not intended: he took him in and raised him at the very time when he was killing the children. Did it not occur to you that someone feared for him, and so cast him into the river?!

Therefore the Exalted says: ﴿And know that God comes between a man and his heart﴾ (Surah al-Anfal 8:24).

Likewise the mother of Musa: ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Musa: suckle him, and if you fear for him, cast him into the river﴾ (Surah al-Qasas 28:7). How can this statement be accepted? And how could a mother throw her child into the river if she feared for him?! How could that happen?! But God came between the mother of Musa and her heart, so the fear for him departed, the tenderness departed, and compassion departed. She did not deny the command addressed to her, and she believed that her infant's deliverance lay in this, so she cast him.

As for His saying: ﴿So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know﴾ (Surah al-Nahl 16:55): that is, disbelieve in the blessings We have given you, and in the harm We have removed from you, and enjoy yourselves in this world; for I have not made the world a place of recompense, the recompense is only in the Hereafter.

The word "enjoy yourselves" (tamatta'ū) here indicates that God, exalted is He, may continue His blessings even upon one who disbelieves in His blessing; otherwise, if He withheld His blessings from them, there would be no enjoyment. He, exalted, says: ﴿for you will soon know﴾ (Surah al-Nahl 16:55), that is, you will soon see the result of your deeds, and in this is a threat and a warning.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 56:

That is: those who disbelieve in Allah, take idols and partners, and assign to them a share. And the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He:

﴿...they know not.﴾ [16:56] (Surat an-Nahl).

What is knowledge?

Knowledge is that you know a proposition, and this proposition is true, meaning it corresponds to reality, and you are able to prove it. If any one of these is lacking, it is not knowledge. These people, when they assigned a share to the idols, brought forth things that have no existence in reality or in knowledge, and that are not facts. Do the idols have any existence? Is there any proof for them?

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿They are but names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority.﴾ [53:23] (Surat an-Najm). These idols have no real existence. In another verse, the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He has created of crops and livestock, and they say, "This is for Allah," by their claim, and "This is for our partners." But what is for their partners does not reach Allah, while what is for Allah reaches their partners. Evil is what they judge.﴾ [6:136] (Surat al-An'am).

Even when they assigned a share to the idols, they made it from what Allah had provided them. Did you not assign the idols' share from what the idols give you, and Allah's share from what Allah has provided you? So this is your acknowledgment of the impotence of your idols, and that you took Allah's provision and assigned it to your idols.

This is evidence that the idols give you nothing, and it is a testimony from you against them. Did the idols know of this? So: ﴿for that which they know not⦆ [16:56], meaning: for the idols, because they have no real existence, while they take what We have provided them and assign it to their idols. Then the Blessed and Exalted says: ﴿By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to fabricate.﴾ [16:56].

The "ta" here in (tallah) is for oath, meaning: "By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you fabricated concerning the matter of the idols." Al-iftira' (fabrication) is deliberate lying.

Whenever you hear the word (Subhanahu) [Glorified is He], know that it is a declaration of God's transcendence above whatever is unfitting. Here it is a declaration of God, glorified and exalted, above what was previously attributed to Him, namely the ascription of daughters to Him. Exalted is God far above that, to a great height. That is, He is glorified above having daughters.

Can He then have male offspring? They ascribed daughters to God, and for themselves they took the males. The Qur'an speaks of this division: ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female? That, then, is an unjust division﴾ (Surah an-Najm, 21-22). That is, unjust (ḍayzā), not made equitable. It would be as if to say: I have a son and you have a son, I have a daughter and you have a daughter. Instead, you assign to God what you dislike, namely daughters, and assign to yourselves what you love.

Therefore, their ascribing daughters to God carried two defects:

The first: they attributed offspring to God, and even if it were male, it would be a baseless fabrication from which God is exempt.

The second: they chose, in their own view, the most despicable kind. No one can say that daughters are the most despicable kind, and why? Because through daughters the species continues. For this reason al-'Abbas said: "If God heard what people say about people, there would be no people left." That is, if God answered people's desire that they not have daughters, and granted it by not giving them any, what would happen? The line of descent would be cut off. So this is a foolish demand, for it is the daughter who bears the son, and through her the species endures and the lineage continues.

As for His words, ﴿Glorified is He... (57)﴾ (Surah an-Nahl), that is, a declaration that He should not have a son, and a declaration that He is exempt from having the more despicable of the two kinds in their view and custom. The Qur'an speaks of them in the following verse:

﴿When one of them is given news of a female, his face darkens and he is filled with suppressed grief. He hides himself from the people because of the evil of what he has been given news of﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 58-59). Therefore, when the Truth, blessed and exalted, speaks to us of procreation, He says:

﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows females on whom He wills, and bestows males on whom He wills. Or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes whom He wills barren﴾ (Surah ash-Shura, 49-50).

The Truth, glorified be He, began with females. Then He gave us this pattern of creation: females, males, males and females, and barrenness. So God's gifts are of four kinds, and from here barrenness too is a gift from God, for a wisdom He intended. But people do not take barrenness as a gift; they take it as a punishment and wrath.

Why? Why do you take it as a curse and a trial? Perhaps He would have granted you a child who turns out disobedient, like the child who becomes a trial to his parents, calling them to disbelief.

Yet if the barren person were content with what God has apportioned to him, regarded it as a gift, and accepted it, he would see every child in society as his own, without the hardship of carrying, birthing, and raising. All the children around him would look to him as their own, and God would turn their hearts toward him as though he were their father. It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted, were saying to him: since you have been content with God's gift to you in barrenness, I will make every child a child of yours.

The Truth, glorified be He, concludes the verse with: ﴿And for them is what they desire (57)﴾ (Surah an-Nahl), that is, males. For a son is a source of honor to his father, benefiting him in war and combat and in increasing his numbers, and so on. A daughter, by contrast, becomes a burden upon him. For this reason God says after this: ﴿And when one of them is given news of a female...﴾.

We know that good news is meant to bring joy, so they should have received it as glad tidings. But they received it as people who resent and hate what they were given the good news of; you see the face of one of them—

﴿Darkened…﴾ (Surah An-Nahl 16:58). The blackening of the face means its contraction from rage. Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿while he is suppressing [his grief]﴾ (Surah An-Nahl 16:58).

Al-kazm (كظم) means: holding in a thing. Therefore He, exalted is He, says in another verse: ﴿those who restrain their anger﴾ (Surah Ali 'Imran 3:134).

It is derived from the phrase kazm al-qirba (كظم القربة), when a water-skin is filled with water and then one kazama it, meaning ties it shut, so you see it full, as if it is about to burst. Likewise is the angry person: his veins swell, blood rushes to his face, and congestion occurs in him, so he is makhzum (مكظوم), restrained from bursting.

The Qur'an, 16:59: "He hides himself from the people because of the evil of that whereof he has been given tidings."

That is, he conceals himself from his people for fear that it will be said, "He has begotten a daughter."

﴿from the evil of that whereof he has been given tidings﴾ (16:59).

We notice the repetition of the tidings in this verse as well, as though God, glorified and exalted is He, is softening his heart towards her and calling him to gentleness with her.

He is hesitant, not knowing what to do. Therefore God, exalted is He, says:

﴿Shall he keep it in humiliation, or bury it in the dust?﴾ (16:59). That is, what will he do with what has been born to him? Will he keep it in humiliation, that is, in disgrace and abasement, or will he bury it in the dust, that is, bury it alive in it?

﴿Certainly evil is what they judge﴾ (16:59). That is, evil is what they judge in both situations: the situation of keeping her in humiliation and disgrace, or the situation of burying her in the dust. Both are evil. Some of these people, when a daughter was born to them, hated her; if he kept her, he kept her in a state in which she was humiliated in his sight, despised and abased, though she was a helpless one who had committed no sin.

For this reason, the Arab woman who lived through these events understood what we came to know only recently, when the modern world discovered that the matter of begetting a son or a daughter rests with the man and not with the woman. Abu Hamzah often left his wife and became angry with her, because she bore only daughters. So what did this Arab woman whom her husband had abandoned say? She said:

"Why does Abu Hamzah not come to us angry?
Are we not the ones who bear sons?
By God, that is not in our hands:
we are like the earth for those who sow in us,
we give them the like of what they gave."

The Truthful and Exalted God, when He desires balance in the universe, brings about this balance through the requirements of the human soul. Among its requirements is that a person should have standing and should have honour. But man errs in constructing this standing and honour, and he thinks he is able to make what he wishes by his means alone.

Were he to know that the construction of standing and honour is by something beyond his means, by something created by God, by a measure created by God, were he to know this truth, he would approach the matter from its proper door.

For honour does not lie in what you beget. Honour here belongs to God, to His Messenger and to the believers. Take pride here in the band of faith; take pride in being in a believing, mutually supportive environment, where if injustice befalls you, everyone rallies to you.

Do not take pride in lineage and offspring, for a son may come out undutiful, who does not help his parents in hardship nor assist them in need. That is because you have resorted to tribalism of blood, and blood-tribalism may fail; but tribalism of creed, tribalism of faith and religion does not.

Let us take an example of this: what happened between the Ansar and the Muhajirun, of mutual support and cooperation that surpassed anything humans could imagine, and there was nothing between them but the bond of creed and the tribalism of faith. What happened between these exceptional men?

We find that faith-based solidarity made a man sacrifice the most precious thing he begrudges to others. Imagine in this situation that the Ansar, by reason of the blessings they possessed, were to share them with their Muhajir brothers: whoever had a mount or a dwelling, for example, would say to his Muhajir brother, "Please, ride this mount, or dwell in this house." All of this is a natural matter.

But as for the bounty of women, human nature is stamped with the trait that a person does not like his blessing in this regard to pass over to another. Yet look at faith, and what it did to souls! The Ansari would say to the Muhajir, "Look at my wives: whichever pleases you, I will divorce her so that you may marry her." What moved him to this was not the tribalism of blood or the tribalism of sex, but the tribalism of certainty and faith.

For this reason all tribalisms vanish in the story of Noah, peace be upon him, and his disbelieving son, when Noah, peace be upon him, called to him:

﴿My son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers.﴾ (11:42). He said, "I will betake myself to a mountain that will protect me from the water." He said, "There is no protector today from the command of God, except for him on whom He has mercy..." (11:43).

Noah clings to his son and is most eager for his salvation, saying:

﴿My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is true...﴾ (11:45).

Then comes the decisive word on this matter: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family; indeed, he is one whose conduct is other than righteous. So do not ask Me for that of which you have no knowledge. I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾ (11:46).

So then: this son is not of your family, because kinship here is kinship of deeds, not kinship of blood and lineage. It is true that a person loves honour and seeks it for himself, but you must consider how true honour is attained and what its causes are.

Take honour through God, through His Messenger, and through the environment of faith, and all children become your children, because they are with you in your certainty of God and your faith in Him, glorified is He. But if you take honour in your own way, seeking honour in the male child, who knows whether you will find in him honour, support and multiplicity?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 60:

His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the evil description. And for Allah is the highest description.﴾ (Surat an-Nahl)

"Mathal al-su'" (evil description): the attribute of evil, i.e., the vile and wicked attributes, such as disbelief, denial and rejection, blindness of insight, and other evil attributes.

Why is it that those who do not believe in the Hereafter have an evil description? Because the equation they worked out is a mistaken equation. The one who does not believe in the Hereafter has shortened his lifespan, so the life of this world is short in his estimation. We have said: beware of measuring the world by its own lifespan; rather, measure the world by your own lifespan. The lifespan of the world is the period of your own stay in it. Indeed, it remains after you for others, and you have no share in it after the end of your lifetime.

So then: the lifespan of the world is your lifespan in it. Your lifespan: a month, a year, ten years, a hundred. This is the true lifespan of the world, in relation to you yourself.

Nevertheless, however long the lifespan of the world may be, it is destined to vanish. Whoever does not believe in Allah and does not believe in the Hereafter has chosen the losing path, because he cannot guarantee that he will live in this world even to the average lifespan. Suppose you lived in this world until the average lifespan, or even until the most decrepit old age. Suppose you enjoyed your worldly life with every kind of sin: what will the end be? That you will lose all of this to death.

So the state of this person is like the state of the one who believes in Allah and believes in the Hereafter. We say to the one who does not believe in the Hereafter: your worldly life is uncertain; you may live in it, or death may overtake you suddenly. Even whoever lives to the average lifespan, the end is still vanishing.

As for the enjoyments you have obtained in your worldly life, you took them according to the measure of your own capacities. So you have taken a limited, uncertain transaction, and you have abandoned an unlimited, certain transaction. Is this transaction not a losing one?

As for the one who believes in the Hereafter, his transaction has profited, since he has chosen an extended life in which he finds enjoyment according to the capacities of the Bestower, glorified and exalted be He.

﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the evil description﴾, i.e., the attribute is extremely evil, because they are certainly losers. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And for Allah is the highest description﴾, i.e., Allah has the highest attribute. It is as if the verse says to you: leave the attribute of evil and take the highest attribute, in which you find enjoyment according to the capacities of the Truth, glorified and exalted be He.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted be He, concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾.

﴿Al-'Aziz﴾ (the Mighty): the One who is not overcome in His affair. If it is said that there may exist someone who is not overcome in his affair, yes; but He, glorified be He, is ﴿Mighty, Wise﴾, who employs subjugation and domination with wisdom.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 61:

The saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿And if Allah were to take mankind to task...﴾ [16:61] (Surat an-Nahl)

Here we have al-akhdh (seizing) and al-mu'akhadhah (taking to account). Al-akhdh is obtaining a thing and encompassing it. This indicates that the one who seizes has the ability to hold firmly, either by himself or through another. For example, you can carry a pebble, but you cannot carry a large rock; and something may be simple yet bound to something else and held by it, so it draws strength from it.

So the meaning of akhdh is that you contain a thing, and your containing it means that you are stronger than its holding itself together, or than another's holding onto it. Seizing may also occur without any sin.

As for al-mu'akhadhah, it means: he takes from you, so you take from him. From it is one of us saying to his brother, "La mu'akhadhah" (no blame), in some situation. The meaning is: I did something for which I deserve requital and reproach, so I say: "Do not hold me to account; I did not intend it."

Therefore, the Truth, blessed and exalted, says here: ﴿And if Allah were to take mankind to task...﴾ [16:61]

He did not say: "if Allah were to seize mankind." In another verse He, exalted is He, says:

﴿And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizing is painful and severe.﴾ [11:102] (Surat Hud)

Why did Allah seize them? He seized them because they took from Him His rights to be the One God, and they denied it; and His rights in legislating what is good, and they denied those too. The Truth, glorified is He, shows that this taking to account, if it were to occur, would be caused by the people themselves. So He, glorified is He, says: ﴿for their wrongdoing﴾ [16:61].

The first of the wrongdoing is that they denied the Oneness (of Allah). He, exalted is He, says:

﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a tremendous wrong﴾ [31:13] (Surat Luqman). So it is as though they took from Allah His right of Oneness, and they took from the Messenger ﷺ, so they said, "A liar," and they took from the Book and said, "Clear magic." All of this is wrongdoing.

So if the Truth, blessed and exalted, were to take them to account for what they took, taking something for something, if He treated them in this manner, He would not leave upon its back any creature. Therefore we find in verses of supplication:

﴿Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or err...﴾ [2:286] (Surat al-Baqarah), meaning: we have taken much from You, O Lord, by what has occurred from us of excess and shortcoming and action contrary to the requirement of Your command, so do not hold us accountable for what has come from us. So if Allah were to take mankind to account for what they committed of wrongdoing... ﴿He would not leave upon it any creature﴾ [16:61].

One may say: Allah, mighty and majestic, will take mankind to account for their wrongdoing, so what is the sin of the animal? What did it do? We say: because the animal was created for their sake and subjected to them, and it is one of Allah's blessings upon them. So the matter is not then a punishment of the animal, but of the one who benefits from it; and it may be intended as general for all creation.

If Allah does not take mankind to account for their wrongdoing in this world, does He leave them thus? No, rather:

﴿But He delays them until a specified term...﴾ [16:61]. This term is the ending of the world and the establishment of the Hereafter, even if they do not believe in the Hereafter, for Allah, exalted is He, gives them respite in this world, as He says in another verse:

﴿And indeed, for those who wronged there is a punishment besides that...﴾ [52:47] (Surat at-Tur).

In this specified term there may be good for the truth. Many of the Companions used to enter battles, loving to kill so-and-so and so-and-so of the people of disbelief, then they were not able to do that and did not reach them, and they would grieve over that.

But the term of these people had not yet come, and in Allah's knowledge these disbelievers would believe, and their faith would benefit the Muslims. It is as though destiny was storing them: either they themselves would believe, or their offspring would believe.

Indeed, 'Amr ibn al-'As believed, and 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and others. Among those who were saved was Khalid ibn al-Walid, the drawn sword of Allah.

﴿So when their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it﴾ [16:61]. That is: when the end comes, it is not postponed. This is a reasonable matter. But how: "nor can they advance it"? When the term comes, how can they not advance it? The matter then seems impossible. How can it be that when the term comes it had come before that? This does not stand. But the meaning stands perfectly on the basis that:

﴿nor can they advance it﴾ [16:61] is not the answer to "when," rather the answer was completed at "an hour." So the meaning is: when their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour; and if it has not come, they cannot advance it. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 62:

His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And they assign to Allah what they dislike.. (62)﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

The fitting principle is that what is given for the sake of Allah must be of the best of what Allah has granted. So when you wish to give charity, give the best of what you have, or at least from the middling of what you have. But to give the basest and most worthless things, to give what you yourself dislike, like one who gives bread that is not good, or meat that has gone bad, or tattered clothing, this is to assign to Allah what they dislike.

In truth, if people trusted in Allah's recompense for what the servant gives, they would give their Lord the best of what they love. Why? Because that is a sign of your love for the Hereafter, and that you are of its people. You build it with what you love. As for the worldly person who loves the world, he gives the least of what he has, because the world in his view is more important than the Hereafter.

By this a person can measure himself: is he of the people of the Hereafter or of the people of this world, by what he gives to Allah, Mighty and Majestic?

His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And they assign to Allah what they dislike.. (62)﴾ (Surat an-Nahl), meaning: of what was mentioned in the preceding verses, their saying:

﴿For Allah are daughters.. (57)﴾ (Surat an-Nahl), and that the angels are daughters of Allah, and they made a kinship between Him and the jinn, besides their other sayings. They assigned daughters to Allah while they themselves dislike daughters. Therefore:

﴿And when one of them is given news of a female, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief (58)﴾ (Surat an-Nahl). The matter here is not merely assigning daughters to Allah; rather, any assigning by them is rejected. For if they had assigned to Allah what they love of males, it would not have been accepted from them either, because they assigned to Allah what He did not assign to Himself.

Thus those who said, "Uzair is the son of Allah," and those who said, "The Messiah is the son of Allah," are not accepted from them, because they assigned to Allah, glorified is He, what He did not assign to Himself. This is rejected, and that is rejected, because we do not assign to Allah except what Allah has assigned to Himself, glorified is He.

So we assign to Allah what we love of what Allah has permitted, as came in His saying:

﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love.. (92)﴾ (Surat Ali 'Imran), and His saying:

﴿And they give food, despite their love for it.. (8)﴾ (Surat al-Insan). For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, said to His Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers (81)﴾ (Surat az-Zukhruf). Had He had a son, I would have believed it; but the truth is that He has no son. So the matter is not in assigning to Allah what they dislike, but in assigning in general; for we are servants who draw near to Allah through worship, and the worshipper draws near to the worshipped by what the worshipped loves him to draw near by. So if Allah assigns something to Himself, it is upon the eye and the head (i.e., gladly accepted), as in His command that we spend from what we love and from the best of what we possess.

For this reason His saying:

﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love.. (92)﴾ (Surat Ali 'Imran) enjoins that the right of the poor be observed, and the necessity of making him as yourself, so that giving him the worst of what you have is not easy for you. When the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, wished that we draw near to Him through sacrifice and the slaughter of the offerings and sacrificial animals, He said:

﴿So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor (28)﴾ (Surat al-Hajj), because when you know that you will eat from them, you will choose the best of what you have. And His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And their tongues describe falsehood.. (62)﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

Falsehood (al-kadhib): a proposition uttered by the tongue that has no reality in existence, that is, a contradiction of the reality witnessed to by the heart. And why is the heart the witness to it?

They said: Because the statement may correspond to the actual reality, yet we still judge it to be false, as came in His saying:

﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars (1)﴾ (Surat al-Munafiqun). By Allah, is this proposition true or not? It is a true proposition: you are the Messenger of Allah, and their statement agreed with what Allah knows. So why did the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, testify that they are "liars"?

And in what are they liars?

They said: In reality they are truthful in their saying, "You are indeed the Messenger of Allah," but they lied in their testimony: ﴿We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.. (1)﴾ (Surat al-Munafiqun), because they do not truly bear witness; for testimony requires that the heart agree with and support the tongue, whereas this testimony from them is from the tongue alone, unsupported by the heart.

A person is liable to say truth at one time and falsehood at another, but these people, as soon as they say "We testify," are liars. This is the meaning of:

﴿Their tongues describe falsehood.. (62)﴾ (Surat an-Nahl), because when they say, for example: "Uzair is the son of Allah," "The Messiah is the son of Allah," "The angels are the daughters of Allah," all these are false propositions with no reality that agrees with what the tongue utters. Thus their tongues describe falsehood.

And if you wish to know a falsehood that does not correspond to reality, listen to it: as soon as it is said, you know it is false. Like what happened with Musaylima, who claimed prophethood: as soon as he said, "I am a prophet," we said, "Musaylima the liar."

And the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿That for them is the best.. (62)﴾ (Surat an-Nahl), meaning: the falsehood in their saying, "For them is the best." This is deception and wishful thinking about Allah without right. A similar statement occurs in Surat al-Kahf, in the story of the two gardens owners. He, exalted is He, says:

﴿And he entered his garden while he was wronging himself. He said, "I do not think that this will ever perish. (35) And I do not think the Hour will occur. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a destination." (36)﴾ (Surat al-Kahf). These are three false statements:

His saying: ﴿I do not think that this will ever perish (35)﴾ (Surat al-Kahf), this is the first. How many things have changed, and who guarantees you the continuance of what you are in? And the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says in another verse:

{Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the people of the garden, when they swore to harvest its fruit at dawn (17), and did not make exception (18). So there came upon it a visitation from your Lord while they were asleep (19), and it became like the black, barren night (20)} (Surat al-Qalam).

The second lie: ﴿And I do not think the Hour will occur (36)﴾ (Surat al-Kahf), for he denied the Hour.

The third lie: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a destination (36)﴾ (Surat al-Kahf).

This is the evidence in the verse here: in it is deception and wishful thinking about Allah without right, like those who claimed that for them is the best, while they are not worthy of it. In another place the same statement appears:

﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless (49). And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, "This is for me, and I do not think the Hour will occur. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have with Him the best." (50)﴾ (Surat Fussilat). Thus is man by nature: he does not tire of seeking good, and whenever he reaches a rank in it, he wishes for something higher; if evil touches him he despairs, and if Allah removes it from him and shows him mercy, he says, "This is mine; I deserve it, I am worthy of it." Would that he had said, "This is a bounty and favor from Allah." Then after that he wishes upon Allah his desires, saying:

﴿Indeed I have with Him the best (50)﴾ (Surat Fussilat).

It is narrated that our master Dawud (peace be upon him), despite what Allah had given him of kingship and greatness, once climbed to the roof of his house, and Allah tested him with a swarm of golden locusts. When Dawud saw them, he began gathering them into his garment. His Lord said to him, "Did I not make you rich, O Dawud?" He said, "Yes, but I have no independence from Your bounty."

His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿Without doubt, for them is the Fire.. (62)﴾ (Surat an-Nahl). "La jaram" means: truly, for them is the Fire, because of what preceded from them in assigning to Allah what they dislike, and their tongues describing falsehood; these are deeds for which they deserve the Fire. The phrase "la jaram" is derived from "jarim," meaning "criminal," so the meaning is: there is no crime in punishing these people, because the punishment for a crime is not itself called a crime. So it has two meanings: either that for them the Fire is certain, or that there is no crime in their having the Fire as the recompense of their deeds.

﴿And that they are those who will be neglected (or: sent forward to the Fire) (62)﴾ (Surat an-Nahl). The word "mufarrituun" has several readings: mufarraṭūn, mufriṭūn, mufarriṭūn, mufarṭūn. All of them converge in meaning.

When we pray over a funeral, for example, if the deceased was a responsible adult, we say in supplication for him: "O Allah, forgive him, O Allah, have mercy on him... O Allah, if he was a doer of good, increase him in his good, and if he was a doer of evil, overlook his evil deeds." But if he was a child, not responsible, we say in supplication for him: "O Allah, make him a fareT (forerunner) and a treasure (dhukhr)." So what is the meaning of "fareT" here?

Its meaning: that the child be a forerunner for his parents and a precursor to them to Paradise.
