He goes before his parents and precedes them to Paradise, as if he goes ahead to prepare the way for them, so that Allah may forgive them. So the meaning of "mufarrituun" is: those sent ahead. But to the Fire.

We know that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, swears by whatever He wills, about whatever He wills; as for us, we swear only by Allah. And in the noble hadith: "Whoever is going to swear, let him swear by Allah or let him keep silent."

Here the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, swears by His own Being, glorified is He, as in: "Tallah" (by Allah), like "wallahi" and "billahi." Oaths have come to affirm the meaning; for this reason one of the righteous said: "Who has angered the Generous until He compelled Him to swear?!"

The Truth, glorified is He, may affirm an oath by His own Being, or an oath by some of His creation, and He may negate an oath while swearing, as in His saying:
﴿I swear by this city﴾ (Surat al-Balad), [the negation here is "la" preceding the verb "uqsimu"].

And His saying:
﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars, and indeed it is an oath, if you only knew, tremendous﴾ (Surat al-Waqi'ah).

The meaning of "la uqsimu" (I do not swear) is that this matter is so clear and evident that it does not need an oath; and had I been one who swears, I would have sworn by it, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And indeed it is an oath, if you only knew, tremendous﴾ (Surat al-Waqi'ah).

So then: the Truth, glorified is He, swears by His own Being to affirm the matter for us with emphasis. The affirmation of a matter in judgment in the courts, for example, is either by acknowledgment or by oath. So when you swear to him and take an oath, you have blocked the avenues of denial to him. The Truth, glorified is He, says:
﴿Indeed We sent [messengers] to nations before you…﴾ (Surat al-Nahl). That is: you are not unprecedented in being denied by your people; this is the nature of those who receive the call from Allah through the tongues of the messengers, because Allah does not send messengers except when corruption spreads and becomes general.

The meaning of the sending of messengers, then, is that there is no solution except that the heavens intervene; this is because man has innate inner safeguards within himself, namely his self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwamah) which blames him when he errs and corrects his conduct; it is a deterrent to him from within himself.

So when this soul becomes dulled and accustomed to error, society around it takes up this task: whoever is not deterred by his self-reproaching soul is deterred by the society around him. So when society too becomes corrupt, what then is the solution? The solution is that the heavens intervene to rescue these people.

So then: the heavens intervene by sending messengers when corruption becomes general throughout society; for this reason the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ), from its honor before its Lord, was told: "You are entrusted with the care of My method within yourselves, self-reproaching over your own souls, commanding the good and forbidding evil in others. Therefore I will not send another messenger among you, for you will carry out this task."

For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, said:
﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil…﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran).

He has entrusted the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ) to be a guardian of His method, either through the self-reproaching soul or through a society that enjoins good and forbids evil; and this is a great honor for this nation.

So then: the messenger comes when corruption becomes general. What is the meaning of corruption (fasad)? Corruption is that the interests of one group exist at the expense of another group. The people of corruption and those who profit from it, when a messenger comes to free people from their corruption, how do they receive him? Do they receive him with welcome? Certainly not; they must receive him with hatred and denial, and declare war upon him in defense of their interests.

The Truth, glorified is He, follows this with His saying:
﴿So Satan made their deeds appear good to them…﴾ (Surat al-Nahl). Here Satan intervenes and makes the deeds of the people of corruption appear good to them, and urges them to fight the messengers. "These who will end your authority will take what is in your hands of the enjoyments of this world; they will shake your positions and lower your standing among people… these will raise the base and the slaves above you."

Thus the people of corruption and oppression cling to their oppression, holding onto it with their back teeth, and they stand toward the messengers in a stance of hostility. So prepare yourself for this; you will meet from the masters nothing but denial, rejection, and warfare. Then He, exalted is He, says:

﴿So he is their ally today…﴾ (Surat al-Nahl): that is, in the Hereafter. Since Satan took them as allies in this world, made their deeds appear good, and incited them against the messengers, let him now be their ally, and let him defend them on the Day of Resurrection. The Noble Qur'an has presented this situation to us in His saying:
﴿Like Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, [Satan] says, "Indeed, I am free of you; indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ (Surat al-Hashr).

And in their dispute on the Day of Resurrection with Satan, they say to him: "You misled us and made [sin] appear good to us." What does he say? He says:
﴿And I had over you no authority except that I invited you and you responded to me. So do not blame me; but blame yourselves…﴾ (Surah Ibrahim). The authority here is either through a convincing argument, or through compulsion, domination, and force that imposes what it wants; Satan possesses none of that. He has no argument by which to persuade you to act, and no power by which to compel you to act while you are unwilling.

Thus Satan disputes with them and refutes their claims: he has no authority over you; rather, a mere suggestion led you into disobedience. In another verse the Truth, glorified is He, says:
﴿And [mention] when Satan made their deeds appear good to them and said, "No one among the people can overcome you today, and indeed I am your protector." But when the two groups sighted each other, he turned back on his heels and said, "Indeed, I am free of you; indeed, I see what you do not see; indeed, I fear Allah…"﴾ (Surat al-Anfal).

His saying:
﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾ (Surat al-Nahl): here the punishment is described as painful, severe, and destructive; Allah has described the punishment as painful, great, humiliating, and severe. Punishment is a feeling of pain and sensation of it, and scholars have concluded that all sensation resides in the skin; for this reason the Truth, glorified is He, said, to perpetuate the punishment for these people:
﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins that they may taste the punishment﴾ (Surat al-Nisa'). Thus the punishment continues with the continuation of the skins and their replacement.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 64:

"The Book" is the Noble Qur'an. And the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿That you may make clear to them that about which they differ.﴾ (Surah an-Nahl)

This is evidence that disagreement arose among the followers of the earlier messengers. What kind of disagreement is this, since they were followers of one prophet? What is its cause?

They said: The cause of this disagreement is what they call temporal authority (al-sultah al-zamaniyyah). To clarify the meaning of temporal authority, we give an example of someone who was, say, the shaykh of a Sufi order (tariqah). When he died, his sons disputed the succession after him. Each wanted it for himself, and began to gather around him a group of his father's followers. Had this succession been clear in their minds, this disagreement would not have occurred.

Likewise, temporal authority arose among the followers of the messengers, who began to write the documents (al-sukuk) and to mention what they liked and what they saw as correct from their own point of view. All of these had influence through what we call temporal authority.

So how could they leave Muhammad (ﷺ) to take this authority from them and deprive them of the dominion they were in? The Messenger (ﷺ) came to make things clear to them, that is, to return them to the path of truth and to the straight way.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And as guidance and mercy.﴾ (Surah an-Nahl). Guidance (al-huda) means showing the clear path to a beneficial goal. A path is not clear unless it is free of difficulties and obstacles, and free of fears as well. It is a clear, safe, easy path, and it is also short, bringing you to your goal by the shortest way.

The opposite of guidance is misguidance (al-dalal), which is that it misleads you: if you seek a path, it turns you toward something else, points you to other than it, or points you to a path full of fears and obstacles. As for mercy (al-rahmah), the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, described the Qur'an as mercy when He said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers.﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 82). How can the Qur'an be a healing? And how can it be a mercy?

Healing: when a disease afflicts us, our Lord, glorified is He, says: Treat your illness and cure your sicknesses with such-and-such, and refer the judgment to God. This is healing.

As for mercy: it is that the disease is prevented from coming back a second time, so that it becomes a protection that uproots the disease from its root so that it does not return.

This happens in the world of medicine as well. You may go to a doctor to treat you of a certain disease, such as blisters on the skin, for example. He is concerned only with what he sees on the surface, and prescribes for you something to treat these blisters. Then after that it returns to you again.

But the skilled and proficient physician does not look only at the surface; he seeks its cause within, and tries to uproot the causes of the disease from their roots, so that it does not return to you again.

Therefore, if we look at the story of Ayyub (Job), peace be upon him, and what God tested him with, we see in it a wonderful example of treating both the outside and the inside together. His Lord tested him with a affliction whose effect appeared clearly on his body. When He, glorified is He, permitted him to be healed, He said to him: ﴿Strike with your foot; this is a cool bath and a drink.﴾ (Surah Sad, 42).

(a cool bath): that is, it washes and removes what remains in you of the traces of this affliction.

(and a drink): that is, a drink that cures you of the causes of this affliction, so that it does not return.

The same applies to the treatment of society. The Noble Qur'an came while the world was full of great corruption and many diseases, which required a method to heal these diseases, and then we give them immunities that prevent these diseases from returning again.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿For a people who believe.﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 64). That is: this Qur'an contains guidance and mercy for those who believe in you and in your message, because the physician whom we have given as an example here does not treat every patient, but treats the one who trusts him, goes to him, and presents himself to him, so the physician examines him and learns his ailment.

Likewise, the Noble Qur'an is heard by the one who believes in it, so it becomes for him guidance and mercy, and leaves in his soul luminous illuminations that elevate him and raise him to the highest ranks. Whereas another hears it and understands nothing from it, and says, as the Noble Qur'an relates: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until when they leave your presence they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?"﴾ (Surah Muhammad, 16).

And He said: ﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing.﴾ (Surah Fussilat, 44). ﴿And as for those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them.﴾ (Surah Fussilat, 44). So the Qur'an is one, but the reception differs.

Al-Haqq tabaraka wa ta'ala, in this verse, moves us to a material, sensible sign that no one denies: the sending down of rain from the sky and the giving of life to dead land by this rain. This is to be a tangible proof of His power, and that He is trustworthy toward His creation.

It is as if He, glorified is He, were saying to them: If I give you such-and-such, and provide for you the material matter that shows My care for you, then when I send down to you a method (manhaj) that benefits you and sets your conditions right, believe in it.

This is a material, sensible proof that leads them to affirm the immaterial method (al-manhaj al-ma'nawi) which came through the hand of the Messenger (ﷺ), in His saying, may He be exalted:
﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers...﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 82).

And His saying: ﴿And Allah sends down water from the sky...﴾ (Surat al-Nahl, 65). This is a cosmic, sensible sign that no one denies. Then He says: ﴿and gives life thereby to the earth after its death﴾ (Surat al-Nahl, 65). The death of the earth means its state of being barren and desolate, with no crops and no vegetation in it, and this is destruction itself for them. So when the earth becomes barren, they look expectantly toward a cloud, a rain cloud, and await from it the rain that gives life to this dead earth, giving it life with plants and herbage after it had been lifeless and dead.

Had the water of the sky been withheld from the earth, they would have perished of hunger. So take from this sensible verse a proof of the truth of the immaterial verse, which is the method of God to you through His Messenger (ﷺ). Just as you trusted Me in the first, trust Me in the second. And His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who hear﴾ (Surat al-Nahl, 65). Although this sign is seen with the eye and not heard, the Qur'an says: ﴿for a people who hear﴾ (Surat al-Nahl, 65)... Why?

They said: Because Allah, glorified is He, brought this sign to draw their attention to the method that will come to them through the hand of the Messenger (ﷺ), and this method is heard from the Messenger who conveys the method of God.

An example of this is also His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then hear?﴾ (Surat al-Qasas, 71). Light is seen, not heard, but He said "Will you not then hear?" because He is speaking about the night, and the means of perception at night is hearing.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 66:

The universe that Allah Most High created contains multiple kinds of beings. The lowest of them is the inanimate (jamad), represented by the earth, the mountains, the waters and others. Then comes vegetation (nabat), then animals (hayawan), then humankind (insan).

In the previous verse, the Blessed and Most High gave us an example of the inanimate, which was stirred to life by rain, and He gave us vegetation. Here, this verse moves us to a higher kind, which is animals.

﴿And indeed in the cattle there is a lesson for you.. 66﴾ (Surah al-Nahl). What is meant by al-an'am (cattle) is the camels, cows, sheep and goats. They were mentioned in Surah al-An'am in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Eight pairs: of the sheep two, and of the goats two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you are truthful. 143 And of the camels two and of the cattle two.. 144﴾ (Surah al-An'am). These are the an'am.

As for His saying, Exalted is He, (la'ibrah, "a lesson"), al-'ibrah is the thing by which you take warning, and from which you extract what guides you to the power of the Wise Creator, Glorified is He. You take from these things evidence of the truthfulness of His method, Glorified is He, so that you affirm it.

Among the meanings of 'ibrah is crossing over (al-'ubur) and moving from one thing to another, i.e., that you take from one thing a lesson that benefits in another matter. Among them is 'ibrah meaning a tear (al-dam'ah), which is a hidden thing that you bring to notice and make manifest. The meaning of 'ibrah in the creation of the cattle is: ﴿We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, from between digestive waste and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers. 66﴾ (Surah al-Nahl).

The root saqa (س ق ي) occurs in the Qur'an as saqa and as asqa. Some have said that their meaning is one, but the verified view is that each has its own meaning, even though they agree in the general sense. Saqa, as in His saying: ﴿And their Lord gave them to drink a pure drink. 21﴾ (Surah al-Insan), meaning He gave them what they drink. Its present tense is yasqi. Among its instances is His saying in the story of Musa, peace be upon him: ﴿So he watered for them.. 24﴾ (Surah al-Qasas).

As for asqa, as in His saying: ﴿And We sent down water from the sky and gave you to drink of it, and you are not its storers. 22﴾ (Surah al-Hijr): its meaning is that He, Glorified is He, sent down the water from the sky, which people do not drink at the time of its descent, but so that it may be in the earth for whoever wishes to drink. The Blessed and Most High did not open people's mouths during the descent of the rain so that they might drink from it. No, rather it is stored in the earth for whoever desires it. The present tense of asqa is yusqi.

So there is a difference between the two words, even though we agree on the general sense. And there is a difference between giving what can be benefited from at the moment, as in His saying: ﴿And He gave them to drink.. 21﴾ (Surah al-Insan),

and giving what can be benefited from later on, as in His saying: ﴿So We sent down water from the sky and gave you to drink of it.. 22﴾ (Surah al-Hijr).

Therefore they say: the one who does good may do it immediately, giving the needy, for example, a loaf to eat, or he may do it deferred, giving him what helps him earn continuously, so that he himself may eat from his earnings whenever he wishes. The Blessed and Most High gave us this idea in Surah al-Kahf, in the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn, He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Until, when he reached between the two barriers, he found beside them a people who could hardly understand a saying. 93﴾ (Surah al-Kahf). Since they do not understand speech, how did Dhu al-Qarnayn communicate with them, and how did they say: ﴿O Dhu al-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land, so shall we pay you a tribute on condition that you make between us and them a barrier? 94﴾ (Surah al-Kahf).

We say: the one who wants to do good and kindness strives toward it and devises a way to reach it, as if he devised a way to make them understand, and he was patient with them until he reached a method of communicating with them, although he was able to leave them and turn away from them, his argument being that they do not understand and do not speak.

When Dhu al-Qarnayn wanted to build the barrier for them, he did not build it himself. Rather, he taught them how construction is done, so that they might undertake it themselves whenever they wished, without needing him. So he said: ﴿Bring me blocks of iron, until, when he had leveled between the two cliffs, he said: Blow, until, when he had made it fire, he said: Bring me molten copper to pour over it. 96﴾ (Surah al-Kahf).

So: he taught them and dealt kindly with them, a kindness that never ends. And His saying: ﴿from what is in their bellies.. 66﴾ (Surah al-Nahl).

That is, from what is in the bellies of the cattle. The pronoun in (butunihi, "their bellies") is written in the singular because the intended sense is the genus. Allah, Glorified is He, willed that this milk be brought forth: ﴿from between digestive waste and blood, pure milk.. 66﴾ (Surah al-Nahl). Al-farth is the digested food matter in the animal's paunch.

So the lesson here is that Allah Most High gave us, from between the farth, which is the dung of the cattle and the remnants of food in their paunch, which has a foul smell and a filthy, repellent appearance, and from between blood, which has its red colour and is likewise unpalatable, that from these two the Creator, Glorified is He, brings forth for us milk, pure, free of impurities, clean and sound, without the colour of blood or the smell of farth. Who can do that except the Creator, Glorified is He?

The Blessed and Most High concludes the verse by describing this milk: ﴿pure milk, palatable to the drinkers. 66﴾ (Surah al-Nahl).

That is, the drinker swallows it easily and takes pleasure in it, and he does not choke on it; rather it is palatable and slides down smoothly while drinking. For some food or drink may be sweet to you and easy to swallow, and you find pleasure in it, yet it is not wholesome. Therefore the Blessed and Most High says: ﴿So eat it with satisfaction and ease. 4﴾ (Surah al-Nisa'), hani'an meaning that you find pleasure in it, and mari'an meaning beneficial to the body, that it agrees with you digestively; for you may find delight in something while eating or drinking, and then it causes you hardship afterwards. It is hani' but not mari'.

So milk is among the bounties of Allah that point to His power, Glorified is He, and in its being brought forth from between farth and blood there is a lesson and an admonition. It is as if the Blessed and Most High gives us this lesson to lead us from the sensory meaning that we witness to the moral meaning in the method. He who made for us this lesson to correct our bodily form is able to make for us from the method what corrects our hearts.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 67:

The fruits of the date palm are: al-balah (unripe dates, the fresh dates). And al-a'nab (grapes) is what we call al-karm (the vine). The Qur'anic expression here, although it bestows favour upon His servants with good provision, does not bestow favour upon them by their taking from grapes sakaran (an intoxicant): that is, an intoxicant. Rather, the Truth, glory be to Him, gives us a lesson here, for these verses were revealed before the prohibition of wine (khamr).

It is as if the verse carries an introduction to the prohibition of wine, which they now find pleasing and praise. For this reason the scholars say: whoever reads this verse with the insight of one who looks ahead from God, knows that God has a ruling on intoxication that will come.

How did they arrive at the conclusion that God, the Exalted, has a ruling on intoxication that will come?

They said: because He described the provision as good (hasan), whereas He did not describe intoxication as good. This means that it is not good. That is because we eat the fruits of the date palm (al-balah) as they are, and likewise we eat grapes directly, without any interference from us in what God has created for us.

As for our altering its nature until it becomes wine, intoxicating, this is a corruption of the nature which God chose for us to be a good provision.

It is as if He, glory be to Him, is alerting His servants: "I do not bestow favour upon you with what I have prohibited, for I have not prohibited it yet. So take this intoxication, as you see it, as a pleasure for you, but take from it a lesson: that I did not describe it as good. For if it is not good, then it is ugly. So when the prohibition comes, I will have alerted you from the very beginning."

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who use reason﴾ (Surat an-Nahl). For reason requires that we weigh two things against each other and ask: why was intoxication not described as good? Does it not mean that God, the Exalted, does not love this matter and does not approve it for you?

Therefore, it is as if the verse contains the intention of prohibition. So when God sends down the prohibition of wine, this will have been a preparation for it.

The verse is: the wondrous matter by which God, who created these things for you for the soundness of your physical structures and material forms, informs you that He is capable and trustworthy to legislate for you what guarantees the soundness of your inner meanings and your value-bearing, spiritual hearts.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 16, verse 68:

The bee (al-nahl) is one of the creations of God, and every creation of God has been endowed by God, in it and in its instincts, with that which sustains its welfare. This is explained by the words of the Exalted: ﴿Who created and proportioned; and Who determined and guided﴾ (Surah al-A'la).

That is, He created this one in such a way, and that one in such a way, according to what suits its nature. That is why you find that what is below man follows a method that does not vary. Man, for example, may eat beyond his capacity, and may reach the point of overeating, and then afterwards complain of an illness and seek a remedy for it.

As for the animal, when it has eaten its meal and taken what suffices it, it never adds to it, even if you force it to eat. That is because it is governed by a mechanical instinct, and it has no intellect with which to choose.

We may give as an example of instinct in animals the donkey, which they always accuse and take as a proverb for stupidity. If you drive it to cross a water channel, for instance, you will find it looking at it as though measuring the distance precisely. If it finds it within its capability, it leaps over it without hesitation; and if it finds it beyond its strength and greater than its capacity, it draws back and does not venture upon it. Even if you beat it and shout at it, you can never compel it to do anything beyond its ability.

That is because it is governed by the automatic instinct that God, glorified is He, placed in it, unlike man, who reflects on such matters in order to choose what suits him: this will be such, and that will be such. We may liken this instinct in animals to the electronic brain, which gives you only the information with which it has been fed. As for the divinely given human mind, it is able to think, choose, and weigh alternatives.

The True One, glorified is He, says: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee…﴾ (Surah al-Nahl) [16:68].

The True One, blessed and exalted is He, may bestow favour upon some of His servants and teach them the language of birds and animals, so that they can communicate with it and address it, as in the story of Solomon, peace be upon him. God, glorified is He, who created it and originated it, inspires to it what He wills. So what is wahy (inspiration)?

Wahy (inspiration): the informing by a higher teacher to a lower learner by a hidden way which we do not know; for if He informed it by an explicit way, it would not be wahy.

Wahy therefore entails: a mūḥī (one who inspires), who is the higher; a mūḥā ilayh (one to whom it is inspired), who is the lower; and a mūḥā bihi (that which is inspired), which is the meaning intended by the inspiration.

The True One, blessed and exalted is He, has the full freedom of power to inspire whatever He wills to whomever He wills of His creation. God, glorified and exalted is He, has inspired inanimate matter in His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) quaking, and the earth brings forth its burdens, and man says, "What is wrong with it?" On that Day it will report its news, because your Lord has inspired it.﴾ (Surah al-Zalzalah) [99:1-5].

He informed it by a hidden way specific to the power of the Creator over His creation. Here God inspired the angels: ﴿When your Lord inspired the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who believe"﴾ (Surah al-Anfal) [8:12].

And He inspired the messengers: ﴿Indeed, We have inspired you as We inspired Noah and the prophets after him, and We inspired Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the descendants, and Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon…﴾ (Surah al-Nisa') [4:163], and He inspired His close servants: ﴿And when I inspired the disciples, "Believe in Me and My messenger…"﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah) [5:111]. He inspired them with luminous thoughts that pass through their hearts. And He, glorified is He, inspired the mother of Moses: ﴿And We inspired the mother of Moses, "Suckle him…"﴾ (Surah al-Qasas) [28:7].

This is God's inspiration to whomever He wills of His creation: to the angels, to the earth, to the messengers, to His close servants, to the mother of Moses, to the bee, etc.

Inspiration may also come from other than Him, glorified is He, and it is likewise called wahy, as in His saying: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies…﴾ (Surah al-An'am) [6:121].

And His saying: ﴿They inspire one another with decorated speech as deception…﴾ (Surah al-An'am) [6:112].

But when the word (wahy) is used absolutely without qualification, it refers to the inspiration from God to the messengers; therefore the scholars of jurisprudence say: wahy is God informing His Prophet of His method, and they set aside the other types: the instinct-inspiration, the inspiration of creation, the inspiration of nature (fitrah), etc.

As for His saying: ﴿That take for yourself dwellings in the mountains, and in the trees, and in what they construct﴾ (Surah al-Nahl) [16:68], many researchers are eager to study the bee and the stages of its life since ancient times. Among them is a researcher who traced the historical stages of the bee and concluded that the bee, when it first existed, lived in the mountains, then took to trees and made its hives in them, then took the hives that humans made for it, which is what we now know by the name of the artificial hive or apiary. The wonder here is that this researcher does not know the Noble Qur'an, yet what he concluded matches the Qur'an in complete agreement.

Likewise, he concluded that the oldest honey found is that found in mountain caves; they reached this fact by burning the honey and converting it into carbon, and then through measuring the radiation of the carbon the age can be determined. Thus they found that cave honey is the oldest kind of honey, then tree honey, then honey of hives and apiaries.

So: God, exalted is He, inspired the bee by a hidden way that we do not know, and the process of inspiration differs according to the one who inspires and the one to whom it is inspired. We may illustrate this process with the clever servant whom his master merely glances at, and from that glance he understands everything: Does he want a drink? Or does he want food? Or does he want such-and-such?

The reason honey contains healing for people is that the bee feeds on all kinds of fruits. The variety of fruits makes the honey rich in beneficial elements. When a person consumes it, each element goes to a particular function in the body, and there is healing in it by God's permission.

But what has happened now? We see some people saying: "I have eaten a lot of honey and have not felt any benefit." We say: this is because we have interfered in this process and corrupted the nature that God created for us. The original arrangement is that we leave the bee to feed on all kinds of fruits. What actually happens is that we give it sugar, for example, in place of natural blossoms and flowers, and so the taste of the honey changes and it no longer has the distinctive quality that the Noble Qur'an mentions.

Therefore, whoever follows the prices of bee honey finds a clear difference in price between one type and another. This depends on its quality and how closely it conforms to the nature that the Noble Qur'an describes. The Exalted says: ﴿Then follow the ways of your Lord, made easy﴾ (Surah An-Nahl). That is, move freely among the flowers here and there. For this reason we cannot build the bee houses in which it would reside. It must move from one garden to another. When the crops dry up, the bee feeds on its honey. But people now take all the honey and leave nothing for it, and they put sugar in its place so that it feeds on that throughout this period.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿made easy﴾ (Surah An-Nahl), that is: made smooth, prepared and compliant, so that the bee goes forth seeking these ways and nothing turns it back or prevents it. It flies here and there from one flower to another. Have you ever seen a tree turn away a bee? No. God has made its life and its path easy for it.

From His wisdom and His mercy toward us, He has made the ways of life easy for us, and He has made easy for us what we benefit from. Were it not for His making these things easy, we would not benefit from them. We see a huge camel driven by a small boy, who controls it, makes it kneel, loads it with heavy burdens, and leads it as he wishes, whereas if the camel gets agitated or angry, no one can control it. The small boy did not control it by his own strength, but by God's making it subservient to him.

As for the snake, for example, despite its small size it poses a danger that frightens everyone, and people fear to approach it. This is because God has not made it subservient to us, so it frightens us despite its small size. Likewise, if we consider the flea, for example: how small and insignificant it is, yet it disturbs our sleep and deprives us of the pleasure of quiet rest. Can anyone make the flea subservient to him?

In this there is profound wisdom, as if the Exalted is saying to us: if I make something subservient to you, even if it is among the largest creatures, such as the camel and the elephant, you can benefit from it; and if I do not make it subservient to you, you have no power to subdue it, however insignificant and small it may be. So: matters are not in your power, but take them as God created them for you.

﴿It comes out of their bellies﴾ (Surah An-Nahl). This is because the bee sucks nectar from here and from there, then a divine cooking process takes place in its belly that turns this nectar into purified honey. Someone might think that it takes in the nectar and then regurgitates it as it is. Therefore the Qur'an did not say "from their mouths," but said "from their bellies." This is the divine laboratory that gives us honey in which there is healing for people.

﴿Drink of varying colours﴾ (Surah An-Nahl). Since the bee feeds on all kinds of fruits, and fruits yield different products according to their substances, their colours, their tastes and their smells, it follows that the drink must be of varying colours.

﴿Wherein is healing for people﴾ (Surah An-Nahl). For this reason we find many doctors, may God reward them with good, who are concerned with bee honey and conduct many experiments to learn its medicinal value. But what hinders these efforts is that they cannot find natural honey as God created it.

Nevertheless, despite human interference in the bee's food, benefit remains in it and the quality of healing remains in it. Most important is that it draws out water from the body. Any microbe you want to destroy, draw out its water and it dies immediately.

So when we have natural honey, which God created, the wisdom of its Creator is made manifest in its healing. But when a person interferes in this process, he corrupts it. The whole universe, in which man has no part, proceeds in a straight course without deviation, like the sun, the moon, the stars, and so on. Only man is the sole creature who departs from the way of God.

So for whatever you have a part in, you either intervene in it according to the method of its Creator or you leave it alone. If you intervene in it according to the method of its Creator, it gives you safety and good. But if you intervene in it according to your own method, you corrupt it. The Exalted and Most High says: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers"﴾ (Surah Al-Baqarah). They do not know. They do not distinguish between corruption and reform. The Qur'an contains examples of people who cause corruption on the earth while supposing that they are doing good. He says: ﴿Say, "Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose efforts are lost in the worldly life, while they think they are doing well in work"﴾ (Surah Al-Kahf).

Consider the one who invented the car and these machines that spew their poisons and pollute the environment that God created. It is true that they have saved us time and effort in transport and travel, but look at the harm that has befallen people because of these machines. Look at the exhaust of cars and its effects on human health.

The inventor of these machines should have weighed the benefit they provide against the harm they cause. To the health damage is added the collisions and terrible accidents that take lives. By God, have you ever seen two camels collide on any day? So we must weigh benefits and harms before proceeding with anything, so that we do not corrupt the nature that God created for us.

As for His saying: ﴿wherein is healing for people﴾ (Surah An-Nahl), "people" is a plural of people who differ in their diseases according to individuals and the causes of their diseases. How then can this drink be a healing for all diseases of every kind? We say: because this drink that God prepared for us by His power, the Exalted, came with varying colours, of nectar of many kinds, shapes, tastes and substances. It is not one uniform mixture that all people drink. Rather it came varied and diverse according to the differences among people and the diversity of diseases among them. It is as if each of its components cures one of these diseases.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought﴾ (Surah An-Nahl), reflection (tafakkur) means that you reflect on what you are engaged with in order to derive from it something you were not engaged with, and by this knowledge is enriched. For information, if it does not cross-fertilize, if no new generation arises from it, it stops and becomes rigid, and a person suffers from the stagnation of ambition. When a person suffers this stagnation, progress halts, because the advancements we see in the universe are the result of thinking and the use of reason.

For this reason, the Exalted warns us that when we pass by a phenomenon of the universe, we should not pass by it heedless and turning away, but rather reflect on it and take it into consideration. He says: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by while they turn away from it﴾ (Surah Yusuf). In this verse there is an exhortation to reflect on the phenomena of the universe, and a warning against turning away and heedlessness toward the signs of God. Through thought we derive from the universe what we benefit from.

If we take, for example, the one who invented the steam engine: how did he arrive at this invention that benefited humanity? We find that he arrived at it when he saw a pot boiling on the fire, its lid rising with the steam rising during boiling. He asked himself: why does the lid rise? He used his reason and applied his thinking until he arrived at the power of rising steam, and he was able to employ this power in moving and propelling carriages. Likewise, Archimedes and many others arrived, through consideration and reflection on the phenomena of the universe, at laws of nature that led to beneficial inventions that we now enjoy. The one who invented the wheel: how great was the hardship of man in carrying loads, and what was the most he could carry? After they invented wheels and used them for transport, man became able to carry and move many times what he used to carry.

The one who invented water tanks: how great was the hardship of drawing water from a well or from a river? After the making of tanks and the pumping of water, we now find water in our homes merely by opening the tap.

All these are fruits of the mind when it contemplates, when it reflects on the phenomena of the universe, and uses the raw material that God created and urged us to reflect upon and derive lessons from. As if the Exalted is saying to us: We have given you the necessities of life. If you want the luxury and refinements of life, then use the blessing of reason, thought and contemplation to reach these refinements.

Here the Exalted draws our attention to another point: that He makes perceptible things bring us closer, in meaning, to His method. Therefore He moves us from the perceptible to the abstract.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 70:

His saying: ﴿And Allah created you; then He causes you to die; and among you is he who is returned to the most abject age...﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 70). This is a fact that no one denies, and no one claims it for himself. He has supplied you with the means of your life on earth: the plants, the animals, and the cattle which give us milk, pure and palatable to those who drink it, and then the bee, in which there is healing for mankind.

So Allah, glory be to Him, has given us life, given us the means of life, and given us that which removes the dangers of life. Since you have affirmed these perceptible things, then listen: ﴿And Allah created you; then He causes you to die; and among you is he who is returned to the most abject age...﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 70). When we hear "created you," we acknowledge that Allah created us, but how He created us, we do not know, because it is not a laboratory process. The One who created is Allah alone, glory be to Him, and He is the One who tells us how He created. As for a human intruding and inserting himself into a matter he does not know, we see someone who says that man's origin is an ape, and so on to this nonsense which has no real basis. Therefore, Allah, glory be to Him, says to us: if you want to know how He created you, then listen to the One who created you. Beware of listening to anyone else; for I: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 51). This is a process of which Allah has not informed anyone: ﴿Nor would I have taken the misguiders as helpers﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 51). That is: I did not take a helper to assist Me in the matter of creation. And what is the misguider (al-mudill)? The misguider is the one who tells you words as if they were truth, while he misleads you. So, our Lord, glory be to Him and exalted, here gives us a preliminary idea: beware, for people will come who will mislead you concerning the matter of creation, and they will alter the truth, so beware of believing them, for they were not with Me at the time I created you, so they claim knowledge of this matter. The same applies to the matter of the creation of the heavens and the earth: Allah, glory be to Him, is the One who created them, and He, glory be to Him, is the One who tells us how He created.

So when He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And Allah created you﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 70), we must say: "We hear and we obey, and it is upon the eye and the head." O Lord, You created us, and You know how You created us; we do not ask about this of anyone other than You, and we do not believe in this other than Your word, glory be to You.

Then He, exalted, says: ﴿Then He causes you to die﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 70). That is: from Him, glory be to Him, was the beginning, and to Him, glory be to Him, returns the final destination. Since the beginning is from Him and the return is to Him, and your life lies between these two brackets, do not rebel against Allah in what lies between these two brackets, for that is not befitting for you, since you are from Him and to Him. So why rebellion?

Our Lord, glory be to Him and exalted, here gives us evidence of the absoluteness of His power in the matter of death. Death has no fixed rule: a fetus may die in its mother's womb, a child may die while still a child, a youth or an old man may die, and a person may be returned to the most abject age, that is, live a very long life. And what is in the most abject age? A person returns, after strength and youth, after dignity and standing, after having been one who commanded and forbade and walked the earth proudly, to weakness in everything, even in the most distinguished feature of his make-up, his thought. After knowledge, memory and a strong recollection, he returns like a small child, remembering nothing and capable of nothing. This is so that you may know that the matter is not something inherent in you, but something bestowed upon you by your Creator, glory be to Him, and so that you may know that when He, glory be to Him, decrees death upon us, this is mercy to us and a veil over us from weakness and decrepitude, before we come to need someone to help us and assist us in the simplest matters of life, and to command over us those whom we once commanded.

Hence, death (tawaffi) is one of the blessings of Allah upon us. And so that you may be certain of this truth, look at those whom Allah has prolonged in their lives until they reached what the Qur'an calls "the most abject age," and at the weakness they suffer, and at what their relatives endure in serving them, to the point that the nearest of people to them wishes for their death.

Death, then, is a blessing, especially for the believer who has sent forward good deeds, hoping for their reward from Allah; you will see him rejoicing at death, because it is the lifespan of his hereafter, and he loves to come to it. This is unlike the one who has been wasteful toward himself and did not prepare for this day; you will see him fearful and distressed, knowing what he is coming to.

And ﴿thumma﴾ ("then") is a conjunction indicating sequence with delay, that is, the passage of time between two events. So He created you, then after a time and an interval the second event occurs: ﴿He causes you to die﴾. This differs from the particle ﴿fa﴾ ("so"), which is a conjunction indicating sequence with immediacy, that is, the consecutiveness of the two events, as in His saying: ﴿Then He caused him to die and buried him﴾ (Surah Abasa, 21), for after death burial follows without delay. And His saying: ﴿And among you is he who is returned to the most abject age﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 70). And "the most abject age" (ardhal al-'umr) means its worst, its lowest, and its basest. This is because Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, brought man forth from his mother's womb knowing nothing, and so He said: ﴿And Allah brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing; and He made for you hearing, sight and hearts﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 78). These are the instruments of knowledge in man. So when he is returned to the most abject age, these senses lose their capacity and their function weakens, and man returns as he began, knowing nothing, after what has befallen him of senility and decrepitude. The instruments of knowledge have stopped, man begins to forget, and his memory grows too weak to recall what he once knew. His saying: ﴿So that he will not know, after knowledge, anything﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 70). For this reason they call these senses "the inheritors."

The Almighty concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Competent﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 70), because He, glory be to Him, holds creation in His hand from its beginning, and in His hand is death and the return. This requires knowledge, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Should not He who created know?﴾ (Surah al-Mulk, 14). There must be knowledge, because one who makes a craft must know what sets it right and what spoils it, and that requires a capacity for perception; knowledge alone is not sufficient.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 16, verse 71:

If we look at the universe around us, we find that we are equal in only one thing, which is that we are all servants of Allah. We are equal in this alone, and in everything beyond it we differ: our colours differ, our bodies differ, our forms differ, our talents differ, our provisions differ.

What is remarkable is that this difference is itself the very agreement, because difference may give rise to agreement, and agreement may give rise to difference.

For example: if you and your friend enter one of the restaurants and order a chicken, you by nature like the breast of the chicken, and your friend likes another part of it. This is a difference. But when the food arrives, you find that this difference is itself harmony, for you take what you like and he takes what he likes. This is a difference that led to harmony. But suppose that both of you like the breast, for instance. This is a harmony that may lead to difference when the food arrives and we sit down: which of us takes the breast?!

Allah the Exalted created us differing in things, and He willed that this difference be complementarity among us. So how would complementarity be, then?

Do we imagine, for example, that there could be a person who combines all talents, such that if he wants to build a house, he is the engineer who draws, the builder who builds, the labourer who carries, the carpenter, the blacksmith, the plumber, and so on? Can we imagine that a person could be like this? No.

But the Creator, glorified is He, scattered these talents among people in a scattering, so that each of them remains in need of others in what he does not possess of talents, and by this complementarity is completed in the universe.

So then: the difference between us is itself the harmony, and it is one of His signs, glorified is He, and a wisdom that the Creator, majestic and exalted is He, willed. Thus He said: ﴿And they will not cease to differ﴾ (Surah Hud, 118). So He created us in this way. Otherwise, if we were united and agreed in talents, would it be conceivable that we were all philosophers, physicians, scholars? Then who would build? And who would farm? And who would manufacture?... and so on.

So then: it is of Allah's mercy that He made us differing and complementary. The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿in provision...﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 71). People look at provision from one side only: for them it is wealth, so this one is rich and that one is poor. The reality is that provision is not wealth alone; rather, everything from which you benefit is your provision. So this one's provision is his mind, and that one's provision is his physical strength. This one thinks, and that one works.

So then: we must not view provision as one colour, but rather view everything that Allah created for His creatures of diverse talents: health, capability, intelligence, forbearance, courage... all of this is from the provision in which people are differentiated.

When the Truth, glorified is He, addressed the matter of provision, He left the preference here indefinite, and the verse did not specify who is superior and who is inferior. The word "some" is indefinite, so that we understand from it that every part of the parts is superior in one respect and inferior in another. The strong is superior to the weak by his strength, and he is also inferior, for perhaps the weak is superior by what he has of knowledge or wisdom... and so on.

So then: each one of Allah's creatures has been given by Allah a talent. This talent is not repeated among people, so that creation may be complete and they do not repeat one another. And when a talent is found in one person and is missing in another, the interest requires that the two parties be bound together, not a bond of favour, but a bond of need. How?

The strong works for the weak who has no strength to work with, so he is superior in his strength; and the weak is superior by what he gives the strong of wealth and wages which the strong needs to sustain himself and his dependants. The Truth, glorified is He, did not will that the matter be a favour of one of them over the other, but made it an exchange bound by the need by which a person sustains his life.

Thus this matter comes as a necessity, not as favour from anyone, because favour is not binding; not everyone is able to give without return, or to work without wages. Rather, need is what governs this matter.

So then: what bound society together? It is need, not favour. And since the world is bound by need, every person who sees himself as superior in some respect should not be deceived by his superiority, but should look to the superiority of others over him; and thereby pride is crushed among people, for each completes the other.

We have given as an example for this the wealthy pasha, possessor of greatness and standing, whom circumstances may compel and force to need a simple worker to repair a defect in the facilities of his house. Perhaps he does not find him, or finds him busy, so this great pasha remains distressed and troubled until this simple worker helps him and fulfils what he needs. Thus the owner of wealth and standing needed a person who has none of life's talents except to carry out such simple tasks in the home... and at the same time he is superior to the pasha in this thing.

So then, all in the universe are equal. There is none among us between him and Allah, glorified is He, any lineage or kinship that would give him favour. We are all servants of Allah, and Allah has scattered talents among all people, so that they complement one another, and so that each of them remains in need of the other, and by this the bond in society is completed.

This matter was presented in another verse, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in degrees, so that some of them may take others in service﴾ (Surah Az-Zukhruf, 32).

Some understand that the poor is made subservient to the rich, but the reality is that each of them is made subservient to the other. The poor is subservient to the rich when he does work for him, and the rich is subservient to the poor when he gives him his wage. For this reason the Arab poet says:

"People are for people, from Bedouin and town-dweller, some are servants to others, even if they do not realise."

Here we give an example from the lowliest of trades in people's estimation, though all trades are honourable, and there is no baseness in them so long as a person sustains himself and his dependants from them with lawful means. Baseness lies in the idle, clumsy man who does not master any work.

This simple labourer, the shoe-shiner, people view as lower than them and themselves as greater. But if they looked at the tin of polish he uses, they would find many workers, scholars, engineers and wealthy people working for him in producing this tin, and he is superior to all of them when he buys this tin of polish. Yet people do not look at the subjection of all these people to this simple labourer.

So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so that some of them may take others in service﴾ (Surah Az-Zukhruf, 32).

Which of us subjects the other? Each of us is subservient to the other: you serve me in what you master, and I serve you in what I master. This is Allah's wisdom in His creation, so that balance and complementarity may be achieved among the members of society.

The Lord, glorified is He, did not make these professions natural in us, saying "this is for such and such, and that for such and such." No. Whoever is content with Allah's decree in the work suited to him, however lowly in people's eyes, then perfects the work, strives in it, and exerts his utmost effort, the Truth, glorified is He, says to him: since you have been content with My decree in this work, I will elevate you by it to a standing at which creation will marvel...

Indeed you see them look at one of them and point at him: "he was a porter... he was a hired labourer..." Yes, he was. But he was content with what Allah apportioned, perfected and excelled, so Allah recompensed him, elevated him and raised his station.

Therefore they say: whoever works sincerely at any work for ten years, Allah will make him master for the rest of his life; whoever works sincerely for twenty years, Allah will make his children masters; and whoever works for thirty years, Allah will make his grandchildren masters. Nothing is lost with Allah, glorified is He.

So there is no high and low among us. Beware lest you think you are higher than people. We are equal, but among us is one who perfects his work and among us is one who does not perfect his work; therefore they said: the worth of every person is what he does well.

Do not look at one side of a person, but look at the totality of sides, and you will find that the Truth, glorified is He, is just in distributing talents among people.

We have mentioned that if you made an equation between people, you would find that the total of each person equals the total of every other person. That is, if you took for example: health, wealth, children, strength, courage, peace of mind, a righteous wife, standing and rank... and so on, you would find each one's share at the end of the equation equal to the other's share. You surpass me in strength, and I surpass you in knowledge, and so on... because we are all servants of Allah, and none of us has any lineage or kinship between him and Allah.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then those who were favoured with their provision would not give it to those whom their right hands possess, so that they would be equal therein﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 71):

"Those whom their right hands possess" are the slaves and bondsmen. The meaning: we have not seen any of you whom Allah favoured with provision, and who then gave it to his slaves and bondsmen, never. This has not happened from you. Allah does not blame them for this conduct, nor does He demand that they distribute Allah's provision to their slaves; rather, the verse establishes the proof against them, and an argument for the wrongness of their conduct towards Allah, glorified is He.

As if the Qur'an were saying to them: if Allah has favoured some of you in provision, has any of you volunteered to give his provision to his slaves? Never. This has not happened from you. So how do you take Allah's right of servitude and lordship, His right of obedience, worship, vowing and sacrifice, and give it to idols and images? For you have not done that with what you possess. So how do you permit yourselves to take Allah's right and give it to idols and images?

And He, exalted is He, says in another verse: ﴿He has coined for you a parable from yourselves: Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided you?﴾ (Surah Ar-Rum, 28). That is: you have not done this with yourselves, so how do you do it with Allah? This is a point: you deal with Allah otherwise than you deal with yourselves: ﴿so that they are equal therein﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 71), that is, you have made equal between Allah, glorified is He, and your idols, and made them partners with Him, worshipping them alongside Allah.

The Truth, glorified is He, though He provides and favours us, has also preserved for us wealth and preserved our ownership, and did not command us to give our wealth to people without work and exchange of benefits. So if He asks you to give your needy brother beyond what is obligatory upon you of zakat, He says to you: ﴿Who is it that would lend Allah a goodly loan, so He may multiply it for him?﴾ (Surah Al-Baqarah, 245). Although the Truth, glorified is He, is the giver of provision and blessings, He asks you to lend to Him, as if He, glorified is He, respects your work and effort, and respects your private ownership which He bestowed upon you... so He says: lend to Me. Knowing, glorified is He, the place of wealth in souls, and the lender's eagerness to be certain of the borrower's ability to repay, He made the loan to Himself, so that you, O lender, may be confident that repayment is guaranteed by Allah.

The Truth, glorified is He, concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿Then is it in the favour of Allah that they deny?﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 71). That is: after Allah bestowed provision upon them, and did not ask them to scatter it to others, they denied this blessing, rejected Allah's favour, made partners for Him from idols and images, and gave Allah's right of servitude and lordship to idols and images. This is the very essence of ingratitude and denial of kindness.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 16, verse 72:

The Exalted Lord, in the preceding verse, established for us the supreme principle of creed: that we must not give to anyone other than Him anything that God has reserved for Himself, such as worship, divinity, obedience and the like. If this creedal principle is sound, then all the principles of the universe are sound.

Then He, glory be to Him, explained that He created us from one soul, then created from that one a spouse for him, so that procreation and multiplication might be accomplished. The continuation of your existence depends on two matters:

The first matter: the preservation of life, which He guaranteed through the provisions He bestowed upon us, so that we eat and drink and thereby preserve life. Having spoken in the preceding verse about the preservation of life through provision, He mentioned the second matter: the preservation of life through the preservation of the species. He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And God has made for you spouses from among yourselves﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 72). The word "azwaj" (spouses) is the plural of "zawj," and "zawj" does not mean the man alone but means both the man and the woman, because the word "zawj" is applied to one that has a counterpart of its kind, so each of them is a zawj. The man is a zawj, and the woman is a zawj; it is applied, then, to a single individual that has a counterpart of the same kind. And ﴿from among yourselves﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 72) means from one soul, as He said in another verse: ﴿He created you from one soul, then made from it its spouse﴾ (Surah Az-Zumar, 6), meaning He took a piece of the husband and created the wife from it, just as God created Hawwa' (Eve) from Adam, peace be upon him. Or ﴿and created from it﴾ (Surah An-Nisa', 1) means from its own kind, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ (Surah At-Tawbah, 128), meaning from your own kind. The matter admits of both meanings. Whoever broadens his understanding to the point that God created Hawwa' from a rib of Adam, meaning from him, from a part of him, there is no objection; and whoever says that God created Hawwa' as He created Adam, as a separate creation, and then joined them in marriage, there is no objection either. The first is in the sense of partness, and the second in the sense of "of your own kind."

We have said: when a plural is set against a plural, the division requires individuals. As when a teacher says to his students: "Take out your books," he is addressing the students, who are plural, and their books are plural. Will each student take out the books of the others? No. Rather each of them will take out his own book only. So the division here requires individuals. Likewise the meaning in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He created for you from yourselves spouses﴾ (Surah Ar-Rum, 21), meaning He created for each one of you a spouse.

To confirm this truth, and that creation began with Adam, peace be upon him, we trace things back into the past, and we will find that whatever multiplies in the future diminishes in the past. For example, the population of the world today is greater than it was last year. Thus the numbers decrease the further we go back into the past, until we arrive at one human being, Adam, peace be upon him, together with his spouse Hawwa', since the minimum of multiplication is from two. So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He created you from one soul and created from it its spouse﴾ (Surah An-Nisa', 1), is a sound statement, supported by induction and statistics.

Therefore our Lord, glory be to Him, bestows favour upon us that He created spouses for us, and bestows favour upon us that He made this spouse from among ourselves, and not from another kind, because a human being's affection and intimacy are not complete except with his own kind. This is among the greatest of God's blessings upon us. You may imagine the situation if God had made for us spouses from other than our kind! How would it be?!

This spouse shares with us in some things and differs from us in one thing. We agree in several things: the form is one, the mould is one, the mind is one, and the parts are one: two eyes, two ears, two hands, two legs, and so on. This commonality helps toward elevation, affection, intimacy and companionship. We differ in one thing, which is the sex: this is male, and this is female. So: our genus is united, and our species is distinguished; thereby the complementarity that God willed for the building of the earth is accomplished.

There is also the possibility that a male may change into a female, or a female into a male. For this, God created provision for this phenomenon: for instance, a man may have a small breast, or other organs capable of transformation, when the need arises to change the sex. This is a wise composition and a high power. So ﴿from among yourselves﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 72) is so that affection, love and tenderness may increase among you. This is why, in the story of Prophet Sulayman (Solomon), peace be upon him, and the hoopoe, when he inspected the birds and noticed the absence of the hoopoe, he said: ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him, or he must bring me a clear authority﴾ (Surah An-Naml, 21). This "authority" is the royal authority that God gave Sulayman. They said concerning ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment﴾ (Surah An-Naml, 21) that it means placing him among other than his own kind. So placing him among other than his kind is a form of punishment. And ﴿from among yourselves﴾ is a blessing and mercy from God.

In another verse, the Exalted One mentions three elements for the continuation of the marital relationship, saying: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves that you may find tranquillity in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾ (Surah Ar-Rum, 21). If we reflect on these three stages, we find tranquillity (sakan) between the spouses, whereby each finds rest in the other, feels reassured by him, is happy with him, and finds in him what he needs. When this level is shaken and one of them recoils from the other, the role of affection and love comes into play, which holds the reins of married life and provides both of them with a sufficient measure of acceptance. If one of them weakens in performing his duty towards the other, the role of mercy comes into play, so each shows mercy to the other: mercy for his weakness, mercy for his illness. In this way married life continues and is not exposed to the storms of life's journey. But if these stages are exhausted, and there remains between them neither tranquillity nor affection, nor even mercy from either toward the other, then companionship has become impossible between them, and it has become wise for one to part from the other. Here the Exalted Lord legislated divorce (talaq) as a solution for such cases, yet our Lord, glory be to Him, made it the most detested of the permissible things, so that we approach it only when compelled and constrained.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And made for you from your spouses sons and grandchildren﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 72): the sons are the first link in the preservation of life, and the grandchildren (hafadah), who are the sons' sons, are the second link in the preservation of life. This is because a human being by nature loves life and dislikes death, and he sees it every day reaping souls around him. His belief in death is a certainty, so when he becomes certain that life will escape him personally, he wishes to preserve it in his offspring. From here comes the love of many of us for males, who represent a continuation of the fathers. When God grants him children and secures for him the first generation, he aspires to see the children of his children, in order to preserve life for himself and for his progeny after him. This is why the poet who addresses his son says to him:

"My son... O you who are myself after I have passed away"

This is people's view of children: that they are a male remembrance of them after their death, as though his name were connected and never ends. And God, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿sons and grandchildren﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 72), which shows us the necessity of keenness on the integration of generations: spouses, then sons and grandchildren. So what is the benefit of the integration of generations? What is the benefit of coexistence and mixing between the grandfather and his grandson?

We observe that the young infant begins to perceive as soon as his faculties of perception begin to function, and he starts to pick up from those around him and to learn from them. If he has older siblings, he learns from them, for example, "baba" and "mama"; if he has no siblings, we teach him these words. That is why we see the second child is cleverer than the first, and the third cleverer than the second, and so on, because he takes from those before him and from those around him, and thereby his perception increases and his experiences and knowledge grow. Let us imagine that this son has become a father, and there came the grandchild who lives in the time of both generations: the generation of the father and the generation of the grandfather. The little one grows up in their embrace, so you see him taking from his father the vigour of activity in life and the striving for sustenance, while he takes from his grandfather the religious values, since the grandfather is constantly at home after advancing in years, so he turns to obedience and worship. The little one hears from him the recitation of the Qur'an: "When is the call to Zuhr?" "Son, bring the mushaf." "Son, bring the prayer rug so I may pray," and other such words from which the little one takes these values. So: the grandchild picks up a kind of activity and movement from his father's generation, and picks up a kind of values from his grandfather's generation. Therefore the distancing of generations causes a deficiency in the formation of children, and God, exalted is He, wills that the generations be joined together, so that the child may have the complete elements of upbringing, between moral values and movement and activity.

As for His saying: ﴿and provided you with good things﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 72): the good things are in the provision that God made for the preservation of life, and in marriage that God made for the preservation of the species. Then He says: ﴿Will they then believe in falsehood and deny the blessing of God?﴾ (Surah An-Nahl, 72). Falsehood (al-batil) is the idols they took besides God.

In the verse there is an interrogation expressing wonder and denunciation: how do you deny God's blessing when He created you at the beginning from one soul, created from it its spouse, made for you spouses from among yourselves, placed between you tranquillity, affection and mercy, then made for you sons and grandchildren, provided you with the blessings of life that preserve your lives, and with the blessings of spouses that preserve your species, and placed you in favour and ease? He created you from nothing and sustained you from nothing.

After all this, do you still deny His blessing and reject it, and instead of turning to Him and facing Him, you turn to worshipping idols that neither harm nor benefit? Did the idols do anything of this for you? Did they bestow upon you any of these blessings?

These idols are in need of you: they take from you and do not give to you. This one is crooked and needs someone to straighten it; that one is broken and needs someone to repair it. Move the god; place the god in such-and-such a place, and so on.

Worship (ʿibada) means that the worshipper obeys the one he worships, and this obedience requires carrying out the command and avoiding the prohibition. So is worship only carrying out the command and avoiding the prohibition? We say: no. Rather, every movement in life that helps one toward worship is itself worship, and whatever an obligation cannot be completed without is itself obligatory. To clarify this matter, let us give this example: if you wish to perform God's obligation in prayer, for instance, you need strength to perform this duty, and you will find this strength only through food and drink. Let us take the simplest food that can be imagined: a loaf of bread. Consider how many hands have had a part in it, from the time it was a grain of wheat thrown into the earth until it became a tasty loaf. All those who turned the wheel of this process are performing a positive movement in life, which in itself is worship, because it has helped you to worship.

Likewise, if you wish to pray, it is obligatory for you to cover your nakedness. Look at this cloth without which the prayer is not complete: everyone who contributed to its cultivation and manufacture until it reached you, all of them are performing worship by their movement in making this cloth.

Therefore: everything that helps you to worship God is worship, and every movement in the universe that leads to something of this is worship. When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, summoned the believers to the Friday prayer, He said, glorified is He:

﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of God and leave off trade﴾ (Surah al-Jumu'ah). He did not take them from emptiness, but from work. But why did He say, glorified is He: (and leave off trade)? Why trade in particular? They said: because trade is the goal of all the movements of life; it is the intermediary between producer and consumer. The Qur'an did not say: leave the factories or the fields, because there are things whose fruit does not come in its hour. The one who plants waits months to harvest what he planted, and the craftsman waits until he sells his craft. But a sale is a present transaction, so it is the object of attention. Likewise, it did not say: leave off buying. They said: because the seller loves to sell, but the buyer may buy while he is unwilling. So the Qur'an brought the most precise thing that can tie you to time, which is trade. Then, when the prayer is over, we are commanded to return to work and to strive in the corners of the earth:

﴿Then when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek of the bounty of God﴾ (Surah al-Jumu'ah).

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they worship other than God﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 73), the Truth, glorified be He, wished to speak about the object they prefer over God, which is the idols. God, glorified is He, who created them and provided for them from the good things, and made for them spouses from among themselves, and made for them sons and grandchildren, was due to be worshipped for His blessing and bounty. The one who does not worship God for His essence, glorified is He, worships Him for His blessings and his need for Him. So there is worship of the Essence, because He, glorified is He, deserves worship for His essence, and worship of the attributes of the Essence in what He gives. Whoever does not worship Him for His essence worships Him for His blessings.

Since worship requires carrying out commands and avoiding prohibitions, how then can worship be due to these idols which they have taken? How do you worship them when they have commanded you nothing and forbidden you nothing? This is the first criticism of worshipping other than God, whether it be the sun, the moon, an idol, or a tree.

Likewise: what do the idols, or your other objects of worship, give to the one who worships them, and what reward have they prepared for them? And with what do they punish the one who disbelieves in them? Thus, it is a god without a method.

Religiosity is an instinct in the soul to which a person turns in his time of weakness and need. God, glorified is He, is the One who loves that we turn to Him, call upon Him, and ask Him to fulfil our needs. He has a method which requires demands that crush sovereignty and tyranny in souls, and requires burdensome obligations upon the self.

Thus the disbelievers turned to worshipping idols and images, because they are gods without obligation and objects of worship without demands. How easy it is for a person to cling to a god and say: "I worship him without his commanding anything or forbidding anything!" How easy it is for the instinct of religiosity in the self to be satisfied with worshipping such a god.

But you must not forget that this god who has no obligation, you will not be able to ask anything of him, or turn to him in hardship. This is not reasonable: just as they do not ask anything of you, so they do not possess benefit or harm for you.

Therefore we found that those who claim prophethood, these liars, make the paths of worship easy for people and permit for them what religion has forbidden, such as the mixing of men and women and other things, in order to attract the largest possible number of followers. Then came Musaylima the liar, and wished to make obligation easy for people, so he spoke of dropping the prayer; and another came and spoke of dropping zakat. This ease attracted many fools who are impatient with obligation and incline to an easy religion that suits their base aspirations.

Thus we found supporters for these liars who back them and aid them. But soon the realities are revealed, and these deceived ones stand face to face with the truth about their prophets.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they worship other than God what does not possess for them any provision﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 73). In this verse we notice a kind of elevation in the argument against the invalidity of worshipping idols, because the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, said of them in another verse: ﴿They create nothing, and they are created﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 20). Thus He negated from them the capacity to create, indeed they themselves are created. One of them goes and admires a stone, takes it and works on it with his chisel until he shapes it into some form, then takes it as a god to worship besides God. When He negated from them the capacity to create, He wished here to advance in the argument, so He negated from them mere ownership, for one may own what he did not create. So the verse here establishes that they do not own, even mere ownership.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿from the heavens and the earth anything﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 73). Provision comes from the sky by rain, and from the earth by plants, and from both sources the provision of God comes. By this, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, guarantees for us the necessities and essentials of life, from the water of the sky and the plants of the earth. If you want the luxury of life, then strive in what God has given you of the necessities of life, so that you may reach this luxury. The true, direct provision is what God has sent down to us from the rain of the sky, so that He causes the plants of the earth to grow for us.
