Command and dominion belong to God, and since they did not submit willingly and by choice, let them submit to Him by compulsion, in spite of their noses.

Here a feature of faith becomes clear to us: it has made me submit to Almighty and Majestic God by choice, rather than submitting by compulsion on the day when the truth is revealed, that there is no god but Allah, and He, glorified and exalted, will confront me on a day in which I have no choice.

As for His saying: ﴿And what they used to fabricate will have vanished from them.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl)

A word: Al-dalal (going astray, loss) occurs with several meanings. Among them: "dalla" (it was lost), meaning their intercessors were absent from them, so they began searching for them but did not find them. From this meaning is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "When we are lost in the earth, will we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ (Surah al-Sajdah), that is, they disappear into the earth, where the earth consumes their particles and hides them within its belly. Likewise we say: al-dallah, meaning the lost animal, that is, the beast that strayed, i.e., went missing from its owner. Among the meanings of dalal is forgetfulness, as in His saying: ﴿That if one of them errs, the other will remind her﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah). Among its meanings is hesitation, as in His saying: ﴿And He found you lost and guided you﴾ (Surah al-Duha). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not have a method which he then abandoned, turned away from and left, after which God guided him. Rather, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was perplexed and hesitant regarding what the leaders of the people and those of sound intellect were upon, of actions that conflict with sound reason and luminous nature, so the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) bewilderment concerned what he saw of these people's actions while he did not know their reality.

So His saying: ﴿And what they used to fabricate will have vanished from them﴾ (Surah al-Nahl), that is, it disappeared from them: ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾ (Surah al-Nahl), that is, what they lied about in claiming gods and intercessors besides God.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 88:

Here there is a distinction between disbelief (kufr) and barring from the way of Allah (al-sadd 'an sabil Allah). Disbelief is a sin personal to the human being himself; it does not extend beyond him to others. So disbelieve as you wish, and Allah forbid, you are free! !

As for barring from the way of Allah, it is a sin that transgresses to others: the person calls others to disbelief, compels them toward it, and makes it attractive to them. Here the sin is doubled: a sin for his own disbelief in himself, and a sin for barring others from faith. Therefore the Exalted says in another verse: ﴿And they will surely carry their burdens and other burdens along with their burdens.﴾ (Surah al-'Ankabut, 13).

If someone says: "How? Yet the Exalted has said: ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 164)."

We say: there is no contradiction between the two verses. Each one will bear his own burden: the one who barred others from the way of Allah bears two burdens, while the one who was barred bears only the burden of his own disbelief.

And His saying: ﴿We shall increase them in punishment upon punishment.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 88).

The first punishment is for their own disbelief, and the added punishment is for the disbelief of others, those whom they barred from the way of Allah.

For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam, he will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts by it until the Day of Resurrection, and whoever establishes an evil practice, he will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts by it until the Day of Resurrection."

So beware lest the eye or ear of society fall upon you while you are in a state of opposition to the method of Allah, for this opposition will affect others, and will be a cause of further opposition, indeed opposings, and you will bear a share of this. You are a wretch bearing your own sins and the sins of others.

And His saying: ﴿Because they used to cause corruption.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 88). Ifsad (corruption) means that you deliberately go to something good or near to good and corrupt it; and if you left it alone, it might well be guided to the method of Allah. Thus: you have corrupted what was good, and prevented what was receptive to goodness from becoming good.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 16, verse 89:

His words: ﴿from among themselves﴾ (Surah an-Nahl).

He means: from their own kind. The intended meaning is the people of the call to God: the callers (du'at), preachers (wu'az) and imams who conveyed God's method to people. These will bear witness before God, may He be glorified, against whoever fell short in God's method. It may also be that the meaning of ﴿from among themselves﴾ is: a part of their parts and a limb of their limbs, as the Exalted said:

﴿On the day when their tongues and their hands and their feet will testify against them as to what they used to do﴾ (Surah an-Nur, 24)

And His saying: ﴿And they will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?"﴾ (Surah Fussilat, 21).

When the witness is from the very being of the human and one of his parts, there is no doubt that his proof is strong and his evidence clear. And His saying: ﴿And We have brought you as a witness against these people﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 89) means: a witness against your community, as if the Prophet ﷺ is a witness over the witnesses.

﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 89). The Book is the noble Qur'an. "Explanation" means a complete explanation of everything a person needs. The word "thing" (shay') is called the genus of genera, meaning: everything that is called "a thing," its explanation is in the Book of God, the Exalted.

If someone says: If this is so, why do we ask the scholars to exert effort (ijtihad) to derive a specific ruling for us?

We say: The Qur'an came as a miracle, and it came as a method of the foundations (usul). The Truth, blessed and exalted, gave His Messenger ﷺ the right of legislation, and He said, the Exalted: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ (Surah al-Hashr, 7).

Thus: the Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ, whether in word, deed or tacit approval, is established by the Book, and it explains and clarifies it. For example, the sunset prayer (salat al-maghrib) is three rak'ahs; where is this in the Book of God? We say: in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾ (Surah al-Hashr, 7).

The Messenger ﷺ clarified this matter when he sent Mu'adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) as a judge to the people of Yemen, and wished to ascertain his capacity for judging. He asked him: "By what will you judge?" He said: "By the Book of Allah." He said: "And if you do not find it?" He said: "By the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah." He said: "And if you do not find it?" He said: "I will exert my own opinion (ajtahidu ra'yi) and I will not fall short (la alu), i.e., I will not fall short in ijtihad."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Praise be to Allah who has granted success to the messenger of the Messenger of Allah to what pleases Allah and His Messenger."

Thus: ijtihad is derived from the Book of Allah, and every matter that arises before us for which there is no text, neither in the Book nor in the Sunnah, ijtihad in it is permitted to us.

We mention here that Imam Muhammad 'Abduh (may Allah have mercy on him) related that, while he was in Paris, one of the orientalists said to him: "Is it not in the verses of the Qur'an: ﴿We have not neglected anything in the Book﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 38)?"

He said: "Yes." He said to him: "Then bring me from the Qur'an: how many loaves are there in an ardab of wheat?"

The Shaykh said: "We ask the baker, for he has the answer to this question." The orientalist said: "I want the answer from the Qur'an, which neglects nothing." The Shaykh said: "This Qur'an is what taught us that, regarding what we do not know, we should ask the people of remembrance," and He said:

﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya, 7).

Thus: the Qur'an has given me the proof, and has given me what I rely upon when I do not find a text in the Book of Allah. The Qur'an has mentioned the rules and foundations, and has given me the right of ijtihad in what occurs to me of branches and in what new matters arise. When a general ruling is found in the Qur'an, it is necessary that there be taken within it what is taken from it of rulings issued by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, because Allah entrusted him with that.

He said: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ (Surah al-Hashr, 7).

Likewise, consensus (ijma') of the Ummah, because God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers, We will leave him in what he has taken and burn him in Hell﴾ (Surah an-Nisa, 115).

And every ijtihad is referred back to the people of ijtihad: ﴿And if they had referred it back to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those who derive it from them would have known it﴾ (Surah an-Nisa, 83).

Thus: everything that issued from the Messenger ﷺ, and from consensus, and from the imams who exercised ijtihad, is present in the Qur'an, so it is true.

Here we must distinguish between things and matters, for they are many. What does the Qur'an address? The Qur'an addresses the legal obligations (ahkam taklifiyyah) required of the servant who has believed in God. There are also cosmic matters (umur kawniyyah) whose benefit to a person is not affected by his knowing them; he benefits from them whether he knows them or not. The Earth's being spherical in shape, its orbiting the sun, and other cosmic matters: if he knows them, then good and excellent; if he is ignorant of them, his ignorance does not prevent him from benefiting from them.

For example, the illiterate villager benefits from electricity, though he knows nothing of its nature or how it works; yet he benefits from it. The mere placing of his finger on the switch lights it for him.

Had the Truth, blessed and exalted, clarified the cosmic signs in a clear manner, it might have repelled the Arabs, who knew nothing of the movement of the universe and did not have the culture by which to comprehend the purposes of the Qur'an concerning the cosmic signs. For this reason they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the crescents, as the noble Qur'an relates:

﴿They ask you about the crescents﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 189).

Al-ahilla is the plural of hilal (crescent), which is what appears of the moon at the beginning of the month, when it looks like a paring of a fingernail; then it gradually increases until it reaches the stage of the full moon when its circle is complete, then it gradually decreases again until it returns to what it was. This is a wonder they see with their own eyes, and they ask about it.

But how did the Qur'an answer them? The noble Qur'an did not explain to them how the crescent occurs, and that when the Earth comes between the sun and the moon and blocks the sunlight from it, the crescent and its various phases result.

This detail their minds could not grasp, and they lacked the culture by which to understand such cosmic matters. Therefore He tells them: turn your gaze away from this, and look to the wisdom of the Creator, may He be glorified, in the crescents:

﴿Say: They are times for people and for the Hajj﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 189). Thus He directed them to a matter related to their traditional religion, and He focused on explaining its wisdom. At the same time He left this question to time to explain it to them, for they would find in the Qur'an what helps them understand this subject. Thus: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿of anything﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 38) means: of every legal matter; if the believer does it, he is rewarded, and if he does not do it, he is punished. As for cosmic matters, He gives them of these according to their awareness of them, and leaves to time the task of explaining what new thought occurs in it.

Therefore we see that the noble Qur'an did not exhaust its giving entirely in the Qur'an revealed in it; for had it done so, it would have met the later centuries without any giving. Minds open over the ages and bring forth new thought, and it is not proper that the first giving remain itself without renewal; every century must have a new giving that suits the progress of mankind in its cosmic sciences.

When the Messenger ﷺ saw people pollinating palm trees, that is, fertilizing them, which is what is known as the process of fertilization, where they take from the male and place it in the female, what did he say to them? He said: "If you did not do it, it would bear fruit." In the following season they abandoned this process and the palm did not bear fruit. When the Prophet ﷺ was asked, he said: "You are more knowledgeable about your worldly affairs."

This is a worldly matter subject to experiment and the product of laboratory research, and it is not the task of the Messenger ﷺ to clarify these matters on which people agree and on which their inclinations coincide. Rather, the legal rulings are those on which inclinations differ, and the Truth settled them by judgment.

For example, in the world there are material currents concerned with discoveries, inventions and deductions that harness the secrets of the universe for the service of humanity. Do people differ regarding the findings of this material current? Do we say, for example: this is American electricity, and this is Russian electricity? Do we say: this is English chemistry, and this is German chemistry?

This is a matter born of the laboratory and experiment, on which all people agree, whereas we find them differing over theoretical things and fighting over them: this is socialism, this is capitalism, this is existentialism, that is secularism, and so on. Thus religion came to settle what inclinations differ over.

Therefore we see every camp trying to steal what the other camp has reached of discoveries and inventions, and sending its spies to follow the developments of what others have reached. Do they steal theoretical matters too? No; on the contrary, you find them placing barriers and precautions so that these principles do not pass to their own lands and to the thinking of their citizens.

The Messenger ﷺ made himself an example and model to clarify this matter, although someone might say: it is not fitting regarding the Messenger of Allah that he advise people on something and his advice prove wrong. Rather, the Messenger here wants to convey a rule into the minds of those who speak on matters of religion: beware of throwing yourselves into material, laboratory, applied matters, for these are matters in which the believer and the disbeliever are equal.

For this reason, when scholars discovered that the Earth is spherical and that it orbits the sun, some religious men objected to this and poked their noses into a matter in which religion has no role, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had warned them against this.

And what do you say after scientists ascended to other planets, photographed the Earth, and the picture came out truly spherical? Do not open for yourselves, in the name of religion, a door you cannot close.

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 89).

The Truth, blessed and exalted, described the Qur'an here as ( guidance / hudan ). If the Qur'an had been sent down as an explanation, the parallelism would require that He say "hadiyan" (a guide), but He did not describe the Qur'an as a guide (hadin), rather as hudan, as if it were the very essence of guidance; because "hadin" is a being to whom guidance is attributed, whereas "hudan" means it is the very substance of guidance, just as we say: "So-and-so is just" (adil). In emphasis we say: "So-and-so is justice" (adl), as if justice were embodied in him, and not merely someone to whom the attribute of justice is ascribed. Similarly, our saying: 'alim (knowing) and 'alim (very knowing), and He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And over every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing﴾ (Surah Yusuf, 76).

What is the meaning of guidance (huda)? It is indicating the path that leads to the goal by the nearest route. (Mercy / rahmah): sometimes the Qur'an is described as mercy, and sometimes as: ﴿a healing and a mercy﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 82).

Healing (shifa') means that there is an illness which the Qur'an treats, and mercy is the protection that prevents the illness from occurring. As long as the Qur'an is so, whoever acts by its method has been given good tidings of a great reward from God, the Exalted: an everlasting reward in lasting bliss.

Al-Haqq, blessed and exalted is He, has in this verse three commands: justice ('adl), beneficence (ihsan), and giving to kinsfolk (iitha' dhi al-qurba). And three prohibitions: against indecency (fahsha'), evil (munkar), and oppression (baghy). When this verse was revealed, Ibn Mas'ud said: "The most comprehensive verse of the Qur'an for good is this verse, because it gathers every virtue that can be found in the Noble Qur'an."

For this reason, our master 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) loved for him to embrace Islam, and he would constantly present Islam to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not like to present Islam to anyone unless he saw in them signs and traits that would be becoming in Islam.

It was as though he (ﷺ) cherished these signs being found in a non-Muslim, so he was eager for his Islam and often presented it to him. However, our master 'Uthman ibn Maz'un delayed the matter, until he sat with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a gathering, and he saw him raise his gaze to the sky, then become alert. Ibn Maz'un said to him: "What has happened, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Jibril, peace be upon him, has just now descended to me with the saying of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and beneficence and giving to kinsfolk, and forbids immorality and wrongdoing and oppression. He admonishes you that you may be reminded.﴾ (Surah An-Nahl)

Ibn Maz'un, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The love of faith settled in my heart through this verse, which comprises every quality of good." Then he went and informed Abu Talib. When Abu Talib heard what Ibn Maz'un had said about this verse, he said: "O assembly of Quraysh, believe in what Muhammad has brought, for he has indeed brought you the best of morals."

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while presenting himself to the tribes of the Arabs, with Abu Bakr and 'Ali accompanying him, 'Ali said: "Then behold, a gathering with dignity and awe. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) approached them and invited them to the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Then Miqran ibn 'Amr, who was from Shayban ibn Tha'laba, stood up and said: 'To what do you call us, O brother of Quraysh?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and beneficence and giving to kinsfolk, and forbids immorality and wrongdoing and oppression. He admonishes you that you may be reminded.﴾ (Surah An-Nahl). Miqran said: 'You have indeed called to the noble characteristics and the best of deeds. Quraysh has indeed opposed you and supported one another against you.'"

'Uthman ibn Maz'un took this verse and conveyed it to 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and 'Ikrimah took it and conveyed it to al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and said to him: "A verse has been revealed to Muhammad saying such and such." Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira reflected (afkara), i.e., he pondered what he had heard, and said: "By Allah, it has a sweetness, and upon it is a radiance; its upper part is fruitful and its lower part is abundant; it is elevated and nothing is elevated above it; and it is not the speech of a human being."

Despite this testimony of his, he did not believe. They said: "It is enough for him that he testified for the Qur'an while he is a disbeliever." Thus this verse entered the hearts of these people and settled in their hearts, because it is a comprehensive and preventive verse, calling to every good and forbidding every evil. His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice...﴾ (Surah An-Nahl).

What is justice ('adl)? Justice is equity (insaf), equality, and the absence of inclination; for it occurs only between two opposing things. Therefore the just judge is called "munsif" (equitable), because when two adversaries appear before him, he gives each of them half of his attention, as though he divided himself into two halves, not inclining to either of them by a hair's breadth. This is equity.

And for the sake of equity the balance was made, and the precision of a balance varies according to what is weighed. The sensitivity of a grain scale is not the sensitivity of a jewellers' scale, for example, and the precision of the balance reaches its limit among the people of the pharmaceutical profession, where the smallest excess in the balance can turn medicine into poison. We have witnessed a great development in scales, until we can weigh the smallest thing imaginable.

Justice pervades all the affairs of life, from the summit of the testimony that there is no god but Allah, to removing harm from the road. Justice is required in all matters of obligation: in matters of belief, which are the work of the heart, and likewise in practical matters, which are the actions of the limbs in the movement of life.

How is justice in matters of belief?

If we look at the beliefs of the disbelievers, we find some of them saying there is no god in the universe, denying His existence absolutely, and others saying there are many gods. Thus statements contradicted one another and opinions diverged. Then Islam came with justice: God is one, with no partner, transcendent above whatever resembles created things, and it took a position of justice regarding His attributes, glorified and exalted is He. He has hearing, but not like the hearing of created things. We do not negate such attributes from Him, lest we be among the Mu'attila (those who deny attributes), nor do we liken Him to anything else, lest we be among the Mushabbiha (anthropomorphists). Rather we say: "There is nothing like unto Him," and we stand in the position of justice and moderation.

Likewise, among the matters of belief in which the justice of Islam is manifest is the question of compulsion and free choice (al-jabr wa al-ikhtiyar). It chose a middle position between those who say that a person performs his actions by his own choice without any involvement of Allah in the deeds of the servant, and therefore He ordained reward and punishment for them, and those who say: "No; rather all actions are from Allah and the servant is compelled to them."

Islam comes with justice and moderation on this question and says: "Rather, the human being performs his voluntary actions by the power that Allah created in him for choice."

In legislation and rulings there was a great difference between the law of Musa, peace be upon him, and the law of 'Isa, peace be upon him, regarding retaliation (qisas), for example: In the law of Musa, materialism prevailed among the Children of Israel, to the point that they said to Musa, peace be upon him: ﴿Show us Allah openly﴾ (Surah An-Nisa, 153).

They did not understand the unseen nor were they convinced by it, so retaliation was suitable for them without fail. Had the Truth, glorified is He, left them, killing would have multiplied among them, for they would not desist except by this deterrent ruling: whoever kills is killed, and "retaliation is a means of preventing killing." The Children of Israel transgressed in seeking to see Allah, for your seeing God is a contradiction in divinity, since when your eye sees Him you have limited Him to a space.

Therefore: His not being seen is the perfection in Him, glorified and exalted is He. And how can we hope to see Him, majestic is He, when we cannot see even some of His creatures? The spirit that is between the sides of each of us: what do we know of its nature and its place in the body, by which we move and carry out our works, by which we think and by which we live? Where is it?

When the spirit departs the body, and God takes its secret, it becomes a corpse that people hasten to bury in the dust. Have you seen this spirit? Have you heard it? Have you perceived it by any of your senses?

If the spirit, being a creature of Allah, is beyond the grasp of the intellect, how then with the One who created this spirit? From His greatness, glorified is He, is that no eyes can perceive Him, and He perceives the eyes.

Likewise, there are things that religion requires, such as truth (al-haqq), for example, a meaning that everyone claims and demands to act upon. What is the shape of this truth? What is its colour? Is it long or short? If we cannot conceive of the truth, though it is a creature of Allah, glorified is He, how can we conceive of Allah and hope to see Him?

And of the excess of the Children of Israel in materialism: they made for God, exalted is He, in the Talmud, a group of chieftains, and made Him, glorified is He, sitting on a rock, dangling His legs into a bowl of marble, then a fish came... etc. Glory be to Allah! Has materialism brought them to this extent?

Hence the universe needed a spiritual force, which should also be excessive in spirituality so that a kind of balance might occur in the universe. The law of 'Isa, peace be upon him, came after an excessive materialism and extravagance in Mosaic practice. So how could the ruling of retaliation remain in it, when it aims to elevate the spiritual lives of people?

The law of 'Isa, peace be upon him, came to calm the situation if a killing occurred: since one killing suffices, let the other be spared, and let us not stir up uproar, nor inflame the grudges and enmities among people. So this law called for pardon of the killer.

Then Islam came and took the position of justice and moderation in this ruling: it upheld retaliation and called for pardon. It gave the victim's guardian the right to retaliation, and at the same time called him to pardon in the saying of the Exalted:

﴿So whoever is pardoned by his brother [anything], then pursuit should be made in a reasonable manner, and payment should be made to him in a good way.﴾ (Surah Al-Baqarah, 178)

We note here that the Qur'an made them brothers in order to soften hearts and remove rancour. Retaliation in Islam has lofty wisdoms: its purpose is not to magnify this crime, but to aim at preserving people's lives, as the Exalted said: ﴿And in retribution there is life for you, O people of understanding﴾ (Surah Al-Baqarah, 179). Whoever wishes to preserve his life should not threaten the lives of others. When our Lord, blessed and exalted, gives the guardian of the slain the right of retaliation and enables him to exercise it, his anger cools and his fury subsides, so he considers pardon while he is able to avenge. Thus this ruling removes resentment from hearts and extinguishes the fire of vengeance among people.

Therefore, in some lands where blood feuds spread, the killer comes carrying his shroud on his hand to the guardian of the slain, places himself in his hands confessing his crime, saying: "Here I am in your hands; kill me, and this is my shroud." This has never happened except that the rightful party and the guardian of blood pardoned him, and this is the justice that Islam brought, the religion of moderation and balance.

This pardon from the guardian of blood is an instrument of construction and a means of love. When we give him the right of retaliation and then he pardons, the killer's life has become a gift from the guardian of blood. It is as though he has taken possession of him and preserved him by his pardon. This is a beautiful thing that the killer's family preserves, and they say: "This has preserved the blood of our son."

Another position of Islam's justice and moderation is seen in the ruling on menstruation, for example. In the law of Musa, peace be upon him, a husband would expel his wife from the house for the entire period of menstruation; the two would not be gathered in one house. In the law of 'Isa, peace be upon him, there was no objection to her being in the house, nor to his intercourse with her and enjoying her.

Islam then brought justice in this matter and said: the menstruating woman remains in her house and does not leave it, but the husband does not approach her during the period of menstruation. Allah, the Exalted, said:

﴿They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is a harm, so keep away from women during menstruation and do not approach them until they are clean. And when they have purified themselves, then come to them from where Allah has commanded you. Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves.﴾ (Surah Al-Baqarah, 222)

Likewise, if we take the economic aspect of our lives, which is the backbone of life, by which the preservation of life is achieved through food, drink, clothing and other things, and by which the preservation of the species is achieved through marriage, all of this requires a movement of production and a movement of consumption. By production and consumption life continues, and if either one stopped, unemployment and corruption would occur in society.

Accordingly, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, distributed talents among the servants: what I know, I serve everyone with; what everyone knows serves me; and thus the movement of life continues.

The universe in which you live has interests for you in it, and hopes stir within you. If you take part in the movement of life and earn wealth, which is the backbone of life, then you must balance between your immediate needs and your hopes for the future.

If you spend everything you earn on your present expenses, you have wasted for yourself the fulfilment of future hopes; you will not find what you can use to build a house, for example, or buy a car, or raise your standard with some of life's luxuries. This is what we call extravagance (israf).

On the other hand, just as extravagance is unbecoming for you so that nothing remains with you, likewise stinginess, niggardliness and withholding are unbecoming for you, so that you hoard everything you earn and spend only what keeps you alive; for in this state you will not contribute to the process of consumption, and thus you become a cause of unemployment in society and corruption of its condition.

The Qur'an treated this matter with a precise remedy in the saying of the Exalted:

﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it fully outstretched, lest you sit reproached and stripped bare.﴾ (Surah Al-Isra, 29)

That is: do not hold your hand back out of stinginess and niggardliness, so that you become blameworthy to your family and children, and to the world around you, so that everyone hates you; and likewise do not extend your hand...

Al-Wafa': it is that you fulfil what you have covenanted to do. Covenants do not apply to what is imposed upon you; they apply to what is permissible. You are free to meet me tomorrow, and I am likewise free. But if we agree and covenant to meet tomorrow at such-and-such an hour and such-and-such a place, the matter has passed from the permissible to the obligatory, and each of us becomes bound to fulfil his pledge, because each of us has suspended his own interests and arranged his affairs around this meeting. It is not right that one of us should fulfil while the other breaks his word, for that would cause a lack of equality of opportunity. It is known that the welfare of people in this world rests upon fulfilling covenants.

Some look at fulfilling a covenant as obligating only themselves, or as a burden upon them alone and not upon others. In reality, it is incumbent upon you and upon others alike. Just as it is required of you to fulfil, it is likewise required of others. So every obligation placed on you, do not look at it in this way; rather look at it as being for your own benefit.

Whoever takes the obligation and the commands of God from his side only becomes weary. Just as the Exalted and Glorified God has obligated you for the benefit of people, He has obligated all people for your benefit. So when He forbids you from theft, for example, do not think that it restricts your freedom before others; for He, glorified is He, has forbidden all people from stealing from you. So who is the winner then? I have restricted your freedom by the ruling, and you are a single individual, but I have restricted all creation for your sake.

Likewise, when the Shari'ah commands you to lower your gaze from the forbidden things of people, it commands all people to lower their gazes from your forbidden things. So: do not take the obligation as being upon you; rather it is for you, and for your own benefit.

Many of the wealthy grow resentful of spending and feel constricted by giving, and some of them regard it as a loss, because they do not know the wisdom behind obligating the rich to help the poor. They do not realise that we are securing their own lives. And here we see the world as turns of fortune: how many a rich man has become poor, and how many a strong man has become weak.

So when We take from you while you are rich, We reassure you: do not fear if your circumstances narrow, and if your wealth turns into poverty; for just as We took from you in the time of wealth, We will give to you in the time of poverty. This is how our outlook on the matters of obligation should be.

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿بعهد الله.. " ٩١ "﴾ (Surah al-Nahl).

The covenant of God: it is the thing you covenant with God over. Your first covenant with God, may He be exalted, is faith in Him. As long as you have believed in God, look at what He has asked of you and what He has obligated you with, and beware of neglecting any of His commands; for any deficiency in any obligatory matter from God counts as a flaw in your faith, because when you believed in God, you bore witness to what God bore witness to for Himself, glorified is He, in His saying: ﴿شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو " ١٨ "﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran).

So the first to bear witness for Himself is God, glorified is He, and this is the witness of the Essence to the Essence. (And the angels), that is, the witness of observation, ((and those of knowledge)), that is, through proof and argument.

So: the first covenant between you and God, the Exalted, is that you believed in Him as a Wise, Powerful, Creator, Sustainer God. Listen, then, to what He asks of you; if you do not listen and carry it out, know that the first covenant of faith has been broken. For this reason, the Exalted God has not obligated the disbeliever, because there is no covenant between him and Him; rather He obligates those who believe. So you will find that every verse of the legal rulings begins with this call of faith: ﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا.. " ١٨٣ "﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

As in His saying: ﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا كتب عليكم الصيام.. " ١٨٣ "﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

So, O you who have believed in Me as Lord and accepted Me as God, listen to Me; for I will give you the law of safeguarding your life, a law that will make you happy in the Hereafter through the effective cause, after having made you happy in this world through the means. And His saying: ﴿ولا تنقضوا الأيمان بعد توكيدها.. " ٩١ "﴾ (Surah al-Nahl).

Al-Ayman: plural of yamin, which is the oath that we swear and emphasise, saying: "By God," "By the covenant of God," and so on. So it is not fitting for you to break the oaths you have confirmed; rather you must fulfil them, for if you fulfil them, they will be fulfilled for you as well. Do not take the matter from your side alone, but look to the other party.

Likewise, the covenant between people one with another is derived from the inner core of the covenant of faith in God, the Exalted; for when we make a pact, we call God to witness this covenant, saying: "Between me and you is the covenant of God," thereby bringing the Exalted and Glorified God into our agreement to secure what we have covenanted. Our Lord, the Exalted and Glorified, says:

﴿وقد جعلتم الله عليكم كفيلا.. " ٩١ "﴾ (Surah al-Nahl), that is, a witness, a watcher, and a guarantor. And His saying:

﴿إن الله يعلم ما تفعلون " ٩١ "﴾ (Surah al-Nahl), that is: know that God is watching you, knowing the hidden secrets of hearts and what breasts conceal. So beware, when you give a covenant, of giving it while intending to break it; beware of giving a covenant as a deception, for your Lord, the Exalted and Glorified, knows what you do.

The Most High, blessed and exalted is He, presents us in this verse with an illustrative example for those who break oaths and covenants and do not fulfil them: this foolish Qurashi woman, Rayta bint 'Amir. She would order her maidservants to spin wool from dawn until noon, and then order them to unravel what they had spun from noon until afternoon. Whoever reflects on this example will find in it several lessons.

First: what is spinning (ghazl)?

Spinning (al-ghazl): a process that women used to carry out in the past. They would prepare material suitable for spinning, such as wool or camel hair, and cotton today. These materials are made of fine fibres that differ in length from one type to another, which they call the staple (tilah). They say, "this is a short staple," and "this is a long one."

Spinning means to join these fine fibres into a long, continuous and smooth thread with no knots in it, so that it becomes suitable for weaving afterwards. This process is carried out with a primitive tool called the spindle (maghzal). The woman blends these fine fibres and then twists them with the spindle, so that in the end there emerges a long, smooth, uniform thread with no knots.

The verse mentions the woman in this work because it was a task specific to women at that time rather than men. A woman would remain in her house and practise such simple crafts through which she made the furnishings of her home, such as rugs, clothing and other things.

Even now we see the woman who preserves her dignity away from the crush of life and the clash of mixed company, and we see her doing this kind of women's work.

The spindle has now developed into a knitting machine or a sewing machine, which facilitates these tasks for women, keeps them in their homes, and spreads in the house an atmosphere of cooperation between the mother and her children. Before us, for example, is the project of "productive families," in which the woman participates to a large extent in the advancement of society. There is therefore no objection to women working, provided it is honourable work that preserves her dignity and guards her sanctity.

The Qur'an has thus given us an example from the work of the pre-Islamic woman, a work that requires effort and time to spin, and requires even more to unravel and undo. This is a very arduous process, and perhaps she ordered the maidservants to unpick both the spinning and the weaving as well; for this reason they called her "the fool of Quraysh." As for His saying: ﴿after strength...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 92).

The word "strength" (quwwah) here indicates the stages that the process of spinning passes through, and how arduous it is: beginning with shearing the wool from the sheep or the hair from the camels, then mixing the ends of each fibre with the others, so that the end of each fibre lies within the middle of the others, in order for them to be bonded together by this blending. Then the woman turns the spindle between her fingers so that in the end she produces only a few centimetres of thread. If we compare this manual process with what the spinning industry has reached today, it will become clear to us how arduous it was for them.

It is as though the Noble Qur'an likened the one who gives a covenant and confirms it with emphatic oaths, and makes God a guarantor and witness to what he says, to the woman who spun this yarn, bore its hardship, and then went on to undo what she had accomplished and unravel what she had spun.

Likewise the word (quwwah) shows us that every work needs strength. This strength either sets the still in motion or stills the moving. Therefore He, the Exalted, said in another verse: ﴿Take what We have given you with strength...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 63). This is because we wish to move the stationary one toward good, and to restrain the one moving toward evil from it. In the world of physics they call this (the law of inertia): a body in motion continues in motion until something acts upon it to stop it, and a body at rest continues at rest until something acts upon it to set it in motion.

From here many marvel at the artificial satellites that orbit in space for years: what fuel moves these satellites throughout these years?

In reality there is no fuel that moves them. Fuel is only needed in the launch phase, until the object exits the zone of air and gravitational pull. Once the satellite or spacecraft settles in the zone of no gravity, it revolves and moves by itself without fuel. Thus the moving object continues moving, and the still object continues still.

Through this visible example, the Most High, blessed and exalted, warns us against breaking and violating covenants, because He, glory be to Him, wishes to safeguard the interests of creation, since these are founded upon the contracts, pledges and oaths that are concluded among them. Whoever betrays a covenant or breaks oaths is not trusted, his movement in life is not relied upon, society drops him from its regard, and he is isolated from the movement of dealings that rests upon mutual trust among people. As for His saying: ﴿into shreds (ankathan)...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 92): it is the plural of nakth, which is what has been undone and whose twist has been loosened from the yarn. As for His saying: ﴿taking your oaths as a means of deceit between you...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 92):

Dakhal (deceitful intrusion): to introduce into a thing something inferior to it of the same kind by way of fraud and deception, as when you mix into gold of 24 carats some gold of 18 carats, or as when you mix into almonds, for example, apricot kernels while presenting them as almonds. Thus oaths that are founded on truthfulness and fidelity are given by one who intends by them deception and fraud, so he swears to his companion while intending to lull him and beguile him.

As for His saying: ﴿because one community is more numerous than another...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 92): this is the reason why we take oaths as a means of deceit between us, false and deceptive oaths. For the one who sold apricot kernels, for example, as almonds has taken more (arba) than his due, that is, he took more than his right and diminished the rights of others. So the cause of deception through oaths is greed and the seeking of excess at the expense of others.

Excess may also come in another form: you pledge yourself to someone regarding something, you give him covenants, oaths and pacts, and then someone stronger than him appears to you, whether by coercion and authority or by enticement, so you break the first covenant because the second is more advantageous (arbā) and greater.

In such situations a person must take his caution. Who knows, perhaps he will do to you as you did, and be measured out to you by the same measure with which you measured out to others. So beware: if you dare against God's creation, God will let loose upon you one who will give you to drink from the same cup.

If you are a man of a trade or craft, beware of deceiving people, and remember that you have interests with them, and that in their hands are your livelihoods and crafts. If you dare against them, God will let them dare against you; for He, glory be to Him, says: "I am the Self-Subsisting" (al-Qayyum), that is, the one who stands over your affairs. Sleep, you, and I do not sleep. This is a matter that we must observe carefully.

Whoever dares against people, God emboldens them against him; and whoever makes his work sincere and perfects it, God casts into the hearts of creation that they should perfect their service to him. As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, God tests you thereby...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 92): that is, God tests you through this covenant. He, glory be to Him, knows what you are at the moment you conclude the covenant: is your intention in it fidelity, or is your intention treachery and deception?

Suppose you intend fidelity, and then there arises something that comes between you and it: God, glory be to Him, knows the realities of matters, and nothing is hidden from Him.

Thus, the trial (ibtila') here does not mean calamity and affliction, but merely testing; calamity and affliction fall upon the one who fails the test, so the outcome is what matters. As for His saying: ﴿And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that about which you used to differ﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 92): on the Day of Resurrection the adversaries will gather, the realities will be laid bare, and the judgement will come concerning what we disputed in this world. Suppose a person was blind to the judgement of the earth in certain matters; we say to him: if you are blind to the judgement of the earth, you will not be blind to the judgement of heaven. Await a day on which we shall all gather and judge these matters.

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 16, verse 93:**

*Law* (لو): a particle indicating the impossibility of one thing because of the impossibility of another. That is, the non-existence of the answer (the consequent) is due to the non-existence of the condition (the antecedent), as in the words of God Most High: ﴿Had there been in them (the heavens and the earth) gods other than Allah, they would have both been ruined﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 22).

So corruption is impossible because the plurality of gods is impossible. Thus, had Allah willed, He would have made the whole world one community upon the truth, not upon misguidance, one community in faith and guidance, just as He made the other kinds of creation one community in submitting to what He intends for them.

That is because all the kinds of existence created for the human being, before he comes into life, are created in truth, by a subjugated (taskhiri) creation. No kind among the kinds is refractory to what is intended for it: neither inanimate matter, nor plants, nor animals. All these created beings proceed in sound course as Allah wills for them. And what is astonishing is that the human being should be the only created thing that is out of order in the universe. That is because of his freedom of choice: he acts or does not act. Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Do you not see that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures, and many of mankind? But upon many the punishment has been justified...﴾ (Surah al-Hajj, 18).

Thus all these created beings prostrate to Allah without exception, except for man, of whom He said: ﴿...and many are deserving of punishment...﴾ (Surah al-Hajj, 18).

So why has this difference arisen among people? Because they are possessors of choice: one of them can act or not act. Is this matter outside the will of Allah, or did Allah will it, glorified and exalted is He?

They say that Allah exercised His absolute power in creating the subjugated things, such that nothing departs from what is intended of it. It would have been possible for man to come in this same form of subjugation, but in that case he would add nothing, and would contribute nothing new to the universe. Are not the angels established in subjugation?

Subjugation establishes the power of Allah, Exalted, so that nothing departs from His power or from His will. But choice establishes the lovability (mahbubiyya) of Allah, Exalted, and this is a distinction we must reflect upon.

For example, if you had two slaves or two servants, one of them named Sa'id and the other Mas'ud, and you took Sa'id and tied him to you with a rope, while you left Mas'ud free and unrestrained, and when you commanded each of them, each responded and obeyed, which obedience would be more beloved to you: the obedience of compulsion and subjugation, or obedience by choice?

Thus the Truth, blessed and exalted, created man and honored him by making him one who chooses whether to obey or to disobey. If he comes obedient by choice, while being able to disobey, he has established lovability for his Lord, glorified and exalted. Choice must have conditions. The first is reason, for it is the instrument of choice; likewise the insane is not obligated. When reason is present, there must also be maturity and puberty, which occurs when a person is able to beget his like and has become independent in his own origin.

This is the mark of the completion of the self. Before this completion he is deficient in formation and not fit for obligation. If he is rational and mature through puberty and completion of self, he must be choosing and not coerced. If he is compelled to something, he will not be held accountable for it. If any one of these three conditions is lacking, there is no meaning to choice. In this way the Truth, blessed and exalted, guarantees for the human being soundness in choice.

And although the Truth, blessed and exalted, has honored man with choice, in His mercy toward him He made some of his organs involuntary and subjugated, over which he has no control. If we reflect on these organs, we find them essential, and human life depends upon them. So it was of Allah's mercy toward us that He made these organs work and perform their function without our being aware.

For example, the heart works regularly, waking and sleeping, without our noticing it; likewise breathing, the kidneys, the liver, the intestines and others work by His power, subjugated, like inanimate matter, plants and animals.

And of Allah's kindness to His creation is that He made these organs subjugated; for, by Allah, if you were choosing in the work of these organs, how would you breathe, for example, while you are asleep?!

Therefore: it is of Allah's mercy that He made you choosing in the matters that present themselves to you, and in which you need to consider alternatives. That is why they say: "Man is the father of alternatives." The animal, for example, though the closest of kinds to man, does not have these alternatives and does not know them: if you harm an animal, it harms you, and it has no other alternative.

But if you harm a human being, he may respond in kind, or with more than you did, or less, or he may pardon and forgive, and reason is what weighs one of these alternatives. So, had the Truth, glorified and exalted, willed to make mankind one community, He would have made them so, as He said: ﴿Had Allah willed, He would have guided all mankind﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 31). But He, glorified and exalted, did not will that, as is evident from His words: ﴿But He leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 93). This verse is one at which those who quibble stop, and those whose insight into the Book of Allah is short, who say: "Since Allah is the one who leads people astray, why then does He punish them?" We marvel at this understanding of the Book of Allah, and we say to these people: Why did you take the side of misguidance and leave the side of guidance? Why did you not say: "Since Allah holds guidance in His hand, and He is the one who guides, why then does He admit us to Paradise?"

So this is a statement made by the wasteful, because the meaning of ﴿He leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 93) is: He judges by the one's works that he is astray, and judges by the other's works that he is guided. This is like what happens with us in examination committees: we do not say, "The committee passed so-and-so and failed so-and-so." That is not their task. Rather their task is to examine the answer sheets, and through them the committee judges who succeeds and who fails.

Likewise, the Truth, blessed and exalted, does not make the servant astray; rather He judges his work to be misguidance, and that he is astray. The meaning, then, is: He judges the misguidance of whom He wills, and judges the guidance of whom He wills, and no one may turn the matter to the opposite of this understanding, as is evident from His words after it: ﴿And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 93). The servant is questioned only about what his hands have done, and the question here means: freedom of choice in action. How could you be questioned about a thing in which you have no part? Let us then understand from the Truth, blessed and exalted, His intended meaning from the verse.

The word "dakhl" (deceit, corruption) appeared in the verse before the previous one, and we said its meaning is: to insert into a thing something inferior to it, of its own kind, by way of cheating and deception. Although the meaning is one in both verses, the previous verse came to clarify the cause of "dakhl" and its reason, which is that one community is more numerous than another, and one of the parties gains at the expense of the other. As for this verse, it came to clarify the result of the existence of "dakhl," which is:

﴿And [thus] a foot would slip after it had been firmly planted.. " 94 "﴾ (Surat an-Nahl). In the verse there is a prohibition against taking oaths as a means of deceit, trickery and fraud, because the result of this act is corruption that comes upon society from its foundations, and the loss of mutual trust among people, on which dealings are based and the movement of life is built. Whoever gives a pledge and breaks it, and swears an oath and violates it, becomes known as one who breaks covenants and violates agreements.

Accordingly, people withdraw their trust from him, and no one dares to deal with him, so he becomes despised, and people shake their hands free of him, after he had been trustworthy, worthy of trust, and deserving of esteem. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And [thus] a foot would slip after it had been firmly planted.. " 94 "﴾ (Surat an-Nahl). In this way his rights with society are forfeited, the evil of his deed encompasses him, and he reaps with his own hand the fruits of what he has corrupted in society. With the spread of this bad character, the movement of life is brought to a halt, and trust and honesty are lost.

Therefore, this is a slip and a stumble after firmness and strength: he was once worthy of trust, a person of fidelity to covenants and pacts, to whom people turned and loved to deal with him, because of the honour of his word and the truthfulness of his promise. But then he retreats backward and recedes, and loses this standing.

For this reason we find people of wealth and commerce saying: "So-and-so's position has been shaken in the market," meaning his foot has slipped because of what he did of breaking covenants, violating oaths, and other things that do not befit people of trust in the market. Such a person ends up declaring his bankruptcy in the world of dealings with people.

As for fulfilling covenants, pacts and oaths, it makes your foot firm in the movement of life, unshaken and not wavering, so you find the property of all people as your property, and you find owners of wealth coming to you, placing their wealth between your hands, owing to the good reputation, integrity and trustworthiness you enjoy in dealings.

Therefore, Islamic legislation, when it prescribed partnership (sharikah) for us, took into account this kind of person who possesses nothing but a good reputation, trustworthiness, integrity and fidelity; this is their capital. If a partner enters with this, then he is a partner with the honour of his word and the honour of his conduct, his standing among people, and his distinguished past in dealings.

This is what they call "the partnership of reputations and notables" (shirkat al-wujuh wa al-a'yan), and this man of standing in the world of wealth and commerce has attained this standing only through the respect and trust of people he has earned, and through his record of virtues and noble deeds.

Likewise, we may see this trust not in a particular person but in a brand or trademark, which is bought and sold and has a high value in the market because of the respect and esteem it has earned from people; this too is the result of truthfulness, commitment, trustworthiness and the honour of one's word.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And taste the evil for what you have averted from the way of Allah, and for you is a great punishment. " 94 "﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

"Evil" (al-su'): that is, the punishment that afflicts its bearer in this world, in the form of humiliation and contempt among people, and stagnation in his affairs, after he has fallen from the eyes of society and the bridge of trust between him and his community has been destroyed. And His saying: ﴿for what you have averted from the way of Allah.. " 94 "﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

The discussion here concerns those who break covenants and oaths and do not fulfil them. Is there, in this, an averting from the way of Allah?

We say: first, the meaning of "the way of Allah" is everything that makes the movement of life orderly, run with honour, trustworthiness, truthfulness and the enforcement of covenants.

From here, whoever breaks a covenant and does not keep pacts gives society a bad example that makes the owner of wealth stingy with his wealth and the doer of good retreat. For if you lend something to a person and he betrays you, I do not think you will lend to another.

Therefore, there is no doubt that in this there is an averting from the way of Allah, and a discouragement of people from doing good. And His saying: ﴿And for you is a great punishment. " 94 "﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

In addition to the loss that befell them in this world, and after their foot had slipped and they suffered various kinds of punishment in this world, a great punishment still awaits them, that is, in the Hereafter.

Almighty Allah in this verse forbids us and warns us: beware of breaking the covenant of Allah that you have affirmed to people, and of which you have made Allah a guarantor. Once you were free to make a covenant or not, but by the mere making of the covenant its fulfilment has become obligatory and incumbent upon you.

Or: "the covenant of Allah" means His law which you pledged to act upon and to preserve, and it is the supreme covenant of faith, namely that you believe in Allah and in the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying from Allah, and that you commit yourself to everything the Messenger brought of rulings. Beware of exchanging it for something else that you make more precious than it, because if you break the covenant of Allah for some other thing of the fleeting goods of this world, you have made that thing more precious than the covenant of Allah, since the price, whatever it is, will be small.

Then comes the explanation of that in His saying:

﴿Indeed, what is with Allah is better for you..﴾ (95) (Surah an-Nahl).

So the good, in reality, is not in the goods of this world however abundant they are, but in what is with Allah, the Exalted, and He has clarified this in His saying: ﴿What is with you will end, and what is with Allah is lasting﴾ (96) (Surah an-Nahl).

We pause at His saying: ﴿...it is better for you..﴾ (95) (Surah an-Nahl). This is a style of emphasis by restriction (qasr) through the repetition of the pronoun "huwa" (it). The Truthful, Glorified One did not say "Indeed, what is with Allah is better for you," which would allow that what is with others might also be better for you. But in the Qur'anic expression ("huwa khayrun lakum"), the good lies in what is with Allah by way of restriction, as in His saying:

﴿And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾ (80) (Surah ash-Shu'ara').

He brought the pronoun "huwa" to affirm that the Healer is Allah, because there is a suspicion that healing might come from the physician. As for things in which partnership is not suspected, it comes without this emphasis, as in His saying:

﴿And who causes me to die and then gives me life﴾ (81) (Surah ash-Shu'ara').

He did not say "huwa yumituni, huwa yuhyin," because none causes death and gives life except Allah, so no emphasis is needed here.

What takes a person out of fulfilling a covenant?

What takes a person out of fulfilling a covenant is that he sees a superficial benefit that outweighs what he contracted to, which leads him to abandon what he pledged in favour of this superficiality. But if he reasoned and reflected upon the matter, he would know that what he seeks is a paltry price and a small, fleeting gain when compared with what is stored for him in the case of fulfilment, because what he takes as a share of his worldly life must inevitably vanish.

Reason says: if a thing is small but lasting, it is preferable to a large thing that does not last. How much more so when the small is what perishes and the large is what endures.

An example of this: if I gave you fruit that would suffice you for a week or a month, and you ate it all in one day, you would have enjoyed it only once, and you would have lost many enjoyments and repeated meals had you eaten it at its proper times.

Therefore, the Truthful, Glorified One alerts you that what is with Allah is the true good, and He has made your scales of faith precise. It is folly to sell the abundant and lasting for the little and perishing: ﴿if you were to know﴾ (95) (Surah an-Nahl).

In the verse there is precision of reckoning, precision of comparison, and precision in solving economic equations.

The Exalted and Blessed Lord makes clear that a person's share of his worldly life is a fleeting possession: either he will lose it through death, or it will be taken from him by the events that befall him, whereas what is with Allah endures and never runs out.

﴿And We will surely reward those who were patient..., 96﴾ (Surat an-Nahl).

The word (sabaru, "were patient") indicates that a person will be subjected to inner turmoil as a result of his wavering between fulfilling a covenant and breaking it, when the glitter of wealth appears to him and the desires of the soul stir within him. The Lord, blessed and exalted, says to him: "Be patient, be patient. Do not be hasty. Weigh matters with calm deliberation, bear every psychological hardship, and overcome the desire of the soul, so that you may reach the praiseworthy outcome."

The student who strives, exhausts himself, and endures the hardship of study and learning is patient over immediate desires, because of the lasting and deferred desires awaiting him; behind study and learning lies a greater aim and a loftier goal. For this reason the Lord, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And We will surely reward those who were patient..., 96﴾ (Surat an-Nahl), that is, for the hardships of fulfilling covenants.

﴿...their reward according to the best of what they used to do, 96﴾ (Surat an-Nahl), that is: a reward with an increase in recompense, according to the best that can be. A person who acts out of obligation or recommendation has a reward, whereas for what is permissible (mubah) there is, strictly speaking, no reward; yet Allah's grace rewards it too.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 16, verse 97:

The Exalted, blessed is He, gives us a general principle, namely the principle of equality between men and women. Covenants were customarily made between men, and women had no part in giving covenants. Indeed, when they were included in a covenant with the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of the Pledge of al-'Aqaba, he had one of the Companions pledge allegiance to the women on his behalf.

So, since the woman is distant from this arena, given that this is customarily among the characteristics of men, He (glorified be He) wanted to tell us: We do not prevent a female from having righteous deeds.

And do not think that the matter is limited to men without women. Righteous deeds are accepted from male and female alike, on condition that faith is present in them. For this reason He, may He be exalted, says:

﴿And he is a believer...﴾ [16:97], and thereby the deed has benefit and is accepted by Allah. For this reason we see many people who perform righteous deeds, serve humanity with inventions and discoveries, treat the sick, and build hospitals and schools, but the condition of faith in Allah is not present for them.

So we see that the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, does not deprive these people of their due, but hastens it for them in this world, because they have no share in the reward of the Hereafter. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him thereof, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ [42:20].

And the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [99:7-8].

All of this concerns matters of this world. Whoever does something well reaps its fruit. But as for the recompense of the Hereafter, we say to these people: You have no share today. Take your reward from those for whom you worked. You did good for humanity for the sake of fame and lasting remembrance, and you have received that in this world: they have immortalized your memory, raised your standing, and made statues for you, and they did not withhold from you your due of fame and honor.

On the Day of Resurrection, the Truth, glorified be He, will confront them: You did it so that it would be said... and it has been said. So go and take your reward from those for whom you acted. These are the ones concerning whom Allah said:

﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him, and He pays him his account in full. And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [24:39].

On the Day of Resurrection he will be surprised to find that he had a God whom he ought to have believed in, and whom he ought to have worked seeking His face and His pleasure. So: faith is a condition for the acceptance of righteous deeds, and when faith is present, male and female are equal in reward and recompense. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Then We will surely cause him to live a good life...﴾ [16:97]. This is the natural result of the righteous deed whose doer seeks the face of Allah and the Abode of the Hereafter. Allah thus combines for him two portions of recompense: a portion in this world, in a good, contented life, and a portion in the Hereafter: ﴿And We will surely give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [16:97].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 98:

Al-isti'adha (seeking refuge): taking shelter and holding fast to Allah from something you fear. You do not take refuge, hold fast, seek protection, or call for help except when you sense within yourself that you are too weak to resist your enemy.

If your enemy is Satan, with the power and authority Allah has given him and the access he has to the human soul, then you have no power and no strength to resist him except by taking refuge in Allah, the Mighty who created you and created this Satan. He alone is able to repel him from you, for Satan is in a battle with man whose millstone turns until the Day of Resurrection.

Satan has sworn by the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, saying:

﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, / Except Your sincere servants among them.﴾ (Surah Sad)

So there is nothing for you but to be among those. There is nothing for you but to nestle in the bosom of your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and hold fast to Him. He, glorified is He, is the Strong, able to push away from you what you cannot push away from yourself. So do not confront him with your own strength, for you have no power against him, and do not let him single you out, for if he isolates you and draws you away from Allah, he will have the upper hand.

Therefore we always say: "There is no power and no strength except with Allah" (la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah). That is: there is no turning away (la hawla) from disobedience, and no strength (la quwwa) for obedience, except with Allah.

We see a small child walking in the street, for example, who may be attacked by children his own age; but if he is in the company of his father, none of them dares to approach him. So what about one who walks in the company of his Lord, blessed and exalted is He, and casts himself into the protection of Allah, glorified is He?!

In the station of seeking refuge in Allah, we mention a principle of faith that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught us in his noble hadith: "Whoever seeks refuge in Allah, grant him refuge."

It is incumbent upon the believer to grant refuge to whoever seeks refuge in Allah, even if that person is among the things most beloved to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gives us the example in this: when he married a young woman of great beauty and loveliness, to the extent that his wives became jealous of her, they began to scheme against her and to push her away from before them, so that she would not overcome them in the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ). But how could they do that?

They tried to exploit the fact that this young woman was still a naive girl, enjoying sincerity of intention and purity of heart, having no experience of life from which she might learn cunning or guile. She was also still in the elation of her happiness at having become a "mother of the believers," and was most eager to please the Prophet (ﷺ). The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) exploited all of this, and one of them said to her: "When you enter upon the Messenger of Allah, say to him: 'I seek refuge in Allah from you,' for he loves this phrase."

The girl took this phrase with her sincerity of intention, her love for the Messenger of Allah, and her eagerness to please him, and said to him: "I seek refuge in Allah from you," while she did not know the meaning of this expression. So the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You have sought refuge with the One who grants refuge; join your family."

That is: since you have sought refuge in Allah, I accept this seeking of refuge, because you sought refuge with a Refuge, that is, with One for whose sake we must leave you alone. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) divorced her, in compliance with this seeking of refuge.

So: whoever seeks refuge in Allah, the believer must grant him refuge, and whoever seeks Allah's protection, the believer must be a soldier among the soldiers of Allah and grant him protection until he reaches his place of safety. In the noble verse there is a conditional construction, whose response is joined with the particle fa' in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge...﴾ (Surah al-Nahl).

When you see the fa' (fa), know that what follows it is consequent upon what precedes it, as if you said: "If you meet Muhammad, then say to him such-and-such..." The speech is not complete except after the meeting. But in the noble verse the intended meaning is: "If you want to recite the Qur'an, then seek refuge," because the seeking of refuge here comes before the recitation, as in the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces...﴾ (Surah al-Ma'ida)

The meaning is: when you want to perform the prayer, wash your faces. Likewise, when you want to recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, because the Qur'an is the speech of Allah.

If we believe that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who speaks, we would know that reciting the Qur'an differs from any other recitation. For in order to recite the Qur'an you perform several operations:

The first: calling to mind the holiness of the One who sent it down, glorified is He, in whom you believe and to whose speech you turn.

The second: calling to mind the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying the Qur'an that was sent down to him.

The third: calling to mind the greatness of the Noble Qur'an, with its aspects of inimitability, and what it contains of etiquette and rulings.

So you have three operations by which you prepare to recite the speech of Allah in His Noble Qur'an, and each of them is a righteous act that Satan will not let you perform without confronting you, whispering to you, and diverting you from what you are turning to.

At that moment you will not be able to prevent him unless you seek Allah's help against him and seek refuge from him in Allah. In this way you are in the company of Allah, who sent down the Qur'an, glorified and exalted is He, and in the presence of the greatness of Muhammad, the one to whom it was sent down, truly, and with the reception of what the Qur'an contains of inimitability, etiquette and rulings.

From here it became obligatory for us to seek refuge in Allah from Satan before reciting the Qur'an.

Nevertheless, there is no objection to understanding the meaning as seeking refuge also after reciting the Qur'an, so the intended meaning is: "When you have recited the Qur'an, then seek refuge in Allah..." i.e., after the recitation, because after you have read the Book of Allah you have come out of it with a provision of faith and divine illuminations, and you have encountered etiquette and rulings that were required of you. So you must seek refuge in Allah from Satan, lest he spoil for you this provision and those illuminations, or divert you from carrying out these etiquettes and rulings.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿from the accursed Satan﴾ (Surah al-Nahl), that is: the cursed one, expelled from the mercy of Allah. This is because Satan is not a newly created being whom we need to test in order to know his nature and how to deal with him; rather, he has a record of enmity with us since our father Adam, peace be upon him. Allah warned Adam about him, saying:

﴿O Adam, this is an enemy to you and to your wife...﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha)

He had already been stoned, cursed, and removed from the mercy of Allah, and he threatened us with His saying:

﴿I will surely seize his descendants...﴾ (Surah al-Isra')

So: there is an enmity established between us and him from the creation of man until the Hour arrives.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 16, verse 99:

It is for a wisdom intended by the Creator, glory be to Him, that He made for Satan an authority (sultan). That is, a power to dominate. The word sultan is derived from al-salit (sulit), which is the oil with which they used to light lamps and lanterns before the discovery of electricity. They would place this oil in a closed vessel, like a sultaniyya (lamp-container), from which a wick would emerge. When it was lit, it would draw up the oil and give light. For this reason, proof (hujja) was called sultan, because it illuminates for its possessor the face of the truth.

Sultan is of two kinds: either the sultan of proof, which convinces you in fact so that you act while you are content and convinced by it; or the sultan of coercion and domination, which compels you to act and forces you upon it without conviction.

So, the carrying out of what is demanded has two forces: the force of proof, which lights up for you and makes clear before you the landmarks of the truth, and the force of coercion, which compels you to carry out what is demanded without conviction, even if you do not see it.

In reality, Satan possesses neither of these two forces: neither the force of proof and persuasion, nor the force of coercion. This is clear in the words of the Truth, blessed and exalted, spoken on the tongue of Satan on the Day of Resurrection:

﴿And Satan will say, when the matter has been decided: "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke my promise to you. And I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieved in your associating me [with Allah] before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment."﴾ (Surah Ibrahim).

This is a dialogue that takes place on the Day of Resurrection, after the matter has ended and the reality has been uncovered, and the time of frankness and confrontation has come. Satan says to his followers, disclaiming responsibility: "I had no authority over you," neither an authority of proof that would convince you to act willingly, nor an authority of coercion with which I forced you to act while you were unwilling. I only pointed and whispered, and you came to me willingly.

﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me [ma ana bi-musrikhikum wa ma antum bi-musrikhiyy]﴾ (Surah Ibrahim): that is, we are equal in loss; I cannot rescue you, and you cannot rescue me. Shouting (sarakh) is done by someone who has fallen into distress or hardship from which he cannot free himself by himself, so he cries out loudly, perhaps he will find someone to aid and deliver him. If the people respond to him, they have "answered his cry" (asrakhuhu), that is, they removed the cause of his crying out.

So the meaning is: neither can I remove the cause of your crying out, nor can you remove the cause of my crying out. Likewise, in another dialogue that took place between the people of falsehood who banded together against it in this world, here is the confrontation on the Day of Resurrection:

﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned. What is [the matter] with you that you do not help one another? Rather, they will this day be submitting. And they will approach one another, questioning each other. They will say, "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right." They will say, "Rather, you were not [true] believers. And we had over you no authority; rather, you were a transgressing people."﴾ (Surah As-Saffat).

By His saying "from the right" ('an al-yamin) is meant that a person carries out his deeds with both hands, but the right hand is the principal in work; so "you came to him from the right" means: from the side of the effective hand.

﴿And we had over you no authority; rather, you were a transgressing people﴾ (Surah As-Saffat): that is, you were waiting for a signal from us, merely a signal, so you hastened and fell into what you fell into. Upon whom, then, does Satan's domination and that overpowering and coercion fall?

The Truth, blessed and exalted, makes clear that Satan's domination does not fall upon the one who believed in Him as Lord, sought refuge in Him, and held fast to Him. As long as you have believed in Allah, you are in His company and protection, and Satan, being a creature of Allah, cannot dominate you or overpower you.
